Airlines are to be prevented from charging parents extra fees to sit alongside their children on aeroplanes under new plans set out by the government.

Passengers will also no longer face charges when altering a name on their flight booking in order to rectify an error.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham stated that the regulatory changes form part of a broader crackdown on the "little charges that add up" when families arrange their holiday getaways.

It is understood that ministers intend to introduce the measures prior to the start of next year’s summer holiday season.

MPs are currently debating this updated set of requirements for travel firms as the Civil Aviation (Consumer Protection and Regulatory Reform) Bill progresses through Parliament.

The proposed legislation will grant ministers flexible powers to create a clear list of passenger entitlements alongside a register of duties for both airlines and airports.

Mr Burnham said: “Charging parents just to sit with their children is a rip-off, plain and simple.

“And being hit with a hefty fee for a simple spelling mistake on a booking form isn’t right either.

open image in gallery The new rule will mean airlines will be required to seat children aged under 14 next to their parents or an accompanying adult free of charge ( Getty Images )

“People are fed up with these little charges that add up, so I’m putting a stop to them.

“This is what our everyday fixes are all about – giving people room to breathe by tackling the small irritations that catch people out, waste their time and cost them money.”

The new rule will mean airlines will be required to seat children aged under 14 next to their parents or an accompanying adult free of charge.

According to the Department for Transport, an arrangement to sit together can currently cost a parent and child up to £104 on a return journey.

Rory Boland, editor of consumer magazine Which? Travel, said: “It’s clearly unfair to force parents and children as young as three to pay an extra fee just to sit together.

“Airlines that have separated families are putting profit ahead of passenger peace of mind.”

Earlier this year, Ryanair adjusted its family seating policy after an investigation was launched into the company charging parents to sit with their children on flights.

The Irish operator previously required parents travelling with children aged between two and 11 to pay to reserve what it referred to as a mandatory family seat.

open image in gallery Burnham said charging parents to sit with their children is a ‘rip-off’ ( Reuters )

Children were then allocated seats next to or near parents free of charge.

The fee for a mandatory family seat was typically about £8 each way, the UK Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) watchdog found.

Under the new policy, parents will still have the option of paying to reserve a seat of their choosing and have their children alongside them free of charge.

At the time, Ryanair chief executive Michael O’Leary said its previous policy was “the most progressive and transparent in Europe”.

Under the new policy, he said, “families may have to wait until after they have checked in to find out their seat allocation and are more likely to be seated at the rear of the cabin – but at least the CMA will be able to claim they have done something for consumers”.

Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander has also announced a crackdown on bad behaviour by passengers on aircraft, with the Government, airlines and trade unions working on a new system for sharing information about disruptive passengers.

Airlines logged more than 1,000 serious disruptive passenger incidents in 2025, Government figures show, including what it described as a mid-air brawl which caused a flight to be diverted.

Using the new system, airlines could choose to ban persistently disruptive passengers from their aircraft.

“Everyone deserves to travel knowing their flight isn’t going to be disrupted by bad behaviour from a small minority,” Ms Alexander said.

“These commonsense reforms will make flying safer for staff and passengers and protect people from unnecessary charges, whoever they fly with.”

News.title: FTSE 100 tumbles amid bond market sell-off
News.content:
Thanks for joining me. House prices fell unexpectedly last month as mortgage borrowers prepare for a jump in interest rates.

Typical property values declined by 0.2pc during September, reversing 0.2pc growth in August, according to the Nationwide house price index.

The figure was much worse than analysts had forecasts, with most expecting prices to remain steady.

Over the course of the year to September, the rate of house price growth halved from 1.6pc to 0.8pc, which was the weakest rate since December 2025.

The value of the average home has fallen to £274,251 over concerns the Bank of England is on the cusp of raising interest rates, making borrowing more expensive for mortgage holders.

Money markets indicate there is an 84pc chance policymakers will raise rates from 3.75pc to 4pc in November in an effort to bring down inflation caused by the Iran war energy shock.

Robert Gardner, chief economist at Nationwide, said:“Market activity and house prices have remained subdued in recent months, in part reflecting the uncertain economic backdrop.

“Geopolitical tensions remain high, with the conflict in the Middle East exerting upward pressure on energy prices, fanning inflation concerns.

“This in turn has led to mounting financial market expectations of Bank Rate increases, which has maintained upward pressure on the market interest rates which underpin mortgage pricing.” Here is what you need to know.

5 things to start your day

1) Polanski urges Miliband to block Rosebank oil field over Israel links | Green leader claims North Sea project is a test of Foreign Secretary’s proposed sanctions regime

2) Netherlands ditches wealth tax over exodus fears | Dutch PM scraps plan to target paper profits, instead introducing a more convention capital gains levy

3) Diesel crisis deepens as UK’s biggest refinery shuts for 10 weeks | Fears of squeeze on supplies after fuel costs rise higher than £2 per litre

4) Debt-ridden France branded ‘the new sick man of Europe’ | Investors hope the European Central Bank sees the struggling country as ‘too big to fail’

5) Britain blocks foreign lawyers after surge in south Asian applicants | Bar Standards Board halts scheme unless candidates have already secured a position

What happened overnight

The cost of government borrowing edged higher in Asia as soaring energy costs sparked inflation fears.

Bond yields, a benchmark for what governments pay to borrow money, surged in September as investors brace for a period where interest rates stay higher for ​longer.

The yield on benchmark US 10-year Treasury notes hit 5.31pc, the ‌highest level since mid-June 2007. The 10-year yield gained 87 basis points in the July-September quarter, the biggest quarterly rise since 1994.

Market focus has been on how long US Treasury yields stay above the psychologically important 5pc level, while some investors even contemplate the possibility of yields breaching 6pc.

Yields in Japan have climbed to multi-decade highs too, while those in Germany, France and Britain have all hit 17 to 19 year peaks.

On Thursday, the benchmark 10-year Japanese government ​bond yield was at 3.11pc, not far from the 30-year high it hit last week.

Asian technology stocks rose after a boost from AI chipmaker Micron, ​although US bonds struggled ‌after their sharpest quarterly sell-off in more than three decades as inflation risks from elevated energy prices linger.

Stalling peace talks between the US and Iran to end the seven-month-long war in the Middle East have kept crude prices aloft.Brent futures surged 42pc in the July-September quarter.

The high-stakes earnings from Micron, a key supplier to AI bellwether Nvidia, signalled strong demand for AI memory chips, with financial commitments under long-term supply agreements at $32 billion, up from $22 billion in June.

That helped push tech-heavy stock markets in Asia higher. Japan’s Nikkei jumped over 3pc, and South Korea’s Kospi reversed earlier losses to gain 1.7pc. Taiwan’s stock benchmark was 0.8pc higher.

News.title: Chewing tobacco killed 250,000 people in one year, study shows
News.content:
Chewing tobacco killed around a quarter of a million people in 2023, with use of the product remaining stubbornly high, according to research.

The smokeless tobacco is particularly popular in south Asia that is placed between the cheek and lower gum. It is flavoured and sometimes sweetened, and users often spit out unwanted juices while chewing. It is often viewed as safer than smoking but it is a major cause of stroke, as well as head and neck cancer.

Chewing tobacco is different to white snus or nicotine pouches, which contain no tobacco. These white pouches are also made up of flavourings and sometimes sweeteners, and deliver a hit of nicotine through the lining of the mouth.

Despite a successful fight against smoking over the last few decades, rates of chewing tobacco use have fallen little and it has often been overlooked in tobacco control efforts, researchers point out. In a study published in the Lancet Global Health, researchers from the Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation in the US estimate that 241 million people aged 15 years and older used chewing tobacco in 2023.

Researchers looked at data on use in 204 countries between 1990 and 2023 and found that there was no significant decrease in the number of users of chewing tobacco over that period. And in 24 countries there was a significant uptick in the number of people using the product. Researchers estimate that about one in five men and one in 10 women in south Asia chewed tobacco in 2023.

Bangladesh has seen the biggest increase in the number of people using the product with 15 million new users between 1990 and 2023. Nepal, Madagascar and Yemen also saw increases in the number of users.

In India 105 million people chew tobacco regularly, accounting for just over two thirds of users globally. Historically, Indians would chew paan, tobacco in its raw form which was mixed with betel leaf and areca nut, a mild stimulant. But the use of chewing tobacco exploded in the 1980s when manufacturers began grinding these into a powder and selling them in packets known as gutkha. This was banned in 2012 but is still widely available. Chewing tobacco is also popular in Pakistan, China and Vietnam.

News.title: Esther Rantzen dies aged 86
News.content:
Dame Esther was a vocal supporter of the Assisted Dying Bill, claiming in March that most people “want and need” the right to end their own lives.

When the bill was defeated in the House of Commons in September, as MPs voted 286 to 270 against the legislation, she called it a “tragic day”. The bill would have allowed those with less than six months to live to seek medical assistance to end their lives.

In 2024, she said that she had joined the Dignitas assisted-dying clinic in Switzerland.

Writing for The Telegraph at the beginning of September, Rebecca Wilcox, Dame Esther’s daughter, said her mother was “too ill now to travel to Dignitas as she had planned and paid for”.

Earlier this month, Dame Esther said in a statement that it was too late for her to “buzz off” to the clinic in Switzerland and said Britain’s current laws on assisted dying are “messy and cruel”.

In a final message shared by her family, the presenter said she had been “immensely lucky” for the support she had received from the public, which she said had enabled her “to live such a long and happy life”.

She added: “Sadly, all good things come to an end, as they say. So I particularly wanted to say goodbye and thank you so very, very much. Perhaps I will see you eventually, on the other side. I do hope so. With very good wishes, as ever, Esther.”

News.title: Laptop running slowly? These tips will improve performance (and save your sanity)
News.content:
MacBooks and Windows laptops both have modes intended to maximise battery life. Low Power Mode (Mac) and Power Saver (Windows) should be avoided if you want peak performance.

On a Mac, you’ll find the Low Power Mode switch in Settings > Battery. For the best experience, set this to Never, but remember to change it back if you need your MacBook to last longer.

On a Windows laptop, there are two controls you need to consider. Both are found in Settings > System > Power & Battery.

Energy Saver mode uses multiple tactics to reduce battery consumption, including lowering maximum power. Switch this off, and you have access to Power Mode controls.

Your options are Best Power Efficiency, Balanced and Best Performance. While Balanced is the default, I was able to unlock up to 33 per cent more power by playing around with these settings using my own laptop.

To make matters more complicated, some laptops have their own performance modes. Many Asus laptops have MyAsus or Armory Crate, for example. Lenovo has the Vantage app, Dell has MyDell, and MSI laptops have MSI Center.

3. Stop applications from opening on start-up

If your laptop is slow when it first starts up, it may be because a whole bunch of apps have been given the green light to wake up with it.

Some applications such as antivirus software are critical, but most can be toggled off. As an example, I make sure apps such as Spotify, Steam and WhatsApp don’t open on startup; I only launch them when I need them.

On a MacBook, you can see which apps have this permission in Settings > General, under Open at Login. Select an app entry and click the “minus” button to remove it.

On a Windows laptop, you’ll find the list of start-up apps in Settings > Apps > Startup. Each entry has a little on/off slider.

4. Free up storage space

News.title: Why the UK medicine supply chain is dangerously exposed to global shocks
News.content:
The UK’s medicine supply chain is dangerously exposed to global shocks, experts have warned, with the NHS dependent on a system where much of the world relies on a handful of countries for its drug supplies.

India and China are the backbone of the global medicines market, manufacturing around two-thirds of the world’s active pharmaceutical ingredients. This leaves countries exposed to factory shutdowns, natural disasters, geopolitical tensions, shipping disruption and sudden changes in the price or availability of raw materials, experts told The Telegraph.

“We rely now more than ever on other countries to make sure we can get access to the medicines that the vast majority of people take,” said Dr James Davies, director of research and insights at Community Pharmacy England.

Nearly all the active ingredients in the UK’s most widely used medicines are made overseas, around 80 per cent of them in China and India, leaving the NHS exposed to shocks thousands of miles beyond its control.

The resilience of Britain’s medicine supply has eroded gradually in recent years, as global instability has placed growing strain on the supply chains it depends on.

“We’ve seen more global turbulence in general,” said Dr Davies. “It’s not unique to the UK, but it’s affecting countries across Europe, across the Western world, with the Iran war, with difficulties flying things over Ukraine and Russia, and challenges with shipping in the Red Sea.”

In the UK, shortages have been reported across a wide range of products, including antibiotics, attention deficit hyperactivity disorder medicines, epilepsy treatments, hormone replacement therapy, and some diabetes medicines.

The drugs most at risk are the cheapest and most widely used – statins, blood pressure pills and antibiotics – taken by millions of people and manufactured in China and India at huge scale and minimal cost.

“Some antibiotics are almost exclusively made in China,” said Dr Davies. “For some of the blood pressure medicines, they’re more likely to be made in India. But across the board, those two are where most of the raw ingredients for those active pharmaceutical ingredients come from.”

News.title: Fraudster jailed for 41 years over Pakistani nurse scam in Saudi
News.content:
A fraudster who sent 92 Pakistani nurses to Saudi Arabia on fake documents in an elaborate scam to provide workers for short-staffed Gulf hospitals has been jailed for 41 years.

Ghulam Zulfiqar Ali used forged experience certificates, created fake verification QR codes and phoney employment platform IDs.

Ali was being paid by the Saudi authorities to find staff, but also charged genuine Pakistani nurses who wanted a job overseas, in a racket that has caused major embarrassment to the Pakistan’s authorities.

Gulf nations including Saudi Arabia are experiencing a severe shortage of nurses, compounded by rapid population growth, a rising burden of chronic diseases, and heavy dependence on nurses from abroad.

The World Health Organization (WHO) forecasts a global shortfall of 4.5 million nurses by 2030, and recruiting nurses for developed countries is a lucrative trade.

The 91 women were all genuine nurses, but did not meet the criteria for the “Nurse Highly Qualified” visa category under which they were sent.

When the Saudi authorities realised the fraud they deported all the nurses.

Syed Shehzad Nadeem Bukhari, director of Pakistan’s Federal Investigation Agency, told the Telegraph: “They lost both their money and their employment, and the incident caused serious embarrassment to Pakistan internationally.”

Investigators found that between October 2022 and September 2023, a Pakistani employment firm called M/S Sahou Manpower obtained permissions for the recruitment of 108 nurses for a Saudi-based manpower company, to work in hospitals under the visa category “Nurse Highly Qualified”.

The investigation found the Saudi employer bore all recruitment costs, including visa processing fees and air tickets.

It paid the Pakistani recruiting firm between $800 (GBP 600) and $1,100 (GBP 830) per candidate. However, Ali was also demanding between $800 (GBP 600) and $1,000 (GBP 750) from each nurse.

Investigators found the candidates were genuine nurses, but did not meet experience requirements and were given fake certificates.

Meanwhile Ali had not uploaded their details to Saudi systems designed to verify and check qualifications and give each applicant a QR code. Instead he provided them with faked QR codes and verification platform IDs.

Ali was convicted of cheating, two counts of forgery and emigration offences.

He was given 41 years imprisonment by the special court in Rawalpindi. He was also fined £1,904 and ordered to pay £25,031 compensation – £272 to each of the 92 nurses.

His accomplice, Ghulam Fareed, was given three years’ imprisonment and a £544 penalty.

Nasreen Begum, one of nurses, told the Telegraph: “We are thankful to FIA for compensation. Most of us have genuine qualifications as nurse-midwives, licenced practical nurses, clinical nursing assistants and a lady health visitor but our documents weren’t verified and that landed us in a difficult situation.”

Zeenat Khan, another victim of the fraud, said she had opted to take a job in Saudi Arabia because she was jobless despite having nursing qualifications.

She said: “I have three kids and wanted to give them a good education. Now, I hope to get back my money,” she said.

Swera Ali said she had been working in a private hospital in her native Lahore, Punjab province, but received only £50 a month and performed 16 hours duty.

She said: “My parents took a loan from relatives to facilitate me, but my hope of making money from an overseas job was short-lived when they deported us after less than a month.”

Mr Bukhari added: “The investigation established that their nursing diplomas were genuine. The fake QR codes and fake [employment platform] IDs were created by the accused, and the experience certificates were forged by the visa agent without the knowledge of the nurses.”

News.title: How vaccines and antibiotics can beat some cancers
News.content:
At least one in eight cancers worldwide are caused by viruses and bacteria, according to a new study published in The Lancet.

An estimated 2.3 million new cancer cases in 2024 – out of a total of 20 million recorded worldwide – were caused by common infections, almost all of which could have been prevented with treatments such as antibiotics or vaccines.

Almost half of infection-linked cancers, around 760,000 cases, were caused by H. pylori, a bacterium that infects the stomach, researchers from the International Agency for Research on Cancer found.

The pathogen, which is typically ingested through contaminated food and water and is carried by around 60 per cent of the world’s population at any given time, can remain relatively undetected in the gut for between 20 and 40 years without causing any symptoms.

If left untreated, it can trigger chronic inflammation in the stomach and cellular mutations that, in some cases, lead to gastric cancer.

Cases of stomach cancer linked to H. pylori are particularly common in East Asia, where roughly 80 per cent of the population carries the bacterium. This is due in part to the prevalence of a more aggressive strain of the pathogen, known as CagA, which is endemic to the region.

East Asian diets – which typically include salty, pickled or smoked foods – can also damage the stomach’s protective lining and accelerate the inflammatory processes that can contribute to stomach cancer, researchers have found.

While H. pylori infection is treatable with a course of antibiotics, its symptoms often mimic those of other digestive problems and can be difficult to distinguish without testing.

This means the infection can remain undetected for years, allowing inflammation and damage to progress.

Sports.title: Burnham U-turns from supporting Man City owners after backlash from fans as it emerges club ‘could face criminal probe’
Sports.content:
Next

ANDY Burnham has been forced to back-pedal after saying he did not want to “lose” ­Manchester City’s mega-rich owners.

He was accused of political interference as sporting bodies decide the fate of the club — found guilty of more than 100 rule breaches.



Last night No10 clarified that the initial judgment against City was “serious” and “there can’t be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules”.

MPs and tax experts say City may owe more than £20million and could face a criminal probe. City deny any wrongdoing.



The Prime Minister was blasted for saying he would be “really concerned” if they quit after the Premier League revealed a damning £900million of financial breaches.

Burnham forged close links with the Blues’ owners — Sheikh Mansour‘s Abu Dhabi United Group — in his previous role as Manchester mayor, hailing their investment in the area.

But his comments — described as “extraordinary” by Tory critics — sparked fears of undue pressure placed on the government-backed football regulator, who may have to rule if City’s ownership model is “fit and proper”.

Mr Burnham rowed back amid mounting criticism. A No10 spokesperson said: “The Prime Minister has stressed it’s an ongoing independent process.

“It’s essential that it’s allowed to run its course and the outcome respected.

“Wherever wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences.“



City, who deny any wrongdoing and claim to have “irrefutable evidence” of their innocence, have until today to lodge an appeal.

Mr Burnham’s remarks on Wednesday came 24 hours after he used his Labour Party conference speech to set out a vision for doing politics differently.

Shadow Sports Minister Louie French said: “Andy Burnham’s intervention in support of Manchester City’s owners is frankly extraordinary.



“The club face unprecedented allegations and fans are horrified by what they are reading in the papers.

“Yet Burnham is publicly backing the owners even as the investigation continues.

“Fans will rightly ask whether political pressure is being applied here and how it relates to the owners’ well-reported investments in Manchester.

Mr French added: “Football must be governed independently, with the rules applying equally to everyone. Fans deserve confidence that no club or owner is above those rules.

“Burnham’s comments are completely out of touch with fans and the wider public.”



Reform Treasury spokesperson Robert Jenrick added: “Why is the Prime Minister siding with City’s owners when they’ve disgraced our national sport?

“He seems more interested in Middle Eastern money than protecting the integrity of the game. Fans deserve better than this sell-out.”

City’s owners spent hundreds of millions on housing and infrastructure projects in Manchester while Mr Burnham was mayor.

They include the £450million Co-Op live venue, a £200million football facility and £300million for the Etihad Stadium’s north stand.



There was also a £1billion, ten-year deal with the council to build up to 6,000 properties in Ancoats and New Islington, north-east of Manchester city centre.

Weeks after entering No10 this summer, Mr Burnham held a call with Mansour’s brother, UAE President Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed.

Last year officials from the UAE were said to have privately warned the Government that a harsh outcome in its Premier League case could damage relations and put billions of existing investment at risk.

Former FA boss David Bernstein, chairman of Manchester City from 1998 to 2003, said: “We’re going to see now whether this new (independent regulator) stands up, because the regulator will never be faced with bigger issues than this.



“I’ve been concerned all the way through that there’s a danger of political interference, whether it be that City are just, I use the words, ‘too big to fail’, or there’s a national interest involved.”

Respected football journalist Henry Winter called the PM’s comments “astonishing” and “alarming”, adding: “Burnham spoke as a politician seemingly with one eye on diplomatic and trade links.

“He spoke as a former mayor whose city benefited from investment in east Manchester by Abu Dhabi.”

He warned his words could further “embolden” City, adding: “Bit of an own goal by No10.”

COPS 'MUST PROBE CLUB' By Thomas Godfrey MANCHESTER City bosses should face a criminal probe and may owe millions in tax, a leading lawyer has said. An investigation by Dan Neidle’s Tax Policy Associates group says City could face a penalty of up to £24million over off-book payments to ex-boss Roberto Mancini. A Premier League panel of three top lawyers has described a consultancy contract said to have been set up with Mancini as a “sham”. It allowed the Italy boss, 61, who won the league with City in 2011-12, to receive millions in payments for working four days a year for a mysterious Abu Dhabi-based firm. Mancini received a base salary worth £1.45million after tax through HMRC systems in the UK. Yet records indicate he was also paid £1.75million a year by the Al Jazira Sports and Cultural Club for “consulting work”. Mr Neidle, one of Britain’s top tax experts, yesterday said records show up to £8.866million was ultimately paid to firms associated with Mancini. He added that the payments were a salary — liable to tax. The TPA report estimates that the total tax penalty faced by City could be as high as £24million, across Mancini’s three and a half years in charge. There is also maximum jail penalty of seven years for dishonestly falsifying accounting documents for gain. The report adds: “We are not suggesting that any specific individuals at Manchester City, or indeed Mr Mancini, committed an offence. “We are saying that there appear to be good grounds for a criminal investigation of the circumstances under which a sham arrangement was put in place and tax was not paid when it should have been.” A parliamentary select committee last night wrote to HMRC demanding to know if City would be investigated. Tory peer Lord Cruddas, whose CMC Markets firm sponsors Everton, said: “If accounts have been falsified and auditors misled then it’s potentially a criminal matter.” Mancini said on Monday that the “alleged double contract is not my concern”. HMRC was asked to comment.



Fans also hit out, including Gary Hetherington who posted: “Andy Burnham should be nowhere near this story. Yes, they may have put money into Manchester but this is sport, it should be independent.”

Annie Eaves added: “Andy Burnham has dug himself a big hole.”

But Oasis frontman and City supporter Liam Gallagher welcomed the PM’s comments, posting on X: “There’s only 1 ANDY BURNHAM. I told ya. Friends in high places.”

The football world was rocked last week when City were found guilty of more than 100 financial rule breaches from 2009 to 2018.

The Premier League said they had falsely boosted income by more than £900million, arranging “sham contracts” with commercial partners and filing inaccurate accounts.



The club were also accused of failing to co-operate with investigators.

The PM subsequently said of City’s owners: “I would be really concerned to lose them.

“They’ve been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester.

“Obviously, the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is.” But he added: “I can’t intervene more in the process.”

Independent Football Regulator chairman David Kogan has powers to assess the suitability of owners, directors and executives.



He said: “As proceedings remain ongoing between Manchester City and the Premier League we will await further developments.”

Sources close to City say they have “irrefutable evidence” to clear them on appeal.

He told fans: “Our confidence and intent in proving the Club’s innocence is just as strong as when this began.”

Sports.title: Man City players could RIP UP contracts and walk away for free as uncertainty surrounds Erling Haaland and Co’s futures

SOME of Manchester City’s biggest stars could now potentially rip up their contracts – and walk away for nothing.

Players will likely demand answers when they return to training next week after the club was found guilty of inflating revenues by more than £900million through ‘sham’ deals.



Erling Haaland and his City team-mates are not believed to have relegation clauses in their contracts.

But they could take legal action against the Etihad club and quit to join a rival for nothing.



Leading barrister Paul Gilroy KC told podcast Stick to Football: “A player could say, ‘You’ve breached the implied term of trust and confidence’.

“That is a possibility. I have seen commentators saying that is unlikely – but it depends on so many things.

“What’s the club going to say to the players? How do they sort it out financially?”

Rival players who missed out on trophies and Champions League places because of City’s actions could also launch legal action against them.

FORMER Tottenham talent Troy Parrott scored a sensational solo goal to give the Republic of Ireland an early lead against Austria.

The striker, 24, was dubbed the next Harry Kane when he was coming through the ranks in North London.



But Spurs cashed in on Parrott two years ago and he came back to haunt ex-Tottenham chief Jose Mourinho when he fired Real Betis to victory over Real Madrid last month.

And, at a time when the Premier League strugglers are crying out for a lethal finisher, their former gem bagged an outrageous wondergoal before doubling his tally with a clinical spot-kick.



Parrott, who also found the net during Ireland’s controversial victory over Israel last Sunday, turned Austria’s backline inside out early in the first half of the Nations League clash.

The red-hot marksman embarrassed Philipp Lienhart with a cheeky nutmeg before chopping past Nicolas Seiwald and casually sending his shot through keeper Florian Wiegele’s legs.

Parrott’s moment of magic had fans racing onto social media to compare him to a pair of iconic frontmen.

One said: “Holy. Luis Suarez is that you?”

A third stunned football fan claimed: “I think it’s the best individual goal I’ve ever seen in an Irish shirt.”

One wrote: “Wow, that’s pretty special.”

Sports.title: Portugal lose almost a MILLION followers within 24 hours of Cristiano Ronaldo quitting camp and flying home
Sports.content:
Next

THE official Portuguese national team Instagram account has lost almost a MILLION followers after Cristiano Ronaldo made the bombshell decision to leave camp on Wednesday.

Ronaldo dramatically left the national team amid rumours of a rift between him and head coach Jorge Jesus.



He did not feature for Portugal against Norway on Sunday, with Jesus later saying: “I’m the coach and I told the player that he wasn’t going to play.

“I told him I would take him to the bench and that, if I needed him for 30 minutes, he would play. But I saw the game differently, so he didn’t come on.



“It won’t be Cristiano, or any other player, who changes my ideas as a coach. Never. Neither him nor anyone else. Not even a president. Never.”

Jesus made his view clear during a press conference on Wednesday, shortly before Ronaldo made the decision to leave.

A statement from the five-time Ballon d’Or winner on social media read: “Following the national team manager’s press conference, and after a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I decided to leave the national team’s training camp.

“In due course, I will tell the Portuguese people the truth about the reasons behind my departure from the national team, to which I have always been dedicated.

“Now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my team-mates, without exception.”

Now, one day on from the statement, Portugal have lost almost a million Instagram followers.

Sports.title: English Wag who cheered on Argentina vs Three Lions in World Cup semi-final has contract ripped up by Hashtag United
Sports.content:
Next

KELCI-ROSE BOWERS hit the headlines when she turned her back on England during the World Cup – and now she has been cast aside by her club.

The defender, 22, is the girlfriend of Marcos Senesi, who joined Tottenham in the summer.



And Bowers was in the stands controversially cheering for her partner’s Argentina as Lionel Messi and Co ended England’s World Cup dreams with a stunning semi-final comeback.

But the Wag is now preparing to take her own career in another direction after Hashtag United Women ripped up her contract.



A statement read: “The club can confirm Kelci-Rose Bowers has left the club via mutual termination.

“We welcomed Kelci to the club this summer following her relocation from Bournemouth.



“But, unfortunately, the move has not worked out and the club have agreed to her transfer to another FAWNL club. We’d like to wish Kelci the best in this next chapter of her career.”

Bowers ditched Bournemouth for Hashtag when Senesi, 29, was snapped up by Tottenham after his deal with the Cherries expired.

She joined the south coast outfit on loan for the 2023/24 season before making the switch permanent, racking up 70 appearances and scoring 11 goals.

And Bowers helped Bournemouth to FA Women’s National League Division One South West glory, along with the National League Plate and the National League Cup.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

But the Cherries confirmed in June that she would be quitting, opening the door for a move to Hashtag.

Bowers, who featured for the England Under-15s and U19s earlier in her career, failed to make an impact at the Women’s National League Premier Division strugglers.

And that led to the Essex-based side being prepared to pull the plug on their agreement after just TWO MONTHS.

The model and influencer came through the ranks at Chelsea and Southampton before jetting out to Louisiana State University.



When she returned to England, Bowers joined Portsmouth and then switched to Bournemouth.

It was during her time with the Cherries that she met Senesi and they became a footballing power couple.

Sports.title: Humphries dazzles on the doubles to reach Grand Prix quarter-finals
Sports.content:
Luke Humphries put in a much-improved display as his doubling prowess and a 10-dart finish secured a 3-0 rout of Jermaine Wattimena and a spot in the World Grand Prix quarter-finals.

There were 3-1 victories for James Wade and Niels Zonneveld over Stephen Bunting and Gary Anderson, while Gian Van Veen came through a deciding-set cracker with Ryan Searle to triumph 3-2.

Humphries - the title favourite after defending champion Luke Littler's shock defeat to Luke Woodhouse on the opening night - had averaged only 80 and gone at 26 per cent on his closing doubles in a scruffy 2-0 win over Dave Chisnall on Tuesday evening.

Two nights later, the 2023 champion and 2024 and 2025 runner-up averaged 94.11 and secured a finishing-double percentage of 64, although his starting-double percentage of 74 was the most eye-catching stat as he peppered double 16 early in legs.

Image: Humphries will take on Niels Zonneveld in Friday's quarter-finals

'Cool Hand' - who will face Wattimena's fellow Dutchman Zonneveld in the last eight on Friday - hit his 10-darter at the start of the third set, while Wattimena twice hit the wrong double in the opening set.

Humphries said afterwards: "I've got a good chance of winning this. At the moment I'm a bit up and down, but if I can put that right I'm going to be tough to beat.

"It wasn't the best performance, but it was a good performance. It was a lot better than it was on Tuesday.

"I think I got in every time with my first three darts. When you're doing stuff like that, it's going to take a top performance to beat you."

Wade: Double start is 'hellish'

Wade, meanwhile, delivered a starting masterclass to reach his eighth World Grand Prix quarter-final, hitting an opening shot of 160 five times during his 3-1 win over Bunting.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player James Wade regularly started legs with 160s against Stephen Bunting

The sixth seed dropped his standards in the third set but was electric in the other three as he set up a meeting with Van Veen.

Wade said: "I am so grateful as it is so hard to win with a double start. We can play it cool and pretend to be relaxed but it is awful, it is hellish, really hard work.

"I don't feel anywhere near my best but I am having to play better against better players. I have loads more gears to go - but talk is cheap.

"And I am full of cheap talk!"

Van Veen wins thriller to secure Wade showdown

Elsewhere, Searle - who landed a 167 checkout, the highest of the week - threw for the match against Van Veen after breaking the Dutchman with a finish of 100 in the fourth set, only to be broken straightaway in the deciding leg.

Van Veen, who had led 2-0 in the penultimate set before being pegged back to 2-2, then blitzed the final set 3-0.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Ryan Searle pinned a brilliant 167 finish on the bull during his defeat to Gian van Veen at Mattioli Arena

The third seed said: "When I was 2-1 down in sets, I was like, 'oh no, this is not how I want to go out'.

"As good as double 16 went for me in the first round, it kind of bothered me today. But at the end it really came good.

"I was quite happy with my scoring, but just missed a couple of darts at a crucial time. Luckily I got the job done."

Anderson tumbles out as Zonneveld's run continues

Van Veen's compatriot Zonneveld followed his opening-round win over Josh Rock by dumping out Anderson, starting by winning a first set in which every leg went against the throw.

Anderson made a terrible start to the match, hitting single one and then suffering two bounce-outs, while he was the victim of another bounce-out in the third set as he aimed for a leg-winning bullseye.

Zonneveld subsequently broke before closing out victory in the next leg.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Gary Anderson sees the humorous side as he misses a double, followed by two bounce-outs, on his first three darts

The 28-year-old said: "Especially in this tournament, it is one of the biggest things in my whole career.

"I have achieved many things Pro Tour-wise and Euro Tour-wise but not on the main stage, just once at the World Series Finals. I have become a dad so less sleep and all that but I feel in rhythm again."

Sports.title: 'Awful' and 'hellish' - Wade's brutal verdict on unique World Grand Prix format
Sports.content:
Veteran James Wade admits playing the World Grand Prix is "awful" and "hellish" despite reaching the quarter-finals on Thursday.

The 43-year-old, who last lifted a major trophy at the UK Open in 2021, continued his bid for a third World Grand Prix after producing a superb display to defeat Stephen Bunting 3-1 in the unique double-start format in Leicester.

Wade averaged 93.20 and fired in 15 140s, defying a 96 average from Bunting to book his place in the last eight.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on Love The Darts, Polly James and Paul Nicholson discuss Wade's chances at the World Grand Prix

"I just felt like it was timing at the right place and the right time. It wasn't the right place for Stephen," Wade, nicknamed 'The Machine ', told Sky Sports' Polly James.

"I was better than average, I think. I am just grateful to win. It's so hard to win a double start.

"We can all play it cool and pretend to be relaxed and enjoying the game. But it's awful, it's hellish.

"It's not very nice. It's graft and just really hard work. We're not all cool, we are working very hard."

Wade, who took in a local art gallery in Leicester as part of his preparations, was asked whether he is currently playing some of the best darts of his career.

"Nowhere near really," he replied. "But I am having to play better against better players. I've got loads more gears to go.

"But talk is cheap and I am full of cheap talk."

Speaking at his press conference, Wade said: "I get nervous, I make myself feel ill, I don't want to get involved in it.

"I just want it to be over and done with quick.

"So am I well equipped or do I just deal with the c***** end of the stick better than others? It's so nerve-wracking; it's awful."

Sports.title: Shaw earns Man City draw with late Real goal dramatically disallowed
Sports.content:
Bunny Shaw and a dramatic last-gasp decision from the referee ensured Manchester City took a point off Real Madrid with a 1-1 draw in the Women's Champions League.

Standout Linda Caicedo had given Real the lead in the first half but City improved after the interval and Shaw levelled with an equally expert finish across the goalkeeper to put the league-phase clash in the balance.

Shaw headed over and Yui Hasegawa volleyed wide for the hosts before Ayaka Yamashita had to pull off an excellent stop to deny Irune Dorado as both sides pushed for a winner.

Silvia Cristobal thought she had clinched it in the 89th minute for Real Madrid with a wonderful finish into the top corner - but referee Silvia Gasperotti had whistled to stop play after inadvertently blocking Beth Mead from reaching the ball.

Real Madrid's players and coaching staff were furious and appealed for the goal to stand but ultimately this closely fought contest ended in a draw - the same result City achieved in their opening game away to Bayern Munich last week.

They will now turn their attention to this weekend's Women's Super League clash with Arsenal, live on Sky Sports, while Real prepare to face Barcelona.

Jeglertz: A lot of noise but players are very calm

Man City boss Andree Jeglertz:

"Of course there is a lot of noise outside but the players are very calm. There are no discussions, no thoughts from us [about the Premier League investigation].

"I haven't seen or noticed anything which would take any percentage out of the players' performance."

Real Madrid protest disallowed goal

Image: Real Madrid's Silvia Cristobal (left) reacts after referee Silvia Gasperotti rules out her goal

Image: Real Madrid head coach Pau Quesada protested against the ruled-out goal after the final whistle to referee Silvia Gasperotti

As it happened…

10: OFF THE BAR! Alex Greenwood clips an excellent free-kick from out wide into the Real Madrid six-yard box where Mary Fowler meets it - but sends her header against the bar!

21: BIG SAVE! Ayaka Yamashita rushes out to close down Felicia Schroder as she spins and shoots close to goal.

29: GOAL! Linda Caicedo runs around the outside of Laura Blindkilde Brown down the right and then is allowed too much space in the box by Greenwood before clipping her shot inside the far post.

40: CHANCE! Shaw shows good hold-up play in the box before laying off for Yui Hasegawa to shoot - and Maelle Lakrar bravely heads the powerfully hit effort away.

51: GOAL! Bunny Shaw hauls City level with a sharp finish across the keeper after Hasegawa does really well to turn the ball over in midfield.

62: OVER! It looks like a great chance for Shaw to add a second from Lauren Hemp's cross - but her header sends the ball over the bar.

75: OFF TARGET! A Greenwood corner comes out to Hasegawa just inside the area... but for the second time in the game she sends a volley wastefully wide!

77: SAVE! Another excellent stop from Yamashita, who gets a hand to Irune Dorado's shot.

89: BALL IN THE BACK OF THE NET...BUT NO GOAL! Real Madrid are fuming! Silvia Cristobal picked out the top corner and thought she had scored, but the whistle had already gone because referee Silvia Gasperotti had inadvertently blocked Mead, preventing her from getting to the ball.

Shaw pleased with second-half improvement from City

Man City's Bunny Shaw to Disney+:

"We started the second half much better than how we started the first half and that's something we're going to look on as a team.

"We're disappointed we didn't win the game but definitely [showed] fight at the end and that's good as well."

Analysis: City stay focused for hard-fought draw

Sky Sports News' Ben Ransom at City Football Academy:

"A hard-fought draw for City in their first home game back in this competition. There were a lot of distractions for everyone connected to the club in the build-up but it didn't show in their performance.

"An excellent strike from either side with moments of quality and it gives both teams something to build on from here.

"Big games await for both this weekend - City hosting Arsenal at the Etihad while Real Madrid go to Barcelona."

Sports.title: Bellamy gets perfect response as Wales beat 10-man Norway
Sports.content:
Wales responded to their disappointing defeat to Denmark with a spirited victory over Erling Haaland and 10-man Norway in Cardiff.

Craig Bellamy had admitted he was hurt by the performance against the Danes as his side continued their winless start to their Nations League campaign.

However, after a slow start, the Dragons showed their heart by producing an unerring display in front of their home fans to turn around an early deficit to secure three points.

The big news pre-match was that Erling Haaland started for the visitors in his first game since Manchester City were found guilty of all charges related to serious breaches of Premier League financial rules by an independent commission.

Image: Oscar Bobb opened the scoring for Norway

Haaland was largely anonymous though, and it was another former City man in Oscar Bobb who opened the scoring in the worst possible start for Bellamy's men. However, the setback appeared to galvanise the hosts, who responded brilliantly.

Sorba Thomas looked unstoppable down the left-hand side, and after a number of dangerous crosses came to nothing, he found his mark shortly before the half with Daniel James sliding home an equaliser.

Image: Dan James equalised for Wales before half-time

James was at the heart of a chaotic opening few minutes of the second half. Torbjorn Heggem fell asleep at the restart, and was forced to pull down James as he looked to nip in and bear down on goal just 15 seconds into the half.

The defender was shown his marching orders, and Neco Williams smashed home the resulting free-kick low to the goalkeeper's right to turn the game on its head.

Wales had numerous chances to extend their lead and failure to do so made for a nervy ending. However, they held on to secure their maiden Nations League A victory.

Key moments from Cardiff

11: GOAL! Bobb gives Norway early lead after silky Odegaard assist.

17: INJURY! Ryerson forced off early on, with Sorba Thomas toying with replacement Holmgren Pedersen for remainder of the half.

28: CHANCE! Wicked Thomas cross nearly put into own net by Ajer.

38: GOAL! Thomas finally gets his reward as he sets up James for equaliser.

46: RED CARD! Heggem dismissed 15 seconds into second half for dragging down James.

48: GOAL! Williams completes comeback with resulting free-kick.

59: CHANCE! Haaland heads over from close range.

71: WIDE! Thomas misses target in search of deserved goal.

81: HAALAND CHANCE! Striker heads straight at Ward.

Williams: The first two games wasn't us - we put it right today

Wales defender Neco Williams speaking with BBC Sport:

"We knew the first two games wasn't us. The principles, the standards. We knew we had to put it right today.

"We analysed, we were looking at what went wrong in the first two games. We worked in training and we had to put that right. Obviously that worked.

"Going 1-0 down early, it is easy for heads to drop. How we felt in the last two games, it was easy to do that again. But we never did. We kept going and we deserved to win in the end."

Image: Neco Williams says Wales showed their true selves after disappointing performances against Portugal and Denmark

On his goal:

"I think it was more instinct. Looking at the goalkeeper's position and where the wall is. You just decide what's best. Going across the goalkeeper was the best tonight."

On beating a team the level of Norway:

"It's massive for us. Everyone saw how well they played at the World Cup and how good they are as a nation. They've got world-class players. We can do it against these top nations. We have to look forward now until the next game."

Sports.title: Neco Williams fires revitalised Wales to fightback win against 10-man Norway
Sports.content:
On a night when Erling Haaland moped around the pitch, dragging his hulking frame across the Cardiff turf, Wales registered a welcome victory over 10-man Norway and their first this year. Was this just one of those games where the game’s deadliest finisher was stuck on the fringes or was it a case of 115 things occupying his mind? Either way, this defeat proved a humbling experience. “You’re just a shit Kieffer Moore,” was the chant aimed at Haaland from the locals.

Daniel James cancelled out Oscar Bobb’s well-worked opener in the first half and 17 seconds after the restart Torbjørn Heggem was sent off for fouling James as the Leeds winger streamed towards goal, resulting in a free-kick from which Neco Williams earned Craig Bellamy a timely win with an unerring strike.

“It feels a bit like the first punch in the face in a long, long time,” said the Norway and Arsenal captain Martin Ødegaard after his country lost successive games for the first time in four years. “Now we have to respond, stick together and fight back.”

For Bellamy, a first win since last November eased the mounting negativity after a bruising run of results, chiefly their World Cup playoff defeat to Bosnia and Herzegovina in March and a listless display in Denmark last Sunday. “I felt my own disappointment since Bosnia and I’ve felt the stick as well,” the Wales head coach said. “The summer wasn’t easy. These games weren’t easy. But I’ve seen it … I’ve seen managers before me get it. I’ve seen the abuse the previous manager [Rob Page] got. It’s been a really difficult couple of months but it’s ‘welcome to this’ if you want to step into this … this is it. I do think we could be kinder to each other.”

It was plain to see Bellamy had been hurting and he cited his daughter receiving abuse on social media. “I chose to live back down here because I wanted to be on the ground, I wanted to be called a wanker to my face,” he added.

View image in fullscreen Torbjørn Heggem sees red straight after half-time. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

“The World Cup [playoff defeat] moved, I just felt the shift … Look, I am a strong person, I think we all are, but it’s the people around me I’m conscious of. It’s just society. What are we? Eight prime ministers in the space of 11 years? It’s nuts ... We’re such a small country, why can’t we have each other’s backs? Why don’t we look after each other more? The others can go at us. We’re too quick [to criticise].”

View image in fullscreen Dan James brings Wales level in the first half. Photograph: Nick Potts/PA

Wales bounced off the canvas after Ødegaard’s cute ball released Bobb on goal to open the scoring on 11 minutes. Liam Cullen, now of third-tier Leicester, pinched the ball from Sander Berge after the Fulham ­midfielder was sluggish to claim Fredrik Aursnes’s pass and Wales raced away from the scene.

Cullen and Lewis Koumas burst forward and Sorba Thomas zipped a low cross into the box, where James beat David Møller Wolfe to the punch. Thomas, who by his own admission loves staying wide to get chalk on his boots, was a constant threat.

Norway were punished for being slow out of the blocks in the second half, Heggem hauling James down after the restart. James does everything at speed and Heggem knew he was in trouble. The Spanish referee Alejandro Hernández awarded a free-kick on the edge of the box and ­Williams dispatched a wonderful right-foot strike to Ørjan Nyland’s right, to the surprise of the former Aston Villa and Reading goalkeeper.

Bobb played draught excluder behind a white wall of Norway shirts and Nyland stepped to his left. Nyland was out of position when he had to shuttle across his goalline when Williams thrashed the ball into the bottom corner.

Haaland had one of those games; he was on the periphery and recorded just 11 first-half touches, the fewest of any player, including the Borussia Dortmund full-back Julian Ryerson who was forced off through injury after 16 minutes. Ethan Ampadu easily won what, technically, will go down as a duel on halfway but in truth Haaland just stuck out a leg in the hope of claiming the ball. His first whiff of goal came a couple of minutes before the interval but Ryerson’s replacement, Marcus Pedersen, misread Haaland’s movement and the move collapsed.

The substitute Josh Sheehan spurned a golden chance to extend Wales’s advantage, sending a weak shot at Nyland after more fine craftsmanship from Thomas to release the Bolton midfielder on goal. Up the other end, Haaland ambled across the box in preparation for another Pedersen cross. When it arrived Haaland soared high but unmarked sent a header straight at Danny Ward. Then came a puff of the cheeks, a look to the turf. It has been that kind of week.

Sports.title: Nations League: Ronaldo-less Portugal prosper while Klopp gets first win as Germany coach
Sports.content:
Portugal maintained their perfect start to Nations League Group A4 as Jorge Jesus’s squad showed little signs of missing Cristiano Ronaldo with a 4-2 victory over Denmark in Copenhagen.

The 41-year-old Al-Nassr forward and five-time Ballon d’Or winner left the camp before the match amid reports of a falling out with Jesus, his former club manager, having been left on the bench throughout a victory in Norway.

João Cancelo gave Portugal a 13th-minute lead before Brentford midfielder Mikkel Damsgaard equalised.

Gonçalo Ramos swiftly put Portugal back in front after 25 minutes, with Napoli forward Rasmus Højlund levelling things up at 2-2 early in the second half following a swift counter.

Vitinha’s header, his first Portugal goal, and a late strike by João Félix made it three straight wins.

“A victory of the highest quality,” said Jesus. “This Portugal team scored four goals and put in a performance which, in my opinion, was of a very high standard – and that cannot be overlooked. Of course, this is more important than anything else that has happened.”

New Germany head coach Jürgen Klopp got his first win with a 2-0 Group A2 victory over Serbia in Munich. Bayern Munich midfielder Tom Bischof fired in his first senior international goal and Liverpool forward Florian Wirtz then added a second in the 61st minute.

Germany produced a disciplined and intensive game, illustrating the high-pressure soccer Klopp wants to instill in the team. “That’s going in my archive. We’ll make a video out of it now,” Klopp said. “That’s how we want to play.”

View image in fullscreen Jürgen Klopp (right) applauds fans alongside Tom Bischof, who scored his first international goal in the victory over Serbia. Photograph: Angelika Warmuth/Reuters

Speaking to public broadcaster ZDF, he added: “The mix of football and attitude was top level today. I told the boys that this has to be our benchmark.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Wirtz said: “It was important to win again, just for the spirit in the team, and to send a signal out that we’re good football players and also a good football nation. Definitely a step in the right direction.”

In the same group, Tijjani Reijnders scored a late equaliser as the Netherlands fought back to draw 2-2 with Greece, who remain top. Fotis Ioannidis and Giorgos Masouras had the home side 2-0 up at the break.

Liverpool defender Virgil van Dijk powered in a header from a corner on the hour. After Denzel Dumfries had seen his goal ruled out by VAR for offside, Reijnders lashed home a rebound in the 89th minute to secure a point.

In Group B3, Israel and Kosovo played out a goalless draw in Debrecen, Hungary. In Group D1, Malta and Gibraltar drew 1-1 while in Group D2, Azerbaijan were held to a goalless draw by Liechtenstein in Baku.

Sports.title: Pro-Palestine protests interrupt game as Ireland pass up 2-0 lead in draw against Austria
Sports.content:
Protests halted events in Dublin twice before the Republic of Ireland were forced to settle for a 2-2 draw after Austria came back in the second half of their Nations League encounter at the Aviva Stadium.

Despite a significant security presence, the contest was twice interrupted in the opening 45 minutes, first due to what campaign group Stop the Game later referred to in a statement as a “limited tennis ball protest”, when – around the 20th minute – tennis balls wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text “#StopTheGame” were launched on the pitch.

Then around the 35th minute a man ran on to the field of play from the opposite side carrying what appeared to be a Palestinian flag and was immediately tackled by security and carried off.

It has been a tumultuous week for the Republic. Their two Nations League fixtures against Israel have divided opinion in the country, sparking protests, including one which took place pre-match outside the stadium. The Republic’s behind-closed-doors “home” game against Israel in Backa Topola, Serbia, is scheduled for Sunday, and the manager Heimir Hallgrímsson on Wednesday confirmed it was their intention to play.

Troy Parrott got the hosts under way with a sensational 12th-minute opener and added a penalty on the stroke of half-time.

A pair of substitutes proved the Republic’s undoing after Alexander Prass halved the deficit in the 71st minute and Michael Gregoritsch drew the sides level six minutes later.

View image in fullscreen Michael Gregoritsch (left) points to the sky after scoring Austria’s second goal. Photograph: Brian Lawless/PA

Hallgrímsson’s men had a chance to top Group B3 with a victory, but they sit third behind Austria and Kosovo at the halfway point of the group stage.

Hallgrímsson made three changes, including the re-introduction of Finn Azaz, who was greeted warmly when his name was announced over the PA system before the match.

The goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu, who had made himself unavailable for the Israel meetings, was back in the squad, while Liam Scales and John Egan were awarded starts.

There was an audacious early effort from Sasa Kalajdzic, who tried to catch Caoimhín Kelleher off his line with a lob from midfield, before the Republic enjoyed a couple of attacking spells deep in the visitors’ half.

It was a brilliant opener from Parrott, who realised he was on his own after bringing down Adam Idah’s glanced-on header from a goal kick.

View image in fullscreen Troy Parrott slots home the Republic of Ireland’s opening goal in the 12th minute. Photograph: Evan Treacy/EPA

The Real Betis striker was sandwiched in a triangle of white shirts before nutmegging Philipp Lienhart and evading every other challenger with a mazy run before planting the ball past Florian Wiegele and into the bottom corner.

Play was briefly paused just before the 20th minute to clear up the tennis balls, a pause both teams used for a hydration break. The second stoppage of play took place around the 35th minute.

Kelleher denied Patrick Wimmer and there were a few more promising spells for Austria before Parrott doubled their lead. Ryan Manning won the penalty after he was clipped in the box by Nicolas Seiwald. Parrott stepped up after a video assistant referee check and blasted it past the Austria keeper.

Austria cut the deficit after Liam Kitching was caught out and Austria worked the ball to the unmarked Prass, who blasted the ball beyond Kelleher. The offside flag was initially raised, but the decision was reversed by VAR.

The Brentford keeper then failed to stop Gregoritsch, guessing the wrong way as the Augsburg forward fired into the corner.

The Republic captain, Dara O’Shea, was denied by an excellent leaping Wiegele save, Gregoritsch directed a shot over the crossbar, and both sides fended off attempts at a late winner.

Sports.title: Shaw secures WCL draw against Real Madrid as Manchester City show spirit after week of turmoil
Sports.content:
Andrée Jeglertz, the Manchester City head coach, said the noise surrounding the guilty verdict dished out by the Premier League had zero impact on his women’s team’s performance after they played out a high-quality draw with Real Madrid in the Women’s Champions League.

Khadija ‘Bunny’ Shaw’s ruthless finish earned City a point against an impressive Real Madrid side on a night when the hosts were surely glad for attentions to turn – however briefly – towards on-pitch matters after a week when the wider football club has dominated the headlines for the wrong reasons.

“Of course there is a lot of noise but the players are very calm – I haven’t seen or noticed anything that will take any percentage out of the players’ performance,” Jeglertz said.

The result – which was a fair reflection of an even but entertaining game – left both sides with two points from their opening two fixtures but City will know their league phase opponents should theoretically become less challenging from hereon after their opening draw at Bayern Munich. The Swedish coach added: “It is OK, it’s an OK start in the Champions League. It’s not ideal but it’s a good start and we know what is needed from us in the rest of the tournament.”

Quick Guide WCL roundup: PSG pummel Leuven Show The day after Paris FC played their first Women’s Champions League home game at Stade Jean-Bouin, across the road from Paris Saint-Germain’s Parc des Princes, PSG’s women’s team entertained Leuven 20km away at the club’s suburban training centre. Rasheedat Ajibade put the hosts ahead from close range after nine minutes against the Belgian side. Naomie Feller (pictured) then scored a quick-fire double, before Sakina Karchaoui and Vitória Yaya completed PSG's 5-0 rout. In the early games, Modesta Uka scored Austria Vienna’s first goal in the WCL but Inter's captain, Ivana Andrés, levelled in the fourth minute of added time to earn a 1-1 draw. Inter dropping points left Barcelona, who thrashed Roma on Wednesday, as the only WCL team with six points after two games. In a match between two teams that had lost in the opening round, HB Køge crushed visiting Swiss team Servette 5-1 in Denmark. PA Photograph: Benoît Tessier/REUTERS Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Jeglertz had been at pains to insist that it has been “business as usual” for his team despite the damning guilty verdict released by the Premier League towards the men’s side. There was a strange mood around this stadium in the buildup to kick-off with opinions mixed.

Speaking to supporters on the bridge that connects this venue with the neighbouring Etihad Stadium, some appeared relaxed about the situation and unsure what it had to do with the women’s team, while others were clearly troubled and looking forward to watching some football as a form of escapism.

View image in fullscreen Khadija Shaw fires home Manchester City’s equaliser early in the second half. Photograph: Martin Rickett/PA

An elderly City fan, who did not wish to be named, said pre-match: “We’ve been through rough times before, we’ll come through rough times again,” in a matter-of-fact manner. Another simply demonstrated what appears to be a growing dislike for reporters asking about the 115 charges when they said angrily “you’re from the media?” before using an expletive and promptly walking away.

A much politer, younger woman simply expressed her sadness and her hopes that it wouldn’t cause the players stress.

Once the match started, there were occasional references to the news from the stands; midway through the first half one home fan sang ‘Sheikh Mansour, my lord, Sheikh Mansour, oh lord, Sheikh Mansour’, to the tune of Kumbaya, although nobody else appeared to join in. There was also a small group of men carrying an inflatable banana in one corner defiantly chanting about ‘City going down with a billion in the bank’.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Weekly Sign up to Moving the Goalposts No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

In general, though, the regular Women’s Super League match-going fans who are members of the supporters club seemed focused on their usual repertoire of fan chants to encourage the players, whether singing about the brilliance of Aoba Fujino and later chanting the name of Mary Fowler, who hit the crossbar with a header before the break.

By then Real Madrid were already ahead courtesy of Linda Caicedo’s clinical, low finish into the bottom corner after a lethal burst of pace. The visitors could have scored as early as the first minute, when a sloppy mistake by Carlotta Wamser allowed Felicia Schröder to shoot but her effort flew narrowly wide and bounced off the stanchion, rippling the net but from the wrong side. It was a sign of the Spanish team’s intent and they looked sharp throughout.

City’s play was significantly more urgent and incisive after the break and – after Yui Hasegawa spurned a volleyed chance when she was in space inside the box – it did not take long for the hosts to equalise. Shaw turned and clinically fired into the corner of the net with great technique after good pressing from City led to Hasegawa winning the ball in midfield and feeding Shaw in the area. It was the Jamaica striker’s fifth goal of the season in all competitions and her first of this Champions League campaign.

Suddenly the WSL champions were dominating the territory, although Caicedo did go close at the other end with a diagonal shot that bounced wide. The introductions of Beth Mead, Sam Coffey and Grace Clinton from City’s bench only seemed to further strengthen the hosts.

Hasegawa volleyed just wide again, this time from the second phase after a half-clear corner, in another let-off for Real Madrid, who had gone close themselves at the other end when Ayaka Yamashita did well to save from Caicedo. The home fans were on their feet to applaud Yamashita and chant her name when she later produced a quick reaction save to keep out Irune Dorado’s close-range effort and keep the score level.

Sports.title: Criminal or saviour? Rui Pinto abandoned by Portuguese authorities after Manchester City leaks
Sports.content:
More than a decade after Rui Pinto set up the Football Leaks website in a crusade triggered by the Fifa scandal in 2015, he finds himself in the middle of a growing storm. The former history student with trademark spiky hair who used to make extra cash selling books about the second world war has not held back with his statements on social media since Manchester City’s guilty verdict from an independent Premier League commission.

The first targets for Pinto, whose leaks of private documents prompted first Uefa then the Premier League to investigate City’s financial affairs, were what he alleged were the club’s “cheating” executives for demonstrating “a complete lack of respect for the rules”. On Wednesday he turned his attention to the Fifa president, Gianni Infantino.

Less than two hours later, Portuguese authorities confirmed Pinto would no longer be protected as a witness. That is understood to have come as a surprise to the 37-year-old, who finds himself without a job, a home or an income. He has been living in a safe house under protection and has never disclosed his location, and it is understood he has received no visitors.

The Guardian understands talks had been initiated to begin the process of reintegrating Pinto back into social and professional life. That initiative will be halted, leaving Pinto to fend for himself. He has been advised not to return home, contact family members or visit crowded places socially or for work.

Pinto has been a protected witness since 2020 after he agreed to grant Portuguese authorities access to millions of files acquired before his arrest in Budapest, where he moved after a year in the Hungarian capital as an Erasmus student. He has since become a cause célèbre who divides opinion in his homeland and been compared to Edward Snowden and Julian Assange.

The Premier League’s case against City drew heavily on evidence provided by Football Leaks, including the chief executive, Ferran Soriano, writing in an internal memo: “We will need to fight this and do it in a way that is not visible, or we will be pointed out as the global enemies of football.” City continue to protest their innocence and Soriano said this week the club would appeal on the basis that the commission’s verdict “contains clear, material errors of law, principle and fact and that it is unsafe”.

The question of whether the evidence should be used provoked huge public debate in Portugal, but the Premier League’s regulations stipulate that any investigation “shall not be bound by judicial rules governing the admissibility of evidence. Instead, facts relating to a breach of these rules may be established by any reliable means.”

View image in fullscreen Rui Pinto has been advised not to return home, contact family members or visit crowded places. Composite: Manchester City FC/AFP via Getty Images; Manchester City FC via Getty Images

That tallies with Pinto’s assertion in 2019 that it is “nonsense” to claim the data he provided is tainted because it was obtained illegally. “The documents are authentic,” he said. “That is what matters. This and the content. I don’t consider myself as a hacker, but as a citizen who acted in the public interest. My sole intention was to reveal illicit practices that affect the world of football.”

Pinto wore a bulletproof vest during his first trial in 2020 and came in through a dedicated entrance guarded by special forces. People attending the proceedings were searched three times and not allowed to bring mobile phones or computers into the courtroom. At the start of the trial, snipers were positioned on buildings near the courthouse.

He was given a suspended four-year sentence in September 2023 after being found guilty on counts of attempted extortion, illegal access to data and breach of correspondence. Pinto has always insisted he never received money but has admitted regret over asking Doyen Sports Investments for money after he obtained thousands of the agency’s internal emails.

He said to Der Spiegel in 2019: “I told myself: ‘If I allow them to buy me out now, I am no better than this whole business.’ So, I wrote to Doyen and told them to keep their money. Not a single cent was paid. What I did was very naive. Looking back now, I regret it. But I repeat that I deny having committed any criminal offence.”

That defence was found to be “not credible” by the judge, who said Pinto and his co-defendant, the lawyer Aníbal Pinto, were “well aware of the illegality of their conduct”. Rui Pinto started living in a safe house after being sentenced. He lost his mother to cancer when he was 11 and is permitted to communicate with his father occasionally. Even when he was in a relationship with the actor Mikaela Lupu, who he said he had met over “a glass of wine and a book” when announcing they had split last year, the security of the property was never compromised.

For six years, Pinto has been seen in public only twice. On one of those occasions, at a supermarket in Lisbon, he was accompanied by police officers and wore a cap and sunglasses. On the other, he was assaulted in an altercation believed to have been sparked for football-related reasons. It is understood that Pinto was left with a bruised eyebrow and the police were informed, although no complaint was filed.

The decision to end his witness protection has raised concerns for his welfare. Pinto is understood to fear for his safety. A bounty was reportedly placed on his head after the revelations made by Football Leaks and Luanda Leaks, which exposed the inner workings of the business empire of Africa’s richest woman, Isabel dos Santos. She denied corruption allegations.

The Guardian attempted to obtain clarification from the commission for special security programmes (CPES), a Portuguese body under the ministry of justice responsible for managing special witness protection programmes, as to why Pinto is no longer a protected witness but received no response. There has been speculation it could be a response to Pinto being accused of hacking the computer systems of PLMJ, the Portuguese law firm founded by José Miguel Júdice.

Júdice testified against Pinto during the Football Leaks trial, describing the episode as a theft that had caused him significant moral and psychological distress. Júdice is the father of Rita Alarcão Júdice, Portugal’s minister of justice since June 2025.

In April, Pinto was acquitted in a second trial of 241 counts of illegally accessing email accounts belonging to several Portuguese sports bodies, including Benfica, and to law firms, magistrates and the tax authority. None of the evidence he provided to the Portuguese authorities has resulted in any charges.

Sports.title: Jürgen Klopp disgusted by claims his Germany team are ‘not white enough’
Sports.content:
Jürgen Klopp has reacted with disgust to a social media debate questioning whether the Germany team he is in the process of forming are “white enough”. Klopp said he believed there was no point in giving room to “such people and their utterances”, dismissing them as “complete nonsense”.

Asked to respond to the debate as to whether the national team were “not German enough” or “not white enough”, he said: “There is absolutely no reason to pay attention to these people. You won’t get my thoughts on this. I have little time in everyday life for idiocy – and even less on social media.

“The great crux of our lives is that everyone is allowed to express their opinion … it’s insane when something like that exists.”

Klopp said watching sportspeople interact with each other was proof to him that mutual respect was still possible. “The world could learn a thing or two from a sports changing room … There, everyone is respected based on the facts and not discredited based on false opinions.”

Klopp, whose plans for Germany since he took over as coach in the summer have attracted huge attention, said the players he had gathered at the national team camp, including several players with a migrant background, “could not be better united than they are”.

The barrage of racist and generally offensive commentaries on social media followed Germany’s 1-0 defeat by Greece last Sunday, in the Nations League, marking the first time Greece had beaten Germany.

It is also reflective of plenty of utterances from MPs of the far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD), the largest opposition party in the Bundestag, who have repeatedly and consistently criticised the diversity and ethnic makeup of the national team, often referring to the squad in derogatory terms such as a “politically correct mercenary force”.
