Klopp, who has a four-year contract running until the end of the 2030 World Cup, was speaking before Germany’s Nations League match on Thursday against Serbia.

Sports.title: US lined up instead of Qatar to host inaugural Women’s Club World Cup
Sports.content:
The US is poised to host the first Women’s Club World Cup in January 2028, becoming the latest in a series of major Fifa tournaments staged in North America. Discussions to take the competition to the US are at an advanced stage, with Los Angeles and San Diego among the favoured host cities.

It will follow the men’s tournament, whose expanded version debuted last year, in being staged by a country that also hosted the men’s World Cup this summer.

While a deal is yet to be confirmed, the path has cleared for the US to hold the 19-team event without going through a formal bidding process, even though Qatar was in talks with Fifa about hosting.

The winter scheduling will avoid a clash with the men’s Copa América, which the US is the frontrunner to host in June and July 2028, but raises the prospect of a hectic year-round calendar for the world’s top players. The Club World Cup is placed squarely between the 2027 Women’s World Cup and the 2028 Olympics, which will demand full-strength squads. A number of top clubs are in favour of a rule change limiting players to one international tournament per year, whether for club or country.

Fifa is keen to use the Club World Cup as a dry run for the 2031 Women’s World Cup, which the US will host in conjunction with Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica in a decision to be formally approved at an Extraordinary Fifa Congress on 23 November.

Football’s global body is eager to assess the stadium venues, pricing and demand for tickets at the smaller 19-team Club World Cup before the 48-team World Cup three years later. Time to organise and market the Club World Cup is tight, given it will start on 5 January 2028.

Sources have cited the chaos engulfing Fifa’s leadership since the emergence of Gianni Infantino’s ill-fated FFE scheme as a significant reason for the backlog of hosting decisions still to be taken. In July, Europe’s top clubs threatened not to participate in future Club World Cups unless the FFE project was shelved. They also warned the threat would hold unless a joint venture between European Football Clubs and Fifa, agreed in outline form, but yet to be signed off, was completed before television rights could be sold for the women’s Club World Cup.

Another tournament awaiting a venue is the 2029 men’s Club World Cup. The US has expressed interest in hosting that competition, but should the women’s event be confirmed it appears more likely to be co-hosted by Morocco, Spain and Portugal before they jointly host the men’s World Cup the following year.

Sports.title: Yemen and football in the face of civil war: ‘It would be very nice to give the world a different headline’
Sports.content:
The Yemen national coach, Noureddine Ould Ali, chose not to reach for a good old-fashioned football excuse after his team’s 1-0 loss to Qatar in the Gulf Cup on Saturday, despite a clear penalty not given their way. The defeat meant the Reds crashed out of the eight-team regional tournament, taking place in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, with a game of the group stage remaining.

There are other factors the Algerian could list for a defeat against a team that was at the World Cup. Qatar have the Aspire Academy, state of the art stadiums and a former Spain and Real Madrid coach – Julen Lopetegui – in charge. Yemen have nothing approaching that and have not played a home game since 2012, a 2-1 win over Palestine in Sanaa.

Two years later, the capital city came under the control of the Houthis, an Iran-backed militant group, provoking a Saudi-led intervention and years of fighting. The United Nations brokered a truce in 2022 that did reduce hostilities, but the situation has escalated again. In early September, the Houthis swept down the Red Sea coast in its first major military advance in five years and have been targeting Riyadh and other places in Saudi Arabia with missile strikes.

View image in fullscreen Yemen will play in the Asian Cup in January for the second time, managing to qualify despite political turmoil in their country. Photograph: Sipa US/Alamy Live News

At the time, the national team had been training in the southern port city of Aden, home of the presidential leadership council, Yemen’s internationally recognised, Saudi-backed, governing body. “The situation in Aden was OK. We tried our best and had a training camp with local players and then we joined up with the rest of the squad in Jeddah,” Ould Ali says.

“The situation is a political situation and it is not stable. In football we have to be careful. We have a lot of attention on outside factors, but we always try to focus on the football and do better. In Saudi Arabia, the welcome has been great, the people are very friendly and there is a high level of training facilities, hotels and everything. It means we could focus on football.”

Losing 4-0 to the United Arab Emirates in the opener was a reality check, but the UAE have a lot of naturalised talent from overseas to count on and even Andrés Iniesta coaching in the domestic second tier. Yemen barely has a top tier with the local league affected by the fighting. They still beat Bahrain 5-2 in their final group game.

“The league stopped for a long time and restarted this year and they finished the first half of the season,” Ould Ali says. “It is very important. The players need to play, need to keep fit and show their talent.

“The people support us. It is a religion in Yemen. Everyone likes football and the national team and follows their star players. The Yemeni people are the same as anyone else.”

Most of the players are based at home and before the 27th edition of the Gulf Cup, Yemen was the only one of the eight never to have won the tournament and have never got out of the group.

It is hard for the players to keep fully focused on football while in Saudi Arabia. “They worry about what is going on in the country and they hope their families are OK,” the coach said. “This is normal, but they are professional and I ask them to try to focus on the games. I have lived this situation before, I have geopolitics experience in the region.”

Ould Ali spent three years in charge of Palestine from 2018 to 2021, after more than four years as an assistant coach. Instability is not an unfamiliar theme for him. “Each situation is different. Yemen is a problem between Yemenis, not between outside countries.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Fortnightly Sign up to The Hotspot A new fortnightly newsletter covering the intersection of sport and the climate crisis Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

View image in fullscreen Algeria’s Noureddine Ould Ali is used to instability. He coached Palestine before his stint with Yemen. Photograph: ZUMA Press Inc/Alamy Live News

“For a coach, Palestine was very difficult. The Israeli soldiers used to stop me for eight to 10 hours before I could go to work. The players are not free and when we played overseas they stopped the players. It was a pleasure for me to work with Palestine, their difficulties are not made by Palestinians.”

A reunion with Palestine is not impossible at the 2027 Asian Cup, which will also be hosted in Saudi Arabia. In June, Yemen, slightly surprisingly, defeated Lebanon to become the last team to qualify for the quadrennial tournament. “It was a great day for Yemen football and we hope we could make people back home smile for a while.”

In January, Yemen return to Jeddah for their opening game against South Korea and players such as Atlético Madrid’s Lee Kang-in, Kim Min-jae of Bayern Munich and Son Heung-min. It will be a step up from the Gulf Cup and the people back home will be watching.

“Again, we will try to make the people at home proud,” says Ould Ali. “It would be very nice to give the world a different headline about Yemen. When we are united we feel we can beat anyone.”

Sports.title: Portugal star hails Jorge Jesus and ‘step forward in attack’ after Cristiano Ronaldo leaves
Sports.content:
Portugal's Cristiano Ronaldo era may finally be over.

Well, that's if Vitinha's latest admission is anything to go by.

3 Vitinha's goal against Denmark was his first for Portugal Credit: Getty

Vitinha was one of four goalscorers for Portugal as they ran out 4-2 victors over Denmark in Nations League action on Thursday.

Also amongst the goals was Goncalo Ramos, who now firms as the 41-year-old's long-term replacement at the top of Portugal's attack.

It was a dominant display from the Selecao, who finished with 11 shots on target compared to Denmark's tally of just three.

Most notably, the win came a day after Ronaldo abruptly walked out on the national team amid reports he grew frustrated with a lack of minutes under new manager Jorge Jesus.

But if Ronaldo thought his strop would prompt several of his teammates to launch a passionate defence of his qualities, he better think again as Vitinha instead heaped praise on Jesus' tactical acumen when speaking to TVI Noticias.

What did Vitinha say about Portugal's performance against Denmark?

And, rather tellingly, the Paris Saint-Germain ace claimed Portugal 'took a step forward' in their attacking play with Ronaldo nowhere in sight.

"It's all thanks to the manager's work," Vitinha said.

"The truth is, we played an excellent game, and there's no hiding that.

"Winning here is extremely important, in a very difficult place to play, and two years ago, when we lost here, we learned that lesson. Don't be fooled by the result, because it was a very difficult game.

"Furthermore, it was the best performance we've had so far. We are growing, and the truth is, the more we work with the manager, the more we assimilate his ideas.

3 Jesus was appointed as Portugal boss on a four-year deal, so it's very much his ship to steer Credit: AFP

"Today we took a step forward in attack."

Portugal's win over Denmark also extended their perfect record under Jesus from three games.

And Vitinha is desperate to make it four from four when they return to Porto's Dragao Stadium on Sunday for a clash with Norway.

The midfielder also heaped praise on his teammates for the way they blocked out the noise generated by the Ronaldo sideshow.

"We tried to focus on the game and I think that's what we did," Vitinha said.

"We responded incredibly. Congratulations to the whole group."

3 Against Norway, Ronaldo was an unused substitute for the first time in 18 years Credit: Getty

Jesus, who vowed to 'explain everything' regarding the Ronaldo saga following Sunday's game against Norway, was equally delighted with his side's display in Denmark.

Crucially, the 72-year-old now feels like he has the entire group 'under control.'

What did Jorge Jesus say about Portugal's players?

"I have a group that believes... believes in my ideas, believes in the coach's ideas," Jesus said.

"Because they have so much individual quality, things go more easily.

"If you think this means having a group under control, then I have a group under control. Because they go hand-in-hand with me, with my ideas.

"The things that happen don't separate the group, they haven't separated us and they won't separate us."

Jesus and his side now turn their attention to Sunday's clash with Norway, but once the full-time whistle goes, all eyes will turn to Ronaldo who, like the national team boss, insists he'll tell all about the sideshow.

Sports.title: Gutted Arsenal star forced off pitch with worrying hamstring injury
Sports.content:
Arsenal have been dealt a potential injury blow during the latest round of Nations League action.

The Premier League champions are already without five current first-team players.

3 Christos Tzolis was forced off for Greece on Thursday in a fresh injury blow for Arsenal Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Mikel Arteta will now be sweating on the fitness of Christos Tzolis ahead of his side's return to action against Leeds United on October 10.

The summer signing was forced off after just 17 minutes for Greece against the Netherlands on Thursday night.

Tzolis had started for his country in Thessaloniki as they looked to continue their winning start in League A.

However, the winger pulled up with an apparent hamstring injury inside the opening 15 minutes.

He was visibly emotional whilst receiving treatment from the medical staff.

Tzolis could be see pulling his shirt over his face as he lay stricken on the turf.

After several minutes of treatment, he was replaced by Giorgos Masouras for the hosts.

Whilst the severity of the injury is not yet known, reports in Greece state Tzolis will be assessed on Friday to determine the full extent of the issue.

In Tzolis' absence, Greece took a first half lead through Fotis Ioannidis before Masouras added a second in stoppage time.

The Dutch later pulled a goal back shortly before the hour mark thanks to Virgil van Dijk's header.

3 Tzolis was unable to continue after suffering a hamstring injury inside 15 minutes Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Their comeback was completed in the 89th minute as Tijjani Reijnders snatched a dramatic late equaliser as the match ended level.

Tzolis has been in impressive form for both club and country so far this season.

Following his arrival from Club Brugge, the 24-year-old has provided four assists in eight appearances for Arsenal across all competitions.

Meanwhile, he scored in Greece's 2-1 win over Serbia last week before starting in their victory over Germany on Sunday.

Arsenal's injury woes

His potential injury setback adds to an existing selection headache for Arteta ahead of the Premier League's return.

The Gunners boss is already without long-term absentee William Saliba, who has been ruled out until November with a back issue.

3 Tzolis adds to a growing list of injuries for Arsenal and Arteta to contend with Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

Elsewhere, Kai Havertz is currently being assessed after picking up a hamstring injury in Germany's draw with the Netherlands.

The forward has missed both of his country's matches since against Greece and Serbia.

Cristhian Mosquera, Ben White and Declan Rice are also currently sidelined.

However, the trio have been earmarked to return against Leeds next weekend.

Sports.title: Leicester sign former Premier League player on free transfer
Sports.content:
Leicester City have strengthened their midfield stocks with the arrival of Will Smallbone on a free transfer.

The Ireland international joins the Foxes on a three-year deal following his departure from Southampton earlier this summer.

2 Leicester marks the fourth different club Smallbone has represented Credit: Getty

Smallbone's switch to Leicester also reunites him with Russell Martin, who was his manager for 54 games when both were at the Saints.

Will Smallbone's first words as a Leicester player

"I'm really looking forward to [getting started]," Smallbone said.

"I'm hungry and looking forward to being at Leicester City.

"I have spent a long time playing under the manager previously, I know a few of the boys here and I've played against a few of them in my time so I think that should help me to settle in quite quickly."

Will Smallbone's career at a glance

Smallbone's departure from Southampton brought an end to his 18-year association with the club having joined aged eight.

He made 90 appearances for the Saints across the Championship and Premier League, registering 15 goal contributions.

While at Southampton, Smallbone enjoyed loan spells at Stoke City and Millwall.

Smallbone also boasts 15 caps for the Republic of Ireland, although he has not made an international appearance since last October.

He now drops into League One for the first time in his career with Leicester.

Smallbone is eligible to make his Leicester debut as soon as October 6 against Stevenage in the EFL Trophy.

2 Martin and Smallbone played their part in the Saints winning the Championship play-off final in 2024 Credit: Getty

How has Leicester City performed this season?

The Foxes have had a difficult start to life in the third tier, accruing just nine points from their opening seven league fixtures.

Leicester's early season struggles prompted fans to turn on Martin, who took over as manager in the summer.

Adding to Leicester's on-field woes is uncertainty at ownership level.

Foxes owner Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha is understood to be seeking over £200million for the club.

One party interested in purchasing Leicester is the Bharat Consortium Group, fronted by Scottish-Indian businessman Neil Lal.

However, Lal warned that there are serious financial hurdles to be cleared if his consortium are to complete a takeover.

Sports.title: Arsene Wenger changed Arsenal’s history but Gunners ‘block’ was his downfall
Sports.content:
Arsene Wenger needs 'more respect' from his time at Arsenal, according to former player Theo Walcott.

However, the legendary Gunners boss was unable to overcome a mindset amongst his squad which stopped them winning major titles.

5 Wenger won 17 trophies during his 22-year tenure as Arsenal manager Credit: PA

Wenger was appointed manager in October 1996, five years on from Arsenal's most recent league title triumph at the time.

The then little-known Frenchman had an immediate impact, winning a league and cup double in his first full season.

Across almost 22 years in charge, Wenger won a total of 17 trophies including three Premier League titles and seven FA Cups.

He also oversaw the club's historic 'Invincibles' triumph during the 2003/04 season.

However, Wenger's reign also saw Arsenal endure a nine-year trophy drought between 2005 and 2014.

The Gunners also failed to win any European silverware, losing their only Champions League final appearance to Barcelona in 2006.

Walcott joined Andy Goldstein and Darren Bent on Thursday's Drive to discuss Wenger's Arsenal legacy 30 years on from his arrival in north London.

The former England international was signed by Wenger as a 16-year-old in January 2006 and spent 12 years playing under him.

Arsenal players had 'block', says Walcott

Although he won the FA Cup three times with Arsenal, Walcott believes the side had a 'block' when it came to competing for major honours like the Premier League and Champions League.

The Gunners only finished higher than third once whilst he was at the club.

5 Arsenal won the race against big clubs in the Premier League to land Walcott Credit: Getty

Asked why Arsenal did not win the Champions League under Wenger and if they could now, he admitted: "I don’t know what it was, but it was like a block and I think there was a mindset in the players that we were happy just getting in the top four.

"I genuinely felt like that at the stage and it felt like we were probably second best when it came to Liverpool and (Manchester) United.

"We’re talking about United from that era, they were the best team I’ve ever played against, best players I’ve ever played against.

"So we were competing, finishing fourth, but at times wasn’t good enough for a lot of people on the outside.

"However, on the inside, and the manager as well, it was good enough for him at the time when we’re actually going through a change at the stadium as well and you think about teams when they move on, different stadiums, the knock-on effect it creates.

"Leaving Highbury, all the history and the memories, that’s tough for players to that next best thing, but I felt we coped and we did well with everything that was going on in the background.

5 Walcott admits Arsenal and Wenger's mindset played a role in the club's lack of major titles Credit: Getty

"So we’re very proud of everything that we’ve done and achieved, but it’s just one of those.

"I do feel like this team’s got it, though, I feel like this team can do it, they can play that other side of it as well which we couldn’t do."

Under Mikel Arteta, Arsenal won their first league title for 22 years last season as well as reaching the Champions League final.

However, they were ultimately beaten on penalties by Paris Saint-Germain back in May.

Should Wenger have left Arsenal sooner?

During his time at the club, Walcott scored 108 goals and added 70 assists in 395 appearances under Wenger.

He would depart for Everton in January 2018 during Wenger's final season at the helm.

5 Walcott spent 12 years with the Gunners, winning three FA Cups during that time Credit: AFP

Walcott now admits the previous campaign would have provided a better opportunity for the manager's departure, though.

The 37-year-old added: "When I look at my whole career with him, being there for 12 years, and Arsene, he was there for maybe too long in the end.

"However, I feel that when you’re at that level for that long, when people aren’t expecting much from you straight away and then all of a sudden you bring success so quickly, now they’re expecting a lot from you every season.

"He was doing that and he was continuing to do that. I do feel like he needs more respect in that sense and it was quite toxic towards the end.

"Then I look at it and I always feel how you want anything to end isn’t the way it’s going to go. Anyone’s career can end in football, it doesn’t quite go how it’s planned to some extent.

"So I felt maybe when he won the FA Cup, that was a great time to just think ‘right, let’s move on’. Maybe he was just waiting for the right time, the right person to come along."

5 Wenger opted to stay in charge for another season after winning the FA Cup in 2017 Credit: Getty

Wenger won his seventh and final FA Cup in 2017, but saw his side finish fifth in the Premier League.

It represented their lowest position of his tenure to that point as they failed to qualify for the Champions League for the first time in 19 years.

The following campaign would see Arsenal slip to sixth as fan support for Wenger shifted to calls for him to leave the club.

He would ultimately leave at the end of the campaign, with the Gunners board opting to end his contract in the summer of 2018.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi completes takeover of second tier club
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi has completed his purchase of Spanish second-tier club Eldense.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner's interest in buying the team first emerged last month.



3 Messi has retired from Argentina duty but is still playing for Inter Miami Credit: Getty

Eldense have now announced the purchase of a 100 per cent stake in the club by Messi.

Messi's lawyers had been in talks for some time with the club's previous owners, the Colombian investment group TH – led by Juan Carlos Trujillo.

In a statement confirming the news, Eldense said: "Club Deportivo Eldense officially announces the acquisition of the entity by Leo Messi, beginning a new and exciting stage in the more than 100 years of history of the institution.



"The arrival in Spanish professional football as owner of CD Eldense of one of the most important figures in the history of sport marks the beginning of a long-term project with the aim of boosting the sporting, institutional and social development of CD Eldense.

"Founded in 1921, CD Eldense faces this new stage with the ambition to consolidate and grow in professional football, while projecting its roots, history and blue and red feeling.



"The transaction is pending the required authorization from the CSD under the terms established in the Sports Law."

Eldense have just returned to LaLiga2, the second tier of Spanish football, winning promotion back to the division at the first time of asking having been relegated in the 2024/25 season.



Based in the Valencian city of Elda, Eldense are managed by former Spain striker Claudio Barragan, who won six caps for La Roja in the early 90s.

Founded in 1921, they play their home games at the 5,776-capacity Estadio Municipal Nuevo Pepico Amat.

Messi's involvement already goes beyond the pitch

This is not Messi's first venture into club ownership.

3 Messi averaged 0.86 goals per game for Barcelona Credit: Getty

The 39-year-old Argentine – who recently announced his retirement from international football following an epic career in which he captained his country to World Cup glory – took full ownership of third-tier outfit Cornella back in April.



But Eldense would be the first professional club in his portfolio.

Messi's prospective investment is said to be a solo endeavour without the support of any partners.

The greatest of all time?

It was in Spain where Messi ascended to all-time great status, during 17 glittering years with Barcelona.

A ten-time LaLiga champion and four-time Champions League winner with Barca, Messi played 778 games to top the club's all time appearances list – not to mention amassing 672 goals to obliterate their all-time scoring record.

He won six of his eight Ballons d'Or as a Barca player, before leaving in 2021 an undisputed icon.



3 Eldense were founded in 1921, but have never played in the Spanish top-flight Credit: Getty

After a two-year stint with Paris Saint-Germain, he headed to MLS to join Inter Miami in 2023.

Messi in good company among current pros

Messi isn't the only active player to have dipped their toes into the world of club ownership and he joins, among others, his great contemporary Cristiano Ronaldo.

Ronaldo purchased a 25 per cent stake in another LaLiga2 outfit, Almeria, in February this year.



Last year, Croatia legend Luka Modric became a minority investor in Championship Swansea City.

In 2024, Kylian Mbappe's Coalition Capital investment fund bought an 80 per cent stake in French club Caen.

And the previous year, fellow France star N'Golo Kante struck a deal to take over as owner of Belgian outfit Royal Excelsior Vitron.

Sports.title: Marcos Senesi’s girlfriend leaves club less than two months after signing
Sports.content:
Marcos Senesi’s girlfriend leaves club less than two months after signing

Marcos Senesi's girlfriend, Kelci-Rose Bowers, has left non-league club Hashtag United as her shock move has 'not worked out'.

Bowers, who was previously at Bournemouth just like her partner Senesi, only joined Hashtag less than two months ago.



2 Senesi's girlfriend Bowers has left Hashtag United less than two months after signing for the club Credit: Instagram @_kelci.rose_

She departed the Cherries' women's side to follow Senesi to London after he signed for Tottenham over the summer.

The Argentinian international signed a four-year contract at Spurs at the start of June after his deal at Bournemouth expired.

Bowers then left the club too and signed for Hashtag in a shock move just a few weeks later in August.



However, the former England youth full-back has now already departed the club after just three competitive games.

She played the full 90 minutes in Hashtag's season opener against Lewes and then scored in the League Cup before featuring against her old side on August 30, in what was her last appearance.



Hashtag admit move 'has not worked out'

Hashtag announced on Thursday that her contract had been terminated and revealed that she is leaving to join another FAWNL (FA Women's National League) side.

"The club can confirm Kelci-Rose Bowers has left the club via mutual termination," they wrote.



"We welcomed Kelci to the club this summer following her relocation from Bournemouth, but unfortunately the move has not worked out, and the club have agreed to her transfer to another FAWNL club.

"We’d like to wish Kelci the best in this next chapter of her career."

The 22-year-old's new club is yet to be confirmed and Hashtag kept their name out of their statement.

2 Bowers has already left her new club, with Senesi also experiencing a tough start to life in London after his transfer Credit: Instagram @_kelci.rose_



Senesi in the same boat?

Bowers' switch to London hasn't gone too well, and so far, Senesi's move to Tottenham doesn't seem to have either.

Having starred for Bournemouth last season, he has played just one Premier League game for Spurs this season.

The Argentina international, who was in his nation's World Cup squad, started their opening defeat to Brentford, but has remained an unused substitute under Roberto De Zerbi since.

His only other appearance came in the Carabao Cup, as his new side were dumped out at home to Liverpool last month.



Micky van de Ven and Jan Paul van Hecke seem to be the starters for De Zerbi - so will Senesi have to continue to wait for a chance?

The centre-back will hope that things 'work out' for him and that he doesn't also have a quick exit, similar to partner Bowers.

Sports.title: Theo Walcott: Exceptional Arsenal can retain Premier League title but this vulnerability worries me
Sports.content:
Theo Walcott: Exceptional Arsenal can retain Premier League title but this vulnerability worries me

Theo Walcott has backed Arsenal to retain their Premier League crown, but only if they don't fall apart away from home.

The Gunners have won four of their opening five league fixtures, with the only defeat coming away against Brighton.



3 Arsenal only lost three times away from home in the league last season Credit: Getty

It was a contest the Seagulls dominated, with Arsenal's frustration perhaps best summed up when Declan Rice kicked out at Malick Yalcouye.

The result gave credence to Walcott's belief that the Gunners, who he described as 'exceptional', remain 'a little vulnerable away from home'.

Theo Walcott explains why Arsenal are 'vulnerable' away from home

Part of Walcott's reasoning is the drop-off in performance from summer signing Christos Tzolis, who was booked and got taken off at half time in his first away game as a Gunner against Aston Villa.



"I like Tzolis, but from what I've seen away from home, I haven't been as impressed," Walcott said on talkSPORT Drive.

"It's difficult to really shine away from home. You can have those players that are great at home or great at training, but can't [do it] away when it really matters."



Walcott likened Tzolis' dip in performances away from home to ex-Gunners star Mesut Ozil whenever Arsenal visited the notoriously vociferous Selhurst Park.

"Don't play him, play someone else, play someone who is going to work for the team or do something different," Walcott added.



Despite his concerns over Arsenal's vulnerability in away games, even though they've picked up six points from a possible nine on their travels this term, Walcott remains adamant the Premier League title will remain in north London.

"I think they are exceptional and I do feel they've got everything to retain it," Walcott said.

"But it's not going to be easy, because they'll want to win the Champions League."

3 Walcott made nearly 400 appearances for the Gunners Credit: talkSPORT



What is Arsenal's record of set pieces this season?

Another element of Arsenal's game Walcott is slightly concerned about is their set pieces.

The Gunners used them to great effect last term, netting a league-leading 23 goals from set pieces.

However, this season has been a different story as they are yet to get off the mark.

And the longer their drought continues, Walcott fears it could lead to some worrying dressing room conversations.



Theo Walcott voices fears of Arsenal's set pieces

"I know it's really early, but it looks like a stressful environment already," Walcott said.

"You look at the set piece side of things, it hasn't really happened yet. We scored a lot of set pieces at this stage last season, that hasn't happened yet.

3 Set piece coach Nicolas Jover has become a regular fixture on the touchline when Arsenal have a chance with a dead ball Credit: Getty

"So take that away and the players will be thinking, 'Are we doing this right?'



"You don't want the players to be having those conversations, but deep down, they will be, because it hasn't quite gone to plan."

The Gunners will have to wait until October 18, when they take on Nottingham Forest, to remind the competition about their credentials away from home.

Sports.title: Gabriel and Bruno Guimaraes update amid injury fears over Arsenal duo
Sports.content:
Brazil are working alongside Arsenal to not overload Gabriel and Bruno Guimaraes.

The duo are away on international duty with the five-time world champions, who have ventured to Australia and India for friendlies.

2 The centre-back has missed just 45 minutes of action for Arsenal this term Credit: Getty

Carlo Ancelotti's side began the break with a double-header against Australia in Townsville and Brisbane.

A late equaliser from Rayan rescued a 1-1 draw in the opening fixture before the Selecao ran out 4-2 victors in the second contest.

How many minutes have Gabriel and Bruno Guimaraes played for Brazil?

Guimaraes started both matches but came off in the 62nd and 81st minutes of the first and second game respectively.

The midfielder also got on the scoresheet in the second match.

As for Gabriel, he did not feature in the 1-1 draw but played the entirety of the 4-2 win.

Brazil then opted to hold an open training session the day after their win over Australia.

Why didn't Bruno Guimaraes and Gabriel participate in Brazil training?

However, a small group of players, including Gabriel and Guimaraes, conducted a drill separate to the main group at the start of the training session.

The groups then joined up for the rest of the session, but Gabriel and Guimaraes were not involved.

Instead, they were spectators on the sideline.

Luckily for Gunners fans, Gabriel and Guimaraes' non-participation was merely a precaution.

2 The midfielder moved to Arsenal from Newcastle this summer for £75milion Credit: Getty

It is reported that the duo are being managed due to the number of games they've played this term for Arsenal coupled with the lengthy journey to Australia from England.

When is Brazil's next game?

Brazil will conduct one training session before they face India in Kolkata on October 3.

The contest marks the first time Brazil has played India in men's football.

There is also a significant gulf between the nations, with Brazil ranked fifth in the world while India is 138th.

However, Ancelotti will not be taking India lightly.

"It's a preparatory game, a friendly, but for us, there is never a friendly game," Ancelotti said ahead of the game.

Brazil's historic clash against India is due to kick off on Saturday at 3pm.

Sports.title: Jorge Jesus insists he has a 'clear conscience' and team remains united despite Cristiano Ronaldo saga amid rift with captain - as Portugal beat Denmark in first match since star's sensational walk-out
Sports.content:
Jorge Jesus insists he has a 'clear conscience' and team remains united despite Cristiano Ronaldo saga amid rift with captain - as Portugal beat Denmark in first match since star's sensational walk-out

Portugal manager Jorge Jesus is standing firm amid a rift with Cristiano Ronaldo that saw the superstar forward leave the national team camp.

Ronaldo, 41, landed in Madrid in the early hours of Thursday morning after flying from Copenhagen, where Portugal faced Denmark on Thursday, on his private jet. He had been seen leaving the Parken Stadium in the Danish capital on Wednesday after missing a third consecutive training session.

Ronaldo later confirmed in a statement on Instagram that he had left the team's camp because of comments made by Jesus in his press conference.

The Portugal boss said the captain would not start the Denmark clash, just days after sitting on the bench for the entirety of the 2-1 win in Norway, but insisted there was no issue between the two.

Jesus, meanwhile, who took over from Roberto Martinez after the World Cup, oversaw a 4-2 win for his side on Thursday night, and insisted he remains in control of the team – with full faith from the players.

'I don't have a group in my hand. I have a group that believes in the coach's ideas,' he said. 'They believe in my ideas and, because they have a lot of individual quality, things become easier.

'If that's having a group in my hand, then I do, because they go hand in hand with me and my ideas.'

Portugal manager Jorge Jesus insists he is in control of his players and has a 'clear conscience' amid his feud with Cristiano Ronaldo

Ronaldo left the Portugal camp after taking issues with words in his manager's press conference before they faced Denmark

Reports in Portugal claim Ronaldo could be suspended from playing for his country for between one and six months if he is found to have 'abandoned' the team.

The Portuguese Football Federation's disciplinary code states: 'Any player who, having been regularly called up, unjustifiably abandons or fails to appear for training, a match, or any activity of the national teams or related to the sporting representation of the FPF or Portugal, will be sanctioned with a suspension of one to six months.'

Ronaldo said: 'After the national team coach's press conference, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp.

'In due time, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to my departure from the national team, to which I have always dedicated myself.

'Now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates.'

Jesus, though, who also managed Ronaldo at Al-Nassr insists his conscience is clean.

'It's not difficult for me to focus,' he added. 'You know what's difficult for me? It's not understanding what's going on inside. It's not knowing how to train my players. That's what's difficult for me. The rest... zero.

'What's important is what we have to do. The things that happen don't separate the group, they haven't separated us and they won't separate us.'

One group of fans showed support for Jesus in the stands as Portugal beat the Danes 4-2

The support, however, was split, with some making it clear they were siding with Ronaldo

Jesus received support in the stands from some of Portugal's fans, with one fan group each wearing a shirt spelling out: 'Love u Jesus'. Other fans held up banners with Ronaldo's face and name on.

Speaking before the Denmark game, Jesus insisted he had a 'completely' clear conscience amid the Ronaldo saga. 'It was a frantic few hours because we had two games,' he added.

'Now we have another one... Besides, I've been in football for many years and I know I didn't do anything to prevent the situation from continuing as before.'

Footage published by A Bola showed Jesus and Proenca being booed by a small group of fans who had gathered outside the team's hotel in Copenhagen before the team made the short journey to Parken Stadium.

Ronaldo held talks with Jesus and Proenca on Wednesday morning, a meeting initially described as amicable. But the rift between Ronaldo and his manager appeared to deepen after Jesus's press conference.

Jesus admitted Ronaldo had been 'angry' with him, with footage showing the captain walking off down the tunnel after sitting out the victory in Norway.

Jesus said: 'There was no incident whatsoever. Any player - and I was a player myself - when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on, no-one is happy about that.

'Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It's nothing to make a fuss about.'

Jesus also suggested Goncalo Ramos would keep his place in the side ahead of Ronaldo for the Denmark match. 'If I need (Ronaldo), he'll come on,' he said. 'If I don't need him, he won't.'

Jesus had originally planned to bring on the veteran striker for a 30-minute cameo but then decided to leave him on the bench, which has seemingly sparked the feud.

Sports.title: Ireland's clash with Austria is HALTED as furious fans throw hundreds of tennis balls onto the pitch in protest at matches against Israel going ahead
Sports.content:
Ireland saw their Nations League game against Austria brought to a halt as fans protested their matches against Israel. There was doubt over the weekend whether Ireland would fulfil their fixtures against Israel this international break, but the first game was played at the weekend and the second is scheduled to take place too. Ireland beat Israel 3-0 in their first fixture in Hungary on Sunday night, with goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu having pulled out of the highly-charged match on ethical grounds. A petition to stop the game going ahead had been signed by almost 20,000. Hundreds of pubs in Ireland refused to show the first encounter and have vowed to do so again for Sunday's game, while there were protests outside the team hotel in Dublin. The players did not shake hands, and Israel's captain and FA spoke out against the team after the match. On Thursday, meanwhile, fans launched tennis balls onto the field at the 20-minute mark at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin to protest the games taking place. Some balls were wrapped in stickers featuring the Palestinian flag and the text #StopTheGame. Ireland's game against Austria was paused after fans threw tennis balls onto the pitch at the Aviva Stadium A fan with a Palestine flag also ran onto the field with several members of security ejecting him One fan, roughly 15 minutes later, also ran onto the field waving a Palestine flag, with a number of security personnel required to remove them. A majority of players, meanwhile, described as 'significant' by the Football Association of Ireland, ultimately elected to fulfil their 'away' clash on Sunday. A 'Stop The Game' campaign – organised by the pressure group Irish Sport for Palestine called for fans to gather ahead of the match with Austria to voice opposition to Sunday's match with Israel. Ireland captain Dara O'Shea did not shake hands with Israel's skipper Manor Solomon at the coin toss last week, and Ireland wore black armbands 'in recognition of all lives lost in the (Gaza) conflict'. The Ireland players also snubbed the Israeli National Anthem by pointedly looking at the ground while it played. The second match against Israel will take place behind closed doors in Serbia. Bazunu was the only member of the squad to officially make himself unavailable for selection for the Israel matches, but the Bolton goalkeeper chose to remain with the team and be with them for the Austria match. He will then be replaced in the squad by Josh Keeley for the second fixture with Israel. Some balls appeared to have Palestine stickers on - Ireland will take on Israel for a second time in eight days on Sunday Ireland manager Heimir Hallgrimsson had previously said his team are 'playing against genocide' amid Israel's attacks on Palestine, where more than 70,000 people have been killed since the war in Gaza began, according to the territory's Hamas-run health ministry. He also criticised 'lies' that had been reported concerning Bazunu's withdrawal from the first fixture and insisted there is a 'strong bond' in his squad. 'Gavin is a great lad. I've always had a good relationship with him and it's probably more tough for him than the other players, but they have really welcomed him,' said Hallgrimsson. 'There's been a lot of lies said around all of this, but we welcome him back and he's taken part, amazing. 'I think it shows his character, as well, to be with us, so I want to give him praise for that. I want to give the players praise for how welcome they have been with him. After Sunday's game, Israel captain and west Ham winger Manor Solomon hit out at his Irish opponents, saying: 'They said nonsense during the game, I don't want to talk about them. 'If I say what I think about them, I'll probably be banned for a few games so I don't want to say. Of course they hate us and we don't like them. 'I'm already looking forward to the next game against them, it's going to be completely different. What they did with the anthem? I'm not interested in them, we have a country that is ten times better than theirs, stronger, an amazing country with amazing people. (They) can play all their tricks. We are Israelis and love the country. And that will always be the case.' The episode is the latest sign of growing hostility towards Israel and comes weeks after 12 countries including the UK, France and Canada announced sanctions on illegal Israeli settlements in the occupied West Bank. Goalkeeper Gavin Bazunu withdrew from the squad to face Israel at the weekend due to their actions in Gaza The match came against a backdrop of ongoing and increasingly volatile disagreement between the two countries about Israel's military offensive in Gaza. In May 2024, Ireland officially recognised a Palestinian state – alongside Spain and Norway – and later that year joined South Africa's Gaza genocide case against Israel in the International Court of Justice. The country has also refused to take part in Eurovision since 2026 due to Israel's ongoing participation in the song contest and was the first EU nation to boycott goods from illegal Israeli settlements in the West Bank. In June, the country issued travel bans on Israeli government ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich. The war began on October 7, 2023, when Hamas-led terrorists invaded Israel, killing some 1,200 people, mostly civilians, and taking 251 others hostage.

Sports.title: Arsenal dealt ANOTHER injury blow as Christos Tzolis is forced off in Greece's clash with Netherlands just days after Kai Havertz suffered the same fate
Sports.content:
Arsenal dealt ANOTHER injury blow as Christos Tzolis is forced off in Greece's clash with Netherlands just days after Kai Havertz suffered the same fate

Arsenal have suffered yet another injury blow during the international break, with Christos Tzolis forced off with an apparent leg injury while playing for Greece.

The winger left the field in the 18th minute of his side's clash with the Netherlands with his shirt covering his face, and Gunners fans now face a nervous wait to discover the severity of the issue.

It comes a matter of days after first-choice Arsenal striker Kai Havertz was also injured against the Dutch.

Havertz was tasked with leading the line in Jurgen Klopp's first match as Germany's new head coach, and lasted just 30 minutes of the fixture with the forward having gone down appearing to signal an issue with his hamstring.

Havertz's issue emerged just minutes after he had fallen victim to a poor challenge from Quinten Timber, the brother of Havertz's Arsenal team-mate Jurrien.

Timber had arrived late for a challenge and caught Havertz high on his knee, with the German attacker immediately falling to the pitch.

Arsenal have suffered another injury blow, with Christos Tzolis picking up a leg injury while playing for Greece against the Netherlands

It comes just days after Kai Havertz was injured while facing the same side with Germany

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta could now be without two of his first-choice front three for the return of Premier League action next weekend, when the champions will take on Brighton.

Bukayo Saka, the first-choice right winger, is in the England squad and could feature in the Three Lions' games against Croatia and the Czech Republic.

Declan Rice had already withdrawn from England duty with an injury, while Arteta is also currently without Cristhian Mosquera, Ben White and William Saliba.

Captain Martin Odegaard left Norway's defeat by Portugal on Sunday with a foot issue, sparking more concern, but returned to the side for their game against Wales.

Tzolis has started all five of Arsenal's Premier League games so far, making eight appearances in all competitions – picking up four assists.

Sports.title: Disgraced Team USA gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar is quietly REMOVED from Michigan sex offender registry
Sports.content:
Disgraced Team USA gymnastics doctor Larry Nassar has been quietly removed from the Michigan Sex Offender Registry list.

Nassar, who served as team doctor for the national gymnastics team from 1996 to 2014, used his position to exploit hundreds of young athletes, including medal-winning Olympic gymnasts Simone Biles and Aly Raisman.

He is currently serving multiple prison sentences lasting decades after being convicted on multiple counts of sexual abuse and child pornography in both federal and state court.

According to the Eaton County (Michigan) Prosecutor's Office, the 63-year-old is among more than 20,000 people whose names have been removed from the sex offender list after the Michigan State Police recently purged thousands of individuals from the database whose crimes happened before July 1, 2011.

A Michigan Supreme Court ruling on September 9 said that amendments to the Sex offender Registration Act issued in 2021 cannot be used to retroactively require registration due to older incidents, leading to the purge of the database.

The prosecutor's office wrote on social media that: 'The Michigan Supreme Court's decision to eliminate SORA requirements for these offenders is deeply concerning. Our community, along with the victims of these crimes, expected the registry to provide a measure of protection and awareness—assurances that have now been removed by the Court's ruling.'

Larry Nasser has been quietly removed from the Michigan Sex Offenders Registry List

Nasser is serving decades in prison after being convicted of multiple crimes

The registry is intended to 'assist the public' with preventing future criminal sexual acts by convicted sex offenders, according to Michigan State Police, and typically lists a legal name, photo, primary address, work address, age, physical description and court with records relevant to the criminal conviction.

'His conduct occurred before 2011 despite his convictions coming after,' said The Eaton County Prosecutor's Office, confirming Nasser's removal, per CBS News.

The prosecutor's office claimed the Supreme Court could have applied for a different interpretation and allowed for certain sex offenders to stay on the list.

More than 150 gymnasts were abused by Nassar during his 30-year career. Nassar admitted to sexually assaulting the athletes when he worked at Michigan State University and USA Gymnastics.

The doctor also admitted to possessing child pornography, and more than 100 women sought over $1billion from the federal government for the FBI's failure to stop him.

He was sentenced in federal court in 2017 to 60 years in prison on charges of possessing child sex abuse material. The following year, Nassar was sentenced to up to 175 years and up to 125 years, respectively, in two separate Michigan courts for molesting female gymnasts under his care.

Following the federal sentencing, U.S. Attorney Birge said: 'Today was a day of reckoning for Larry Nassar. He more than deserves this punishment for what he did.

'He consumed child pornography on a massive scale. We found 37,000 images of child pornography on his computers. Insatiable hunger of that nature simply encourages those who produce such images to continue to sexually exploit children. Compounding his danger to the public,

'Nassar was an insidious hands-on child predator in his own right. He took advantage of family friendships. And he treated his license to practice medicine as a license to sexually molest children. Thanks to the brave victims who came forward, we learned the full scope of his depravity. The breadth and dark depth of his heinous acts are extraordinary.'

Larry Nassar is pictured in court during his sentencing hearing in Michigan in January 2018

Olympic icon Simone Biles was among Nasser's long list of hundreds of victims

In April 2024, the US Justice Department announced a $138.7 million settlement with more than 100 people who accused the FBI of grossly mishandling allegations of sexual assault against Nassar in 2015 and 2016, a critical time gap that allowed the sports doctor to continue to prey on victims before his arrest.

When combined with other settlements, $1billion now has been set aside by various organizations to compensate hundreds of women who said Nassar assaulted them under the guise of treatment for sports injuries.

Simone Biles publicly broke her silence in January 2018, revealing in a powerful tweet that she was one of Nassar's victims.

'It took me a long time to write that, probably a couple of days, because every time I would go to write, I would start balling, and I couldn't get through it,' she said.

Biles also noted that she was heartbroken over having to continue to train at the ranch, the former USA Gymnastics national training center where she and her teammates were abused by the disgraced doctor.

Sports.title: Bungling Andy Burnham is criticised for ANOTHER error in attempting to clarify his statement on Man City case after being called out for 'tone-deaf' response following 'concern' over losing Abu Dhabi owners
Sports.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has received further backlash after Number 10 attempted to clarify his comments around the financial case surrounding Manchester City. Burnham's claim that he would be 'really concerned' if Manchester City's owners were to sell the club after it was found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial regulations has been hit by widespread criticism. The Prime Minister made the comments following confirmation from the league that Man City had been found to have created a slew of 'sham' deals and contracts which misled the Premier League over £900million-plus in sponsorship deals over a nine-year period. 'As the Prime Minister made clear, the initial judgement is serious and there can't be any suggestion that anyone is above the rules,' a spokesperson said on Thursday. 'He also stressed that it is an ongoing independent process. It is essential that it is allowed to run its course and the outcome respected. 'If wrongdoing is established, those responsible should face the appropriate consequences.' Football fans, though, haven't taken kindly to the latest message. 'Wrongdoing has already been established,' one fan posted on X. 'Get them gone.' Another shared: 'This is an equally bad statement. Wrongdoing has already been established.' A third posted: 'Burnham is a joke. We all heard what he said. He's backtracking, not clarifying.' The end of the statement was later changed to: 'Wherever wrongdoing is established...' Andy Burnham (with Man City chairman Khaldoon Al-Mubarak in 2019) has been criticised for comments made on his 'concern' that the club's ownership might sell

Your browser does not support iframes.

The Premier League's chief executive Richard Masters stated that the club had 'systematically broken' the rules for nearly a decade and called the decision by the Independent Commission who heard the case 'the most significant in Premier League history'. Since confirmation of the decision broke on Tuesday evening, there have been calls for Man City to face relegation, fines, and even expulsion from the top flight, as well as arguments that the Abu Dhabi ownership group should move on – but former mayor of Greater Manchester Burnham took a more hesitant tone and lingered on the investment they had made into both the club and the city. Those on social media were quick to suggest that Burnham's comments could likely interfere with the process of both Man City's appeal and potential future sanctions if the charges are upheld. One fan posted: 'It was a confusing and, at best, tone-deaf intervention. Coming from a skilled operator, it was quite jarring.' Stan Collymore suggested that Burnham's 'concern' was 'tone deaf', highlighting the 'clunky' comments as an example of the power of sports-washing. 'For a PM, the day after a judgement by a respected panel to say 'we can't afford to lose City Group, they've put a lot into Manchester' is missing the point so widely that he's now going to be tagged as taking a side or grossly naïve,' he wrote in a lengthy post on X. 'Neither things people will readily vote for.' Rio Ferdinand added that he thought Burnham was 'on the back foot referencing Manchester City', but other commenters on the site were more critical. 'This is political interference,' one wrote. 'Already stating that he sees them as a positive influence and not wanting them gone. Unacceptable interference by influencing the (government's Football) Regulator.' Another added: 'Absolutely disgusting statement from the PM. He's basically saying you can cheat the system all you want if you pay enough. Just shows what sort of morals he really has'. Green Party deputy leader Mothin Ali also weighed in, saying: 'Andy Burnham's comments are staggering, just one day after saying people should come before profit, he sides with big money over the integrity of a sport that belongs to the people. 'It's a shame the prime minister appears to agree there should be one rule for the rich and one for everyone else.' Conservative MP Louie French, who serves as shadow minister for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport warned: 'Burnham's clumsy comments haven't just undermined the ongoing legal process and Premier League. He's left the IFR Chief, who is a Labour donor and will determine the fit and proper owner test, exposed to future legal challenges, as we warned would happen.' Burnham has received backlash for his comments as a statement trying to clarify what he said was released Burnham's comments did attract praise from one corner of social media, with Man City supporter and Oasis frontman Liam Gallagher writing: 'There's only 1 ANDY BURNHAM.' Burnham, whose mayoral tenure in Greater Manchester began three years after the 2014 deal struck between Manchester Council and the Abu Dhabi United Group worth £1billion promising a regeneration of city centre districts New Islington and Ancoats, had stressed in his remarks that he was unable to 'intervene' in the ongoing case. Speaking at the home of his side Everton at the Hill Dickinson Stadium, he said: 'I would be really concerned to lose (Man City's Abu Dhabi owners). 'They've been such a huge partner in the building of modern Manchester and obviously the building of Manchester City into the global force that it is. 'I can't intervene more in the process. It would be wrong for me to do that. It would be wrong, I think, to jump to a conclusion before having really studied all of the detail, but obviously it's ongoing, and because it's still contested by Manchester City, then I think it's right that I don't say much more.' 'I do actually thank the City Football Group and the wider ownership for the money that they didn't just put into the Etihad (Stadium) and the campus around it but also into the city.' In 2023, when charges were first brought against Man City, Abu Dhabi warned the United Kingdom that a negative outcome might damage relations with the country. Man City have until October 2 to appeal the verdict, and Evertonian Burnham added that he did not want to assume guilt, as some had done in the wake of the Toffees' own sanctions in 2023. 'Everton was in this position a few years ago and you might remember that I fought for Everton in that situation because I still hold the view very firmly that they weren't fairly treated in that process,' he continued. 'I remember people proclaiming Everton guilty at the time and with hindsight I think more people would say that wasn't fair, the way that was handled. 'So it would be wrong of me to leap to one side given the experience that I'd had before becoming prime minister.' Everton had fallen foul of the Premier League's financial regulations and were charged and deducted ten points, later reduced to six on appeal. But this was the scenario Man City seem to have been looking to avoid during the 2009-18 period scrutinised by the Independent Commission. David Kogan, chairman of the Independent Football Regulator (IFR), stated that he had the powers to 'assess the suitability of owners, directors and executive' and that the body would look to use their powers to protect 'the sustainability, honesty and integrity of English football'. The IFR and the FA will assess the findings once the sanctioning and appeals process has been completed. Man City continue to deny any wrongdoing, with chief executive Ferran Soriano stating in a video shared with the club's staff that they were in possession of 'irrefutable evidence' of their innocence that could dispel the Premier League's 'conspiracy theory' on appeal.

Sports.title: Second Hull City star crashes on his way to training - in almost the EXACT same spot as team-mate who flipped his £160,000 Land Rover Defender three weeks ago
Sports.content:
A second Hull City player has crashed their car on the way to training, just three weeks after their team-mate Sorba Thomas flipped his vehicle. A Mercedes was pictured on its side on a residential road close to the Premier League club's training ground. The identity of the player remains unknown, but midfielder Lucas Gourna-Douath posed for a photograph with the car in question in an Instagram post on Wednesday. In a statement, the club said: 'Hull City is aware of images circulating on social media following a road traffic accident near the club’s training ground and can confirm that no one was harmed in the incident.' Humberside Police have confirmed emergency services responded to an incident and that no-one was injured. 'Officers and emergency services were called to reports of a single vehicle road traffic collision on Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham at around 8.30am this morning (Thursday, 1 October 2026). 'Thankfully, no one was injured as a result of the collision.' A second Hull City player has crashed their car close to the Premier League club's training ground The identity of the player remains unknown, but midfielder Lucas Gourna-Douath posed for a photograph with the car in question in an Instagram post on Wednesday

Your browser does not support iframes.

Gourna-Douath, who signed for the Tigers in a £3million move from RB Salzburg in the summer, had recently received the new vehicle. 'Another one! 2026 GLC 53 sourced for Lucas Gourna,' the post read. 'Thank you for your order.' The incident comes three weeks after Thomas flipped his Land Rover on the way to training. The 27-year-old walked away from the crash, which happened on Millhouse Woods Lane in Cottingham at around 8.30am. His vehicle, a grey Land Rover Defender with a personalised number plate, was pictured on its roof, with broken windows. Residents had looked on stunned at the crash on the narrow road, where locals say speeds typically only hit 15mph. Thomas escaped injury in the crash and came off the bench for Hull the following day in their 2-2 draw against Chelsea at Stamford Bridge.

Sports.title: Erling Haaland is SUING a Norwegian airline after they launched a World Cup advert with a plane sporting his ponytail haircut
Sports.content:
Erling Haaland is SUING a Norwegian airline after they launched a World Cup advert with a plane sporting his ponytail haircut

Manchester City forward Erling Haaland is suing a Norwegian airline for using a plane with his signature hairstyle in an advert.

Haaland, who cut his hair at the start of the season, became synonymous with his ponytail hair that he donned while scoring plenty of goals for both club and country.

Airline Norwegian Air Shuttle ASA used an image during the World Cup of a plane with Haaland's hair edited onto it, and the forward has failed to see the funny side of things.

The caption read: 'We've never felt more Norwegian.'

The post has since been deleted from the company's social media channels.

Haaland is now taking the company to court with allegations of a violation of the Marketing Act, and, on October 9, a meeting between the judge and lawyers before the main hearing will take place, according to Norwegian publication VG.

Erling Haaland is suing a Norwegian airline after they used his haircut for an 

Company spokesperson Catharina Solli said: 'We struggle to understand why we have been taken to court. Just like almost everyone else in Norway, we encouraged the national team during the summer.

'We did this by publishing a few things spontaneously, inspired by social media trends.

'It is unfortunate that this encouragement has been greeted by a lawsuit. But we hope to have a reasonable dialogue, in order that we can continue in the future to support our sporting heroes together.'

Haaland's lawyer Thomas Hagen, meanwhile, said: 'This case is about the illegal use by Norwegian of Haaland's distinguishing features to sell air tickets during the World Cup finals.'

Haaland scored seven goals as Norway made it to the quarter-finals in their first World Cup this century before losing to England.

Sports.title: Revealed: Cristiano Ronaldo could be slapped with a six-month BAN after walking out on Portugal - as the country's prime minister reveals talks with the 'betrayed' 41-year-old star
Sports.content:
Revealed: Cristiano Ronaldo could be slapped with a six-month BAN after walking out on Portugal - as the country's prime minister reveals talks with the 'betrayed' 41-year-old star

Cristiano Ronaldo could be facing a ban of up to six months from the Portugal national team after sensationally storming out of the team's training camp amid a row with manager Jorge Jesus.

The star, 41, landed in Madrid in the early hours of Thursday morning after flying from Copenhagen, where Portugal are due to face Denmark, on his private jet.

He had been seen leaving the Parken Stadium in the Danish capital on Wednesday after missing a third consecutive training session.

Ronaldo later confirmed in a statement on Instagram that he had left the team's camp because of comments made by Jesus in his press conference.

The Portugal boss said the captain would not start the Denmark clash, just days after sitting on the bench for the entirety of the 2-1 win in Norway, but insisted there was no issue between the two.

And reports in Portugal claim Ronaldo could be suspended from playing for his country for between one and six months if he is found to have 'abandoned' the team.

Cristiano Ronaldo (left) sensationally walked out on Portugal amid a dispute with his manager

The Portuguese Football Federation's disciplinary code states: 'Any player who, having been regularly called up, unjustifiably abandons or fails to appear for training, a match, or any activity of the national teams or related to the sporting representation of the FPF or Portugal, will be sanctioned with a suspension of one to six months.'

Ronaldo said: 'After the national team coach's press conference, and following a conversation with the President of the Portuguese Football Federation, I have decided to leave the national team training camp.

'In due time, I will tell all Portuguese people the truth about the reasons that led to my departure from the national team, to which I have always dedicated myself.

'Now is the time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my teammates.'

Ronaldo's decision to quit the Portuguese camp has sparked suggestions he may retire from international duty and has even prompted the intervention of the country's Prime Minister, Luís Montenegro.

Record reports Montenegro has discussed the issue with Ronaldo, as well as Jesus and Pedro Proenca, the head of the Portuguese FA.

It is unclear whether Montenegro was attempting to resolve a dispute described as an 'earthquake' in Portugal, or if he was merely wanting to be briefed.

Speaking before the Denmark game, Jesus insisted he had a 'completely' clear conscience amid the Ronaldo saga. 'It was a frantic few hours because we had two games,' he added.

'Now we have another one... Besides, I've been in football for many years and I know I didn't do anything to prevent the situation from continuing as before.'

Footage published by A Bola showed Jesus and Proenca being booed by a small group of fans who had gathered outside the team's hotel in Copenhagen before the team made the short journey to Parken Stadium.

Reports in Portugal claim the dispute in the national team camp has reached Prime Minister Luis Montenegro

Ronaldo's sister Elma has come out in support of her brother after his shock exit from the Portugal camp (Source: Elma_Official/Instagram)

Ronaldo's sister, Elma Aveiro, had earlier fanned the flames of controversy by claiming Portuguese people 'deserve mediocrity' because of their treatment of the country's record goalscorer.

'The national team deserved better structuring,' she wrote on Instagram. 'The Portuguese press deserved more competence and fewer guesses.

'As for the Portuguese... well, they don't deserve the best in anything. We are envious, contemptuous, ignorant, and we deserve to return to the mediocrity we always had in football before CR7. Thank you for everything CR7!'

Elma was not the only supporter from inside Ronaldo's camp to suggest that the five-time Ballon d'Or winner had been treated unfairly, with Spanish journalist Edu Aguirre - who is friends with the Al-Nassr superstar - claiming he had been 'betrayed' by Jesus.

'There was a meeting yesterday, Tuesday night,' he told Spanish programme El Chiringuito. 'A meeting between the Federation president, the coach, and Cristiano. Jorge Jesus apologized to Cristiano for the disregard shown in making him warm up for 30 minutes instead of playing him.

'And not only did he apologize privately, but he also told him he would apologize publicly, that he would publicly admit his mistake. That's Jorge Jesus's promise to Cristiano. And then he goes to the press conference and tells this many lies that nobody believes.

'That's why Cristiano explodes, because he feels betrayed. There's nothing more to it, it's really like that. Your coach comes to you privately: "Look, see, this is how it was, you understand me, okay, I didn't manage the situation well, we're in this together, I'm sorry. If there's a press conference, I'll clarify everything, I'll apologize, don't worry, everything will be fine, everything will be resolved." Then you go to the press conference 12 hours later and leave Cristiano still...

'Worse, you're acting tough, saying that you're the one in charge and that Cristiano is just another player. Go home and move on. That's why I say: betrayal.'

Ronaldo confirmed on Wednesday night that he had left the camp amid a row with Jorge Jesus

The captain confirmed he had withdrawn from the squad because of Jesus's comments

Ronaldo held talks with Jesus and Proenca on Wednesday morning, a meeting initially described as amicable.

But the rift between Ronaldo and his manager appeared to deepen after Jesus's press conference.

Jesus admitted Ronaldo had been 'angry' with him, with footage showing the captain walking off down the tunnel after sitting out the victory in Norway.

Jesus, who also worked with Ronaldo at Al-Nassr, said: 'There was no incident whatsoever.

'Any player - and I was a player myself - when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on, no-one is happy about that.

'Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It's nothing to make a fuss about.'

Jesus also suggested Goncalo Ramos would keep his place in the side ahead of Ronaldo for the Denmark match. 'If I need [Ronaldo], he'll come on,' he said. 'If I don't need him, he won't.'

Jesus had originally planned to bring on the veteran striker for a 30-minute cameo but then decided to leave him on the bench, which has seemingly sparked the feud.

It is an inauspicious start to the relationship between Jesus and Ronaldo, who opted not to retire from international duty after the World Cup.

Only a week ago, Ronaldo reiterated his commitment to the cause, saying: 'I had a conversation with our president, with our coach (about his future).

'I still believe that I'm able to help the national team to reach what they want, and will finish when I feel like I'm not doing anything here.

'I think I can give to the national team my support, not only through the goals, but also outside of football.

'This is a new young generation. But for me the basic point is to be able on the pitch to score the goals and to help the team win games.'

Ronaldo will turn 42 in February and has scored three goals in five games for Al-Nassr so far in the Saudi Pro League this season.

Sports.title: Ireland vs Austria match suddenly halted as furious supporters stage Israel protest
Sports.content:
Ireland vs Austria match suddenly halted as furious supporters stage Israel protest

Ireland's Nations League clash with Austria at the Aviva Stadium was disrupted twice by protest, with tennis balls bearing the Palestine flag thrown onto the pitch in the 20th minute

View 3 Images Security staff tackle a protestor wearing a Palestine flag (Image: Charles McQuillan, Getty Images)

Ireland's match with Austria was twice halted by protestors as demonstrators voiced their opposition to Israel, ahead of the nation's second Nations League match with the side this week. Supporters hurled tennis balls onto the pitch forcing tonight's to stop for a couple of minutes.

‌



‌



The incident took place in the 20th minute, when numerous balls bearing the Palestine flag were lobbed onto the playing surface. It is the second time in succession that a protest has utilised tennis balls at the Aviva Stadium following a friendly against Qatar in June.

‌



A second interruption occurred in the 36th minute when a supporter attempted to invade the pitch but was quickly intercepted by security. They also carried the Palestinian flag.

‌



Before kick-off, protestors gathered with the Stop the Game campaign outside the Aviva Stadium. The movement has been demanding that Ireland boycott the Nations League fixtures with Israel during this international break.

Ireland went ahead with the controversial match last weekend following a turbulent few days behind closed doors, with Gavin Bazunu eventually withdrawing from the squad, expressing his unease over the atrocities unfolding in Gaza.

‌



Despite tonight's demonstration and the widespread sentiment amongst a significant section of supporters, next Sunday's encounter with Israel looks set to proceed, with Heimir Hallgrímsson confirming earlier this week that it remained Ireland's plan to honour that fixture in Serbia.

"The FAI has said we are playing both games. That was our intention when we came into the camp and it is still our intention," said Hallgrimsson. "We are trying to focus on the football. It is already decided we will fulfil the games."

Hundreds of pubs in ireland refused to show the nation's first match with Israel and plan to do the same on Sunday. There have also be protests outside of the team's hotel in Dublin.

‌



View 3 Images Tennis balls with Palestine flags on them had to becollected by security staff (Image: Charles McQuillan/Getty Images)

‌



While they did not boycott the first clash, aside from Bazunu, Ireland's players did not shake hands and looked down during their opponents' national anthem.

Ireland's actions angered Israel captain and West Ham winger Manor Solomon. "They said nonsense during the game, I don't want to talk about them," he said following the match.

"If I say what I think about them, I'll probably be banned for a few games so I don't want to say. Of course they hate us and we don't like them.

Article continues below

"I'm already looking forward to the next game against them, it's going to be completely different. What they did with the anthem? I'm not interested in them, we have a country that is ten times better than theirs, stronger, an amazing country with amazing people. (They) can play all their tricks. We are Israelis and love the country. And that will always be the case."
