World.content:
GERMISTON - A male truck driver survived an accident after the truck he was driving jackknifed and caught fire.

The incident happened at 12pm on Thursday at the N3 South and N12 West split, Elands Interchange in Germiston.

He has since been transported to a nearby medical facility in Alberton.

READ | Culpable homicide case opened after deadly N1 crash

According to the City of Ekurhuleni Disaster and Emergency Management Service spokesperson, William Ntladi, the driver, who was the only person in the truck, managed to escape the burning truck with minor burn and trauma injuries.

Ntladi said once firefighters were alerted of the incident, they rushed to the scene to intervene.

“A scene and risk assessment was conducted. N12 freeway westbound: all three lanes had to be temporarily closed for the duration of the rescue and fire ground operations. N3 freeway southbound, three of the four lanes had to be temporarily closed for traffic as well,” he added.

Ntladi said he anticipates that the closure of both freeways will last until late in the afternoon.

World.title: From prison to palaces: Life, time and 'crimes' of Mr Moneybags
World.content:
Zimbabwean businessman Wicknell Munodaani Chivayo and President William Ruto at State House, Nairobi. [File, Standard]

In life, he was flamboyant and portrayed a larger than life image. In death, an air of mystery surrounds the opulence he was always associated with. Wicknell Munodaani Chivayo, the Zimbabwean millionaire tenderpreneur who died in a helicopter crash on Wednesday, aged 43, built a public persona on luxury cars, presidential handshakes and billion-dollar state contracts.

The source of his riches has always been a debate in Zimbabwe and abroad. Behind the glitzy social media posts and the headline grabbing donations of vehicles lies a far darker narrative, a chronicle of fraud, money laundering and a seemingly charmed existence in the face of serious criminal allegations spanning more than two decades. The secrets of probably the most controversial wheeler-deeler in the continent run deep.

World.title: Ruto downplays rivalry over oil refinery in East Africa
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Former Nigeria President Olesugun Obasanjo, Ali Dangote, President William Ruto and Uganda President Yoweri Museveni during launch of the Lamu Refinery on September 30, 2026. [PCS]

President William Ruto has played down suggestions of rivalry between Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania over competing refinery projects, saying East Africa’s growing demand for petroleum products can support several facilities across the region.

Speaking during a media interview at State House Mombasa, Ruto said Kenya had no objection to Uganda and Tanzania pursuing their own refinery projects, arguing that the different facilities could complement rather than compete with one another.

“There is no bad blood at all. There is no problem,” Ruto said.

His remarks came a day after he presided over the groundbreaking of the Lamu refinery project, which the government is positioning as a major component of a wider industrial complex on the Kenyan coast.

Ruto said he had discussed Uganda’s plans with President Yoweri Museveni and agreed that Kampala could proceed with a smaller refinery without threatening Kenya’s investment in Lamu.

He said Kenya would even be prepared to buy petroleum products from Uganda if they could reach the Kenyan market at competitive prices.

“If it is manufactured there in Uganda and the oil from that place is near Busia, and it can reach Busia at a lower price, we will buy oil from anywhere and bring it to Busia,” Ruto said.

The President argued that the size of the regional petroleum market meant there was room for more than one refinery.

“This one in Lamu cannot serve all of us; it will be necessary to expand,” he said, adding that East Africa had “enough opportunity” for multiple facilities.

Ruto also extended the same approach to Tanzania, saying Kenya could participate in a refinery project in Tanga if it is eventually developed.

“Even if the one in Tanga is built, we as Kenya will go and buy some shares there. There is no problem,” he said.

The comments point to a regional energy market in which petroleum products could move across borders depending on availability, transport costs and prices. Rather than treating refinery projects as competing national investments, Ruto said the facilities could strengthen economic cooperation within the East African Community.

The President said the Lamu refinery would also address some of the challenges Kenya faces from dependence on imported refined petroleum products.

“Lamu will give us an opportunity to have fuel without the fluctuations that we have now,” he said.

He linked the proposed refinery to the need to reduce Kenya’s exposure to international oil price shocks, disruptions caused by instability in oil-producing regions and costs associated with transporting petroleum products over long distances.

Ruto said local refining could reduce expenses related to insurance and transportation while providing Kenya with greater access to locally processed fuel.

However, he said the larger economic opportunity would extend beyond the refinery itself. The government plans to develop industries around the facility, including petrochemical, chemical and plastics manufacturing.

The refinery could also provide raw materials for industries producing fertiliser and bitumen, potentially reducing reliance on imports of some petroleum-based products.

The broader development is expected to create opportunities for employment, investment and trade while strengthening Lamu’s position as an industrial and logistics centre.

Ruto said Kenya’s policy would be guided by competitiveness, allowing businesses and consumers to obtain petroleum products from whichever regional facility can supply them efficiently and at favourable prices.

The President maintained that Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania therefore did not need to view their refinery plans through the lens of rivalry.

Instead, he said, multiple facilities could create a larger and more integrated petroleum market capable of serving the needs of East Africa.

World.title: Outrage as KDF officers detain human rights team along Malindi-Lamu highway
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Activists clashed with police at a Gamba roadblock after being stopped en route to Lamu. [Vocal Africa]

Six members of Muslims for Human Rights (MUHURI), including five staff and a board member, were detained by Kenya Defence Forces (KDF) officers along the Malindi-Lamu highway, prompting condemnation from human rights organisations.

The incident occurred on Monday as the team travelled from Lamu to Mombasa after a field mission. The officers reportedly intercepted them between Gamba and Minjila, detained them for about two hours, then released them.

The Kenya Human Rights Commission (KHRC) and MUHURI said the officers covered their faces and refused to identify themselves when the human rights team challenged them.

The five staff members were identified as Francis Auma, Abdulrahman Mwanga, Fredrick Okado, Lathan Yusuf and Mohamed Abdla, while the board member was identified as Khelef Khalifa.

In a joint statement, the two organisations said the officers' actions violated a High Court ruling by Justice Bahati Mwamuye requiring security personnel to wear clearly visible name tags or identifiable service numbers on their uniforms.

The ruling also prohibits security officers from wearing hoods, balaclavas or face masks to conceal their identities.

"We call on the KDF and other security agencies to comply with the court order. Officers who violate the directive should be held accountable and face legal consequences," the joint statement read in part.

The organisations also demanded immediate compliance with a recent court order lifting the dusk-to-dawn curfew that had been imposed for more than a decade along the Minjila-Lamu highway.

They argued that the curfew had created conditions for arbitrary stops, harassment and detention of travellers using the route, citing the detention of the MUHURI team as an example.

The organisations urged security agencies to respect court orders and protect the rights of travellers using the highway.

However, a senior Anti-Terror Police officer aware of the incident told The Standard that the officers from the Border Police Unit (BPU) manning such roadblocks and tactical borders conceal their faces to protect their identities.

"In high-risk areas prone to insurgent or terrorist retaliation, including Kanyoyo in Kitui heading to Garissa, Moyale and Lamu, anonymity is framed as a matter of personal and operational survival," she stated.

World.title: Kalonzo signals at working with Ruto if 2027 poll is free and fair
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County on September 27, 2026. [Clinton Ambujo, Standard]

Wiper Patriotic Front leader Kalonzo Musyoka has signalled that the Opposition could accept the outcome of the 2027 General Election and consider working with President William Ruto if he wins through a free and fair contest.

Speaking at St Michael and All Angels ACK Cathedral in Bondo, Siaya County, Kalonzo said the political class must commit itself to democratic competition and be prepared to accept the verdict of voters.

“If you beat us, we will have to consider if you have behaved yourself, and if we beat you, we have to look at all these things,” he said.

The Wiper leader also called for stronger democratic institutions, warning against political confrontation that could deepen divisions in the country.

“We have a nation here. We have to make this country truly democratic. I do not think we have a shortcut,” he said.

Kalonzo used the church service to make a broader appeal for a united and effective Opposition, saying political leaders had a responsibility to work together in the national interest.

“Kenya needs a functional official opposition; one that is united and does not thrive on disunity. As leaders, we have a responsibility to work together and play our part in fixing this nation,” he said.

He said he had remained in the Opposition even when some political allies moved into government.

“I have stood in the opposition all these years. Even when others joined government, my brother Eugene Wamalwa and I remained steadfast, and we will continue to stand firm,” he said.

Kalonzo also turned his attention to Parliament, claiming that the National Assembly had been “captured” and challenging lawmakers in both Houses to exercise their constitutional responsibilities.

“The National Assembly has been captured. Let this message reach every leader in the National Assembly and the Senate: you have the power to change things, not just to complain later,” he said.

He urged legislators to defend the interests of the people who elected them and to put the country ahead of political considerations.

The former Vice President also defended retired President Uhuru Kenyatta against claims that he is financing the Opposition ahead of the 2027 contest.

Kalonzo argued that presidential campaigns have historically relied on networks of political allies and supporters rather than family resources alone.

“But here we are saying, please let Uhuru rest; he is a retired President. Stop saying he is our financier,” he said.

Kalonzo cited previous presidential campaigns involving Uhuru, former President Mwai Kibaki and Raila Odinga, arguing that major political campaigns require support from friends and associates.

“Even when Uhuru was running for President, or Kibaki and even Raila, no family has enough resources to support a presidential campaign. It is friends who support you,” he said.

He warned that Kenya was at a delicate political moment and urged leaders to avoid actions that could deepen instability.

“We should not allow the country to get to a worse situation than where it is. We are on the edge of a cliff; the country is at a crossroads,” he said.

World.title: ODM delegates reject Sakaja using the party for gubernatorial bid
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Nairobi ODM chairman George Aladwa addressing the media over the upcoming ODM nominations in Nairobi. [Collins Oduor, Standard]

Nairobi ODM delegates have resolved to reject and lobby against attempts by some people in President William Ruto's broad-based government to give Nairobi Governor Johnson Sakaja the ODM ticket in the 2027 gubernatorial race.

Party members, delegates and branch chairpersons met in Makadara, where they agreed that ODM be allowed to field their own candidates instead of the party allowing UDA leaders to vie on the party ticket.

They also resolved to back Makadara MP George Aladwa. With Tutam songs renting the air during the meeting, they also agreed to back President Ruto's re-election.

"Aladwa should be the party's candidate for Nairobi governor, and every candidate should seek the seat through their own political party," said an agitated delegate from Kasarani.

They insisted ODM should not allow an outsider to join the party and use its ticket to contest for the gubernatorial seat, arguing that the ODM ticket should be reserved for a candidate who enjoys the support of its members.

"We will not allow someone from another party to come and vie using ODM while we have our own members. As a party our only candidate is Aladwa," said delegate chairs.

They added that their position follows a series of meetings held across all 17 constituencies in Nairobi, with Makadara being the final constituency to hold its meeting.

They further argued that the Nairobi gubernatorial seat requires a leader with experience and leadership skills, warning ODM members against supporting candidates they believe lack the necessary political and leadership experience.

They also sustained their criticism towards former president Uhuru, alleging that he is undermining the party and dividing it, and they will not allow it.

George Aladwa backed the ODM members' position, saying every politician seeking elective office should do so through their own political party.

The delegates maintained that ODM should protect its identity and ticket, insisting that candidates from outside the party should not be allowed to use the ODM ticket to pursue elective positions when active and loyal members are sidelined.

The delegates are calling on ODM to ensure that the nomination process is free, fair and transparent, giving party members an opportunity to choose the candidate they want to represent them.

World.title: Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya's first commercial drilling
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Oil rig arrives in Mombasa ahead of Kenya’s first commercial drilling. [Courtes]

Kenya has moved closer to commercial oil production after a 1,500 horsepower drilling rig arrived at the Port of Mombasa ahead of its deployment to the South Lokichar Basin in Turkana County.

The GW70 rig, leased by Gulf Energy E&P BV from Great Wall Drilling Company, docked at Kilindini Port on Friday aboard MV Transit Sedanka after sailing from Duqm Port in Oman.

It is expected to be transported to Turkana, where drilling is scheduled to begin on November 1.

“All workstreams at Gulf Energy E&P BV SEZ are running to a tight project management schedule, and the project remains on course for First Oil production in December 2026,” Gulf Energy Chief Executive Officer Paul Limoh said.

The arrival marks a step in the commercial development of the South Lokichar Basin, more than a decade after oil was first discovered in Turkana in 2012.

The first phase of the project is expected to produce about 20,000 barrels of crude oil per day, with output projected to rise to 50,000 barrels per day in the second phase.

The Energy and Petroleum Regulatory Authority (EPRA) says Kenya is targeting first oil in December 2026, while the first crude exports through the Port of Mombasa are expected in the first quarter of 2027.

The GW70 will undergo commissioning and acceptance checks before drilling begins. Gulf Energy has contracted Baker Hughes for integrated well services and SLB to provide an early production facility for the first phase.

World.title: Two more suspects arrested over lawyer Kyalo Mbobu murder
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads.

Detectives have arrested two more suspects in connection with the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu, as an intelligence-led operation targeting people linked to the September 9, 2025 murder intensifies.

The two boda boda riders Nicholas Lemiso Naula and Noah Kipkirui Langat were arrested in Nairobi’s Central Business District, following sustained efforts by detectives to trace individuals suspected to have been involved in the killing.

According to the Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI), Lemiso is a boda boda rider who allegedly ferried the main suspect, Police Constable Julius Cheruiyot, to and from the scene of the murder, while Langat was arrested over alleged surveillance on Mbobu before his killing.

"With three suspects now in custody, detectives are intensifying the hunt for other persons suspected to have played a role in the meticulously planned killing," DCI stated.

His arrest comes shortly after detectives arrested Cheruiyot in connection with the killing.

“The dragnet over the fatal shooting of lawyer Kyalo Mbobu has widened, with detectives arresting a second suspect as an intelligence-led operation targeting persons linked to the murder intensifies,” DCI said.

The two suspects are currently in custody undergoing processing as detectives pursue additional leads and seek to identify and arrest other people who may have been involved. The DCI said the operation remains active as investigators work to establish the circumstances surrounding Mbobu’s murder.

“The DCI is leaving no stone unturned in its efforts to unravel the full circumstances surrounding Lawyer Mbobu’s murder and bring all those responsible to justice,” the agency said.

World.title: KRA seizes 53,000 under-declared smartphones at Eldoret Airport
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

The consignment was intercepted by KRA enforcement teams following an intelligence report.

Kenya Revenue Authority (KRA) has seized a consignment containing 53,000 under-declared smartphones at Eldoret International Airport, averting a potential tax loss of Sh21.5 million.

KRA enforcement teams intercepted the consignment after an intelligence report indicated it contained undeclared mobile phones and other high-end electronic goods.

The cargo, which had been declared under five Customs entries, was part of consolidated shipments that also included shoes, clothing, automotive spare parts, household goods, electronic accessories and other assorted items.

KRA said an initial declaration listed only 3,000 smartphones. However, verification established 55,607 ordinary smartphones, alongside 309 undeclared high-end smartphones.

The high-end devices included Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra, Samsung Galaxy Z Fold and Apple iPhone 17 Pro Max models.

“The consignment therefore reflects both under-declaration and non-declaration of dutiable goods,” KRA said in a statement issued on Wednesday.

The tax authority said the verification exercise was conducted to establish whether all mobile phones contained in the consignment had been properly declared.

KRA said the alleged tax evasion contravenes Section 203 of the East African Community Customs Management Act (EACCMA), 2004.

The law provides that a person who makes a false or incorrect Customs entry, or knowingly participates in the fraudulent evasion of duty, commits an offence.

“A person who, in any matter relating to Customs, makes any entry which is false or incorrect in any particular, or in any way is knowingly concerned in any fraudulent evasion of the payment of any duty, commits an offence,” KRA said, citing the law.

According to the authority, a person convicted under the provision is liable to imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years or a fine of up to US$10,000.

KRA said it was intensifying efforts to uncover tax evasion schemes to improve revenue compliance and ensure adherence to tax laws and procedures.

“KRA is actively engaged in unearthing tax evasion schemes to boost tax revenue compliance as well as adherence to tax laws and procedures, hence ensuring fair trade is maintained within the market,” the authority said.

The authority also appealed to members of the public, taxpayers and businesses with information on individuals, companies or networks involved in the generation, sale, purchase or use of fictitious VAT invoices to report them.

KRA said information provided would be treated confidentially and the identity of informants kept anonymous.

World.title: Manchester City has been found ‘cheating on an industrial scale.’ What comes next?
World.content:
It’s one of the most extraordinary and monumental moments in the history of the Premier League – a story that has threatened and continues to endanger the very integrity of soccer in England.

Manchester City, one of the most successful teams in the world in recent years, has been found guilty of systematically cheating – financially doping its way to dominance for the best part of a decade.

Ever since this issue sprung into public consciousness in 2018 through a series of leaked emails, this saga has rumbled on in the background. But now, the lid has been blown off, and the outcome could be devastating for the club.

On Tuesday, the Premier League – the domestic competition in which City plays – finally broke its silence with a blistering statement that revealed the outcome of an independent commission.

It said the club was guilty of seriously breaching the league’s financial rules “well over 100 individual” times between 2009 and 2018 through a series of “sham” contracts and commercial agreements that helped conceal “the true state of its finances” by disguising what was essentially secret funding from its UAE ownership.

The league also said the club overstated its income by roughly $1.18 billion (£900 million) and understated its expenses by tens of millions, while also trying to cover up its efforts during the investigation.

Manchester City, though, says it has “irrefutable evidence” that proves its innocence and will appeal the verdict.

The club’s primary sponsor Etihad Airways – after which the team’s stadium is named – has also defended City and its relationship, threatening legal action against the Premier League.

Despite not being named in the report, some of which is redacted, Etihad Airways told CNN Sports that the lack of “clarity and transparency, together with the selective disclosure of information, has created damaging implications for Etihad.”

It added: “Etihad will seek the relevant legal counsel on the options and recourse available to protect its interests.”

So, should City’s appeal be unsuccessful and the club is eventually nailed to rights, just how devastating could the punishment be and what will that mean on and off the pitch?

Manchester City’s dominance

To understand the severity of this matter, it’s important to understand the context around the club.

In 2008, Manchester City was bought by Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan through the Abu Dhabi United Group.

What is going to happen to Manchester City following the Premier League’s scathing statement Tuesday? Oli Scarff/AFP/Getty Images

Under the new regime, the club saw a total overhaul. Billions were spent on upgrading the team’s stadium, training complex and, more importantly, playing squad. Some of the world’s best soccer stars and managers suddenly started signing for a club that had been languishing in mediocrity for some time.

The result was City becoming one of the most potent forces in the sport, winning three Premier League titles, three League Cups and one FA Cup during the period covered by the charges.

The new era saw history made, creating some of the most iconic moments the league has ever seen and giving its fans memories that would last a lifetime.

That period also provided the foundations for where City currently sits within the top echelons of world soccer – having won the UEFA Champions League back in 2023 and winning four consecutive Premier Leagues from 2021 to 2024.

City fans will be hoping the club avoids some of the worst sanctions that are being discussed as possibilities by social media and pundits. Alex Livesey/Getty Images

Now, though, the independent panel says it was all done illegally – a “sham,” as it said eight times in its redacted findings.

And it’s not as though this is the first time that City has faced allegations of financial misconduct. In 2020, the club was initially banned from European soccer for two seasons for “serious breaches” of financial regulations by continental governing body UEFA. The ban was later overturned by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), which also reduced the accompanying $34 million fine to $11.3 million, ruling that City had failed to cooperate with UEFA.

But the result of this latest case with the Premier League could seriously damage the club going forward.

Possible punishments

According to the official league handbook, potential punishments could include a hefty points deduction, an unlimited fine, or even expulsion from the league entirely.

A case of this size has no precedent. Yes, clubs have fallen foul of slightly breaking Premier League rules in the past and have received points deductions as a result.

But as former England international and current pundit Ian Wright says, this is “cheating on an industrial scale.”

“It’s quite surreal seeing it written down like that,” he said on ITV. “I feel unprecedented punishment is required here.”

That punishment could be unlimited. That points deduction, for example, could be so big that it essentially relegates City into the Championship – the second tier of English soccer – or, as has been suggested by English media and pundits, spread out over multiple years to severely hamstring the club’s efforts to qualify for anything notable for the foreseeable future.

City’s triumphs after the period which covers the charges are tainted by the specter of what the independent commission called a “sham.” Michael Regan/Getty Images

There has also been talk that the club should be stripped of all the titles and trophies it won during the period in question. And while that makes sense on the surface, it also opens up another can of worms.

If City has its three league titles taken away from it, what happens to the teams that finished second that year? If those runners-up are awarded the league title, do they then deserve the prize money that would have come with it?

Also, what happens to all the teams that dropped points to City during those nine years? City’s results would have contributed to teams being relegated from the top division, or missing out on lucrative Champions League places. Could there be a scenario where every club during that period seeks compensation through legal actions for lost earnings and revenue? That process would surely take years.

And while this is a logistical headache for people in suits and boardrooms, the length of this case continues to undermine what’s happening on the pitch.

Already, despite the upcoming appeal, that nine-year period of the league now comes with an asterisk. All those titles won, goals scored and memories made have been cast in shadow for the players and fans who lived them.

“(City) knew it would hurt a lot of people, but they still done it,” former Manchester United and Ireland star and current pundit Roy Keane told ITV. “If I was a player, I would 100% be sticking those medals in the bin. It’s cheating.”

It’s a similar sentiment felt by former Liverpool player Jamie Carragher who told Sky Sports that he’d be “furious” if he was a City player from that time.

“I actually feel for the Man City players. I mean, as a team, what they’ve done is wrong. The Premier League have called it a sham five times in this statement.

“In terms of individual players, some of them were coming out to bat for the club and, you know as they would, that’s normal right now, and it must be very difficult for them to see what’s going on right now.

What’s next?

All of this has also been incredibly damaging for the Premier League’s reputation.

Ultimately, the ideal situation for the league would have been City being found innocent because things could have returned back to normal relatively quickly – even if opposition fans would have objected. It’s telling, then, that the league’s statement is so strong. It suggests just how much cheating and blatant disregard for the rules it thinks has gone on behind closed doors.

The punishment to be handed down by the independent commission will be decided sometime in the future. Mike Morese/MI News/NurPhoto/Getty Images

What happens next is unclear. City will appeal, we know that, and the Premier League is keen to close this matter as soon as possible and decide on a punishment fitting for the charges.

But the longer City digs its heels in, the more damaging this will get for everyone involved.

The club shows no signs of backing down, though, with CEO Ferran Soriano calling the case a “Premier League conspiracy theory” in an internal video sent to club staff after the verdict was announced.

Without knowing the outcome or City’s possible punishment – which the league has said will come at a later date by the independent commission – the pure essence of the Premier League is lost. If all of City’s results are to be scrapped this season, next season, or in four seasons to come, then whatever happens in the meantime is somewhat meaningless. The all-or-nothing nature of sports gets muddled with asterisks and different permutations.

It’s a sad state of affairs that could genuinely take weeks, months or even years to conclude, given City is showing no signs of backing down and can afford, ironically, the best legal team in the world.

Manchester City will next play on October 11 against Liverpool – one of the teams that missed out on winning a league title during the period of the charges.

Current City manager Enzo Maresca will have to try focus his plethora of star players – such as striker Erling Haaland – after what must have been a turbulent week for everyone involved at the club.

All of a sudden, their futures are very uncertain.

World.title: What have we learned about Pope Leo during his visit to France
World.content:
Metz, France — France may have a highly secularized culture, but it has given France may have a highly secularized culture, but it has given Pope Leo XIV a superstar welcome.

In Paris, around 800,000 lined the Champs-Élysées avenue, some waving Vatican or French flags while others climbed trees or stood on each other’s shoulders to get a glimpse of the popemobile.

In Lourdes, a holy site in southern France, around 150,000 attended an open-air papal Mass, according to Vatican estimates which dwarf the numbers of faithful who turned out for the last papal visit in 2008.

During the four-day visit, Leo appeared comfortable and relaxed, delivering most of his speeches and reflections in French, as the Chicago-born pontiff sought to tackle several themes during the trip.

A strong focus of Leo’s has been on trying to revitalize faith in a traditional European Catholic heartland as well as on addressing the clerical sexual abuse scandal and big political topics such as artificial intelligence. He’s also offered some more personal, unscripted remarks, helping to shape a clearer picture of himself.

He wants Europe to draw on its Christian roots

While his predecessor never made official visits to the major Catholic European countries of France and Spain, Pope Leo has traveled to both within the first year and a half since his election.

France is sometimes described as the “eldest daughter of the church” because of its deep Catholic roots, but it’s also faced a long-term trend of declining church attendance with estimates of just 5-8% of the population heading to the pews each week.

French bishops have more recently reported some good news though: a surprising rise in new church entrants after around 8,200 adolescents and 13,200 adults were baptized in 2026. That’s a 20% increase on the year prior, with the church also saying 42% of the adults seeking baptism are aged 18-25, a reflection of a trend showing Gen Z’s openness to religious faith.

It’s something Pope Leo will have noted at the Stade de France when 80,000 young people packed the venue for a jubilant – and loud – prayer vigil. It was similar to when the pontiff visited Spain in June.

Pope Leo XIV on stage next to French bishop Etienne Guillet during a prayer vigil with young people at the Stade de France on Friday. Aurore Marechal/Getty Images

“There is a quest for meaning. People need and are in search of meaning and answers to the big existential question,” Rev. Benoît Pouzin, a priest in southwest France involved in youth ministry, told CNN.

France has a strict separation between church and state, so each papal visit needs to be carefully navigated. But in a surprising twist, Leo’s Mass in Paris was celebrated on the Place de la Concorde, a site deeply linked to the secular Republic as it’s where the last king of France, Louis XVI and Marie-Antoinette were guillotined. The separation of the church started with the fall of the monarchy during the French Revolution.

In another unusual move later in the trip, President Emmanuel Macron also attended a papal Mass in Metz, a city in the northeast, despite criticism in 2023 for doing the same during Pope Francis’ visit.

Pope isn’t panicking over AI, but warns of its power

Many among the crowds also pointed to Leo’s role as the other major US leader on the world stage. It’s hard not to see him as a counterweight to President Donald Trump. In contrast to the Trump administration, the pope has called for stronger guardrails around the development of artificial intelligence, warning against a “paradise of machines” while in Paris.

Pope Leo said he is taking the warnings about Artificial Intelligence’s threat to humanity seriously, and said it is irresponsible for people to sit back and dismiss the risks of AI.

Trump has dismissed the warnings about AI as a “hoax” which he made during a surprise phone call with Jensen Huang, the CEO of chipmaker Nvidia, at a summit in Los Angeles.

“I don’t think that that is fake news – as some have said – to try and pause,” Leo XIV said on board the papal plane from Metz to Rome.

Leo, who has expressed a keen interest in artificial intelligence since the start of his papacy, said that he found it “interesting” that Huang had unveiled a new tool to prevent AI agents from operating out of human control.

“He’s the same one, however, that says there should be no limits placed and no government regulation,” the Pope said.

The pope devoted his first major theological document to AI earlier this year, warning about the use of AI in warfare and calling for stronger ethical foundation to the development of the technology.

The pope explained that the Vatican had established its own AI commission to understand how to use it, along with the risks and benefits, and that “we need to continue to invite political leaders, the leaders of AI” so they can “look at what is happening already and what could be down the road.”

He explained: “We are trying to continue to promote dialog, study, investigation, to find ways to make sure that AI does not get to a point where it could destroy humanity.”

“If someone were to ask me, am I in panic mode? No, I’m not, I sleep at night” the pope said, but added: “I do think that the concerns raised by many of the experts, specialists in AI, should be taken seriously.”

“To simply say, oh, it’s not going to happen and close our eyes to it, I think, is probably not the most responsible way to go about that,” Leo said.

Concern over the far right and Christianity

The pope, who spoke out against the US war in Iran, also wants a more united Europe, a stronger European Union and stronger international cooperation. “Today, relations between individuals and states are becoming increasingly uncivilized,” the pope said in Metz on Monday. “The value of keeping one’s word is dismissed; instead, people boast of lies and deceit.”

The pope’s speech also praised one of the founders of the European Union, Robert Schuman, for whom there is an ongoing formal cause to make a saint.

Pope Leo XIV has warned against the use of Christianity by far-right political groups, while calling on the church to be active in seeking to prevent extremism. Speaking on board the papal plane, he said that “the combination of these far-right points of view with a certain kind of religion” cannot be considered an “authentic expression of Christianity.”

The pope’s comments came in response to a question about the rise of extremist parties in Germany as he flew back from making a major speech on European Unity at the French-German border.

“We go back to the values of the Gospel [Christian teaching], which are not about hatred and division, but they’re about understanding and compassion,” the pope said.

Pope Leo XIV delivers a speech during a meeting at the Robert Schuman Conference Center in Metz on Monday. Benoit Tessier/AFP/Getty Images

The American pontiff also responded to Trump’s White House media ban, which includes CNN and other outlets. In answer to a question from CNN, he said he was “very happy that, here, you are all welcome and good coverage, I think, is very important and that we have it all the way around, for everyone.” The response was classic Leo: signaling his support for the press but not wishing to create an unnecessary dispute with the president.

The American pope’s in-flight interactions with journalists were rare, unscripted moments, with his answers often revealing more about his personality. On the flight from Rome to Paris, the pope was asked if he had anything to do with a miraculous recent Chicago White Sox victory, his beloved baseball team. “No comment,” he said before adding with a smile, “Great things happen in Chicago.”

He also recalled childhood memories of watching Fulton Sheen, the American archbishop and broadcaster who was recently declared “blessed,” one step ahead of sainthood, and revealed he’d been practicing his French but was no longer using the Duolingo language app. “It’s fake news!” he said about recent reports. Leo has in the past been spotted using Duolingo to learn German.

Leo isn’t simply vocal about challenges of his homeland. He also voiced concern over assisted dying with France recently approving legislation granting the right to the incurably ill, which is strongly opposed by the Catholic Church. Leo spoke on the subject several times during his visit – most clearly in the “miracle shrine” town of Lourdes, known for drawing many sick and terminally ill pilgrims to its shrine.

A willingness to tackle church scandal

Workers are fitting the fixings that will hold in place the tarpaulins covering allegedly abusive priest Marko Rupnik’s mosaics on the façade of the Basilica of the Rosary ahead of Pope Leo XIV s visit to the shrine at Lourdes. Jean-Christophe Chartre/Hans Lucas/AFP/Getty Images

The pope must, however, continue to wrestle with Catholic Church’s sexual abuse scandals. France was left shocked by a 2021 report that estimated around 330,000 children were sexually abused over 70 years by priests or other church figures. He addressed this by telling crowds the church must admit its own failings and heal “deep wounds” before holding a two-hour meeting with seven survivors of abuse.

The Vatican said that Leo thanked them “for their painful testimony” while “reaffirming his commitment to ensuring that the harm they suffered is not repeated for others.”

But the scandal still lingers. On the façade of the basilica in Lourdes, banners were placed over controversial mosaics ahead of Leo’s visit. These mosaics – which will now be covered indefinitely – were designed by a Slovenian priest and artist, Rev. Marko Rupnik, accused of sexual and psychological abuse of adult women. A local bishop said the pope backed how the apostolic nunciature was handling the artist’s works. Bishop Jean-Marc Micas also said Leo had ordered the Vatican’s in-house media outlets to stop using Rupnik art. Rupnik, who maintains his innocence, is facing a church trial in the Vatican, which complainants say is taking too long and lacks transparency.

The pope was elected 16-months ago and is still carving out a narrative for his papacy. Some in the Vatican find him difficult to read, and the pope is known for keeping his cards close to his chest. But it’s out on the open road when he travels abroad, in France and, in November, in Latin America, where the Leo papacy is beginning to take shape.

World.title: Plane landing was “nothing short of a miracle,” CNN analyst says
World.content:
The emergency landing of a Flydubai flight was “nothing short of a miracle,” CNN national security analyst Alex Plitsas said, describing a series of actions by the crew and passengers that helped avert disaster.

“They had to get everything right to basically make sure everybody survived,” Plitsas told CNN. “And somehow they figured it out as laypersons with no real training.”

According to the analyst, several things stood out.

First was the Indian pilot’s ability to signal an emergency and unlock the cockpit door while being attacked, allowing passengers to enter as the aircraft descended. “The captain somehow had the wherewithal to turn on the transponder and transmit that there was an emergency,” he said.

Second were unarmed passengers who subdued the armed attacker before one pulled back on the yoke to level the aircraft, drawing on knowledge from an air-disaster documentary. Also, Plitsas said, the presence of an additional pilot who happened to be aboard.

“The amount of sheer luck and tenacity and courage from the folks on board is almost impossible to describe,” the analyst told CNN.

According to Plitsas, the episode raises questions about threats originating from within the cockpit. Many post-9/11 security measures focused on preventing outsiders from accessing the cockpit, he noted. A review of personnel records would likely follow, he said, adding that such threats can be difficult to detect.

World.title: UAE and Israel launch probes after Flydubai flight to Tel Aviv forced down
World.content:
The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs commented on Thursday regarding an incident involving a Flydubai flight carrying Israeli passengers.

Via its official account on the X platform, the Ministry stated: “The United Arab Emirates confirmed that it is following up on the incident involving Flydubai flight F21073, traveling from Dubai International Airport to Tel Aviv, which was diverted and landed safely at Tabuk Airport in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia.”

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs explained in a statement that the Attorney General of the Federation, Hamad al-Shamsi, ordered the formation of a specialized team of public prosecutors to investigate the incident and determine its circumstances and causes.

Investigating the circumstances

The formation of the investigation team comes in light of what Flydubai announced regarding an altercation occurring inside the cockpit during the flight, which required the intervention of crew members on board to secure the aircraft.

The ministry emphasized that judicial authorities in the UAE hold jurisdiction over investigating the incident under applicable legislation, as the aircraft is registered in the state and bears its flag, rendering UAE law applicable to crimes committed on board even if they occur outside national territory.

Potential terrorist links

The ministry noted that investigations will examine various circumstances and motives behind the incident, including any potential link to terrorist activity, specific motives, or prior planning and direction.

The UAE further expressed its thanks and appreciation to Saudi authorities, commending their cooperation and swift handling of the incident.

The UAE Ministry of Foreign Affairs stressed the importance of relying on information and data issued by official sources while avoiding the dissemination of speculation or unverified information until investigations are complete.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu stated that Israel will get to the “roots” of the incident involving a co-pilot’s failed attempt to bring down a Flydubai aircraft traveling from Dubai to Israel, adding that Israel “might” participate in the investigations.

Edited translation from Al-Masry Al-Youm

World.title: Far-right Israeli minister says alleged attacker should be extradited to Israel
World.content:
Far-right Israeli Minister of National Security Itamar Ben Gvir has called for the suspect in Wednesday’s apparent hijacking attempt to be extradited to Israel to “pay the highest price here.”

“Anyone who planned to crash a plane and murder 180 Israelis should be extradited to Israel,” Ben Gvir said in a statement. “We must not be satisfied simply because the disaster was prevented.”

“Our security doctrine must be clear: anyone who attempts to murder or harm Israelis — the State of Israel will pursue them and hold them accountable wherever they are in the world,” the minister added.

Despite Ben Gvir’s request for Israel to take the lead, several nations will likely be involved in the probe, including the United Arab Emirates (UAE) and Saudi Arabia, where the plane was forced to land.

UAE authorities have jurisdiction to investigate the incident because the aircraft is registered in the country, and UAE law applies to crimes committed aboard its planes even when they occur outside the country’s territory, state news agency WAM reported Thursday.

The suspect was initially arrested and interrogated by Saudi authorities, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Wednesday. He later added that he assumed the suspected attacker would be transferred to the UAE for questioning, with Israel involved in the investigation.

World.title: Five-day weather forecast predicts warm days and cool autumn nights across Egypt
World.content:
The Egyptian Meteorological Authority (EMA) revealed the expected weather conditions from Friday, October 2, to Tuesday, October 6.

The Authority noted that the country will experience moderate autumn weather in the early morning, turning warm during the day along the northern coast, hot across Lower Egypt, Greater Cairo, and Northern Upper Egypt, and very hot in Southern Upper Egypt, while moderate temperatures will prevail at night.

Expected weather phenomena over the coming days

In its official statement, the EMA explained that morning fog will form between four to eight am on select roads connecting to and from northern Egypt, passing through Greater Cairo, the Canal Cities, Central Sinai, and Northern Upper Egypt.

The EMA also noted chances of light rainfall that may occasionally turn moderate over parts of the northern coastal governorates and Northern Lower Egypt, as well as areas in the Western Desert and Central Upper Egypt at intermittent intervals.

Active winds are expected across most of the country, helping to cool the atmosphere in shaded areas and during the night.

The EMA urged citizens to follow its updated bulletins regarding weather conditions and atmospheric phenomena over the coming period.

World.title: Egypt thwarts Israel’s plans to build Suez Canal alternative: Deputy Prime Minister
World.content:
Egypt’s Deputy Prime Minister for Industrial Development and Minister of Industry and Transport, Kamel al-Wazir, commented on reports regarding an Israeli plan to establish an alternative waterway to the Suez Canal—widely referred to as the “Ben Gurion Canal.”

Speaking during an interview on the Kalam Fi al-Siasa (Talks in Politics) program on the Extra News channel, Al-Wazir stated that Egypt actively monitored and countered all potential alternative maritime and land transport routes designed to bypass or weaken the Suez Canal.

Evaluating alternative trade routes

Al-Wazir addressed rumors surrounding alternative projects, including the proposed Ben Gurion Canal connecting the Gulf of Aqaba (Eilat) to the Mediterranean Sea, as well as railway projects linking the Arabian Gulf to Haifa or ports in Israel and Jordan.

He clarified that Egypt has conducted comprehensive technical and economic feasibility studies on every reported proposal.

The analysis determined that none of these alternative projects—whether canals or rail corridors—possess the geographic, operational, or economic capacity to replace or match the efficiency of the Suez Canal.

Strategic upgrades to the Suez Canal corridor

The minister emphasized that Egypt did not rely solely on its geographic advantage, but took proactive measures to solidify the Suez Canal’s dominance in global trade:

Expanding maritime capacity: The execution of the New Suez Canal project doubled the waterway’s operational capacity, significantly reduced vessel transit times, and accommodated larger modern container ships.

The execution of the New Suez Canal project doubled the waterway’s operational capacity, significantly reduced vessel transit times, and accommodated larger modern container ships. Integrated logistics network: Egypt developed comprehensive logistical corridors connecting the Red Sea to the Mediterranean via high-speed railways, modern highways, and dry ports.

Egypt developed comprehensive logistical corridors connecting the Red Sea to the Mediterranean via high-speed railways, modern highways, and dry ports. Port infrastructure overhaul: Major investments were directed toward upgrading Red Sea and Mediterranean ports (such as Sokhna, East Port Said, Alexandria, and Gargoub) to ensure Egypt remains the primary maritime and logistics hub in the region.

Economic viability and geographic superiority

The Deputy Prime Minister concluded that creating an artificial waterway across complex, mountainous terrain to compete with the Suez Canal is financially unviable and operationally impracticable.

He reiterated that the Suez Canal remains the fastest, safest, and most cost-effective maritime route connecting East and West, and that Egypt’s ongoing infrastructure developments have effectively neutralized competing regional concepts.

World.title: Egypt’s 30-million tourist goal: Ready or bottlenecked?
World.content:
In Egypt’s tourism industry, the central question is no longer: “Can Egypt attract more tourists?”

Recent figures provide a clear affirmative answer. The tougher issue to tackle now: is Egypt’s tourism infrastructure capable of accommodating these numbers and delivering a fitting experience as the country approaches its target of 30 million annual tourists?

During the first eight months of 2026, Egypt welcomed approximately 12.7 million tourists, compared to 12.2 million during the same period last year—a growth rate of nearly four percent.

Tourism revenues rose to around $12 billion, up from $11.8 billion.

Simultaneously, the number of hotels under construction reached 185 comprising roughly 46,000 rooms in 2026, compared to 143 hotels and 33,900 rooms in 2025.

While these figures appear reassuring on the surface, they open a more complex issue – is capacity growing as fast as demand?

Infrastructure constraints: Rooms and airline seats

Minister of Tourism and Antiquities Sherif Fathy addressed the core of the issue during recent meetings with the sector and international institutions, confirming that the primary challenge facing the 30-million-tourist target lies in increasing hotel capacity and the number of airline seats.

He noted that Egypt receives tourists from 179 countries, with traffic growth reaching 20.5 percent in 2025 and continuing to grow at 15.6 percent during Q1 2026 compared to the same period in the previous year.

In the hospitality sector, investments are actively moving, but the gap between current capacity and the target remains substantial.

Data from W Hospitality Group indicates that 46,000 hotel rooms are under construction in 2026—a high number compared to previous years.

However, this does not mean these rooms are immediately operational; the difference between a “planned room” and a “room ready to host a tourist” involves years of financing, construction, fit-out, licensing, and operation.

The Chairman of the Egyptian Tourism Federation, Hossam al-Shaer, stated that Egypt needs to add approximately 200,000 new hotel rooms to achieve the 30 million tourist target.

He warned that converting hotel units into private residential use or closing them for extended periods reduces the actual hotel capacity available to the market.

This reveals a key paradox: Egypt can announce tens of thousands of new rooms, but the actual capacity to host 30 million tourists is measured by active rooms, occupancy rates, and geographic distribution across Cairo, the Red Sea, South Sinai, Luxor, Aswan, the North Coast, and emerging destinations.

Aviation and fleet expansion

If a hotel room provides accommodation, it is the aircraft that brings the tourist in the first place.

Minister of Civil Aviation, Sameh al-Hefny, confirmed that air traffic recorded growth across major and tourist airports during the summer of 2026.

The Cairo International Airport handled approximately 7.94 million passengers between June and August, while the Sharm El-Sheikh Airport surpassed two million passengers during the same period.

The ministry is working to upgrade airport efficiency, maximize operational capacity, and encourage Egyptian and foreign airlines to expand networks and open new markets.

EgyptAir is preparing to expand its operational capabilities.

The Aviation Minister announced that the national carrier currently operates a fleet of 72 aircraft, with 28 new aircraft scheduled to join in 2026 and 2027 as part of a plan targeting a fleet of 125 aircraft in the coming years to support new routes and enhance air connectivity.

However, expanding the national carrier alone is insufficient.

Egyptian tourism relies heavily on foreign airlines and charter flights.

Data from the Chamber of Tourism Establishments reveals that air transport contributed nearly 87 percent of all incoming tourist traffic to Egypt in 2025, making any shortage of seats or flights a direct bottleneck to sector growth.

The challenge does not end upon landing: tourists arriving in Cairo who wish to visit Luxor, Aswan, or Abu Simbel require a safe, fast, and comfortable internal transport system.

Ground transportation and roads

Chamber data indicates that the tourist transport fleet exceeded 12,400 vehicles by the end of 2025, following the licensing of roughly 950 new vehicles during the year.

Road development projects have successfully reduced travel times; for instance, the Cairo–Luxor Western Desert Road cut travel time down to 6.5 hours from nine hours.

Nevertheless, industry stakeholders continue to raise questions regarding specific corridors.

The Head of the Tourist Transport Committee called for upgrading the El Qoseir–Marsa Alam road, rehabilitating the Marsa Alam–Edfu road, and dual-carriageway expansion for the Aswan–Abu Simbel road, as these represent critical axes linking tourist destinations.

The equation is straightforward: increasing tourist arrivals without developing internal transportation strains the quality of the visitor experience.

Human capital and service quality

Beyond hotels and airports lies another critical challenge: workforce and labor.

The World Travel & Tourism Council projects that travel and tourism-related employment in Egypt will reach 3.03 million jobs in 2026, up from 2.97 million in 2025.

However, industry experts emphasize that sheer numbers are not enough and have called for modernizing tourism education and training systems.

The Ministry of Tourism has launched programs to develop human capital, including the EGTAP e-learning platform, in collaboration with tourism chambers and international educational institutions.

World.title: As Liberia Pushes for War Crimes Court, Witness Protection Agency Seeks Safe Houses, Stronger Safeguards for Victims and Witnesses in US$20 Million Plan
World.content:
Liberia’s Witness Protection Agency is seeking to strengthen safeguards for victims, witnesses and whistleblowers under its proposed five-year plan. Credit: Anthony Stephens/New Narratives.

Summary:

Liberia’s Witness Protection Agency has proposed a US$20.54 million five-year strategy that would establish safe houses, rapid-response capacity and stronger safeguards for victims, witnesses and whistleblowers.

The plan comes as Liberia moves towards establishing with war-crimes and anti-corruption courts that will depend heavily on witness testimony and whistleblowers.

The Agency says it has major obstacles: safe houses and other critical infrastructure, and current government funding falls far short of the plan’s projected cost.

By Anthony Stephens, senior justice correspondent with New Narratives

Liberia’s Witness Protection Agency is proposing a five-year, US$20.54 million plan to build a nationwide system for protecting victims, witnesses and whistleblowers as the country moves toward establishing war crimes and anti-corruption courts that will significantly increase the number of witnesses and whistleblowers needing protection.



The plan, reviewed at a two-day gathering of government officials, human rights advocates and international partners in Monrovia last week, calls for trained protection officers, secure case-management systems and mechanisms to relocate people facing threats. It also seeks to strengthen Liberia’s witness and whistleblower laws and secure more reliable financing.

“We believe we have a lot of work to do,” said Maxwell Grigsby, the agency’s director. The consultation was necessary, he said, because protecting witnesses would require government institutions and other organizations to work together.

“That is why we could not sit in our offices to develop a five-year strategic plan for a subject matter that will affect multiple entities,” Grigsby said. “What play will we be doing? How will that play address the realities? How will other actors know the role they have to play, the referral path, and how to address issues that affect real human beings?”

The plan is the first comprehensive strategy developed by the Agency, which experts say is central to building the trust and confidence needed for victims, witnesses and whistleblowers to come forward and cooperate with investigations and prosecutions. The ambitious plan also comes as Liberia’s renewed push for accountability for wartime atrocities and corruption is expected to put greater pressure on a protection system being built by an Agency that has been operational for only about nine months.

The cases against more than a dozen perpetrators accused of crimes in Liberia’s civil conflicts brought by prosecutors in Europe and the United States, have shown that there is almost no forensic or documentary evidence to support cases of crimes committed in the wars, some of which date back more than 30 years. That means cases in Liberia’s court will rely heavily, as the international trials have done, on witness testimony.

For would-be witnesses and whistle-blowers, the danger of coming forward are not theoretical.

In 2023, New Narratives documented 12 cases of government whistleblowers over the previous 14 years who had allegedly faced retaliation. Seven died in circumstances their families alleged were connected to efforts to silence them- though there was no official finding of criminal activity in any of the cases – four lost their jobs, and three others fled the country or went into hiding.

It is against that history that the Agency is trying to build a protection system that remains in its infancy. It has no safe house of its own, limited vehicles and protection personnel, and most of its operations are concentrated in Montserrado. Its five-year strategy proposes two safe houses in Montserrado and three elsewhere in the country, giving authorities secure places to move witnesses and their families when they are in danger.

The Agency estimates that building the system from 2026 through 2030 will cost US$20.54 million. US$6 million is earmarked for protection operations and US$5 million for strengthening its institutional capacity. Financing is expected to come from the national budget, a proposed Victim, Witness and Whistleblower Trust Fund and international donors. The fund would be financed by a one-cent levy on every gallon of petroleum imported into the country.

The Agency also wants a 24-hour emergency desk and agreements with the police and the government’s Executive Protection Service for rapidly moving witnesses out of danger. It plans to train security and justice officials in safely transporting protected witnesses and eventually station protection officers in all 15 counties.

Agency director Grigsby said Liberians with sensitive information have often not felt safe remaining in the country after disclosing wrongdoing.

“We have to change this,” Grigsby said. “We are hoping that just by doing this plan, people will start to think differently. They will believe that they can give testimony in Liberia, stay in Liberia, without having to be so afraid about their safety and our survival.”

But with limited government resources and an exodus of international aid, funds available to the Agency will likely be limited.

The 2026 national budget allocated US$700,000 to the Witness Protection Unit, with government budget projections of US$390,000 for fiscal year 2027 and US$401,000 for 2028 — far below the spending envisioned in the five-year strategy.

The Agency wants the government to commit money specifically to witness protection over several years, beyond its regular operating budget. International donors would be asked to help pay for safe houses, technology, specialized training and psychological services, while the government would cover salaries and other routine expenses.

Oretha Snyder Davis, commissioner for prosecution at the Liberia Anti-Corruption Commission, said financing had to be treated as part of the protection system itself.

“Financing must be considered a strategic part,” of protecting witnesses, Davis said, as a panelist during the program. “We need diversified financing that allows government and development partners to accompany each other.”

The gathering brought together government institutions working on witness and victim protection and international donors.

Hassan Bility, director of the Global Justice and Research Project, Liberia’s leading war crimes investigation group, renewed his call for lawmakers to reduce their salaries and benefits, which often exceed the salaries of lawmakers in European countries with vastly larger national revenue. He demanded they redirect some of the savings toward the proposed courts and witness protection.

The Legislature passed the Witness Protection Act and Whistleblower Act in 2021, but Grigsby said there are gaps, including inadequate penalties for people who violate protections and weaknesses in oversight. The Agency wants both laws amended and clearer rules established for how people enter the protection program and how their information is handled.

The Agency says those changes would require amendments to go through the Legislature, followed by regulations and detailed procedures governing how the agency operates. The Agency has not provided a timetable for when the proposed amendments would be submitted to lawmakers.

International experts took the opportunity to support the Agency’s calls for support, reminding government, lawmakers and stakeholders in the court that victims are at the reason for this court to be held.

“Let us make sure that victims, witnesses, remain at the heart of what we are doing,” said Christian Mukosa, country representative for the Office of the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights in Liberia.

Credible witness protection “is essential for accountability, for access to justice, and for ensuring that victims, witnesses, and human rights defenders can participate safely and meaningfully in national processes,” said Solène Coma, a policy officer and economist in the European Union’s Partnership Section.

She said the European Union was supporting Liberia’s victim-centered transitional justice process through its partnership with the UN Human Rights Office in Liberia and national institutions, including the War and Economic Crimes Court Office.

“Transitional justice, like witness protection, is a collective effort,” Coma said.

This story was a collaboration with New Narratives as part of the Investigating Liberia project. Funding was provided by the U.N. Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights and the European Union. The funders had no say in the story’s content.

World.title: Liberia: Executive Governor Showcases Liberia’s Digital Payments Success Story at MojaCom 32 in Ghana
World.content:
Accra, Ghana – The Executive Governor of the Central Bank of Liberia, Henry F. Saamoi, has presented Liberia’s remarkable progress in digital payments and financial inclusion at MojaCom 32, one of Africa’s premier forums on interoperable and inclusive payment systems.

Delivering a keynote address on the theme, “Accelerating Financial Inclusion Through Instant and Interoperable Payments: Liberia’s Journey and Lessons for Africa”.

Governor Saamoi highlighted Liberia’s ongoing transformation from a fragmented payments landscape to a system driven by real-time, interoperable digital financial services.

Addressing central bank governors, regulators, development partners, financial institutions, and technology leaders from across Africa and beyond, Governor Saamoi emphasized that while access to financial services has expanded significantly across the continent, the next frontier of financial inclusion is connectivity among financial institutions and payment platforms.



“Financial inclusion is no longer primarily constrained by access and affordability. It is increasingly constrained by connectivity,” Governor Saamoi stated, noting that the future of financial inclusion will depend on how effectively financial institutions connect and enable seamless movement of funds across networks.

The CBL Executive Governor highlighted two landmark achievements under Liberia’s payment system modernization agenda: the launch of the Pan-African Payment and Settlement System (PAPSS) and the deployment of the Inclusive Instant Payment System (IIPS). IIPS facilitates real-time interoperability between Liberia’s leading mobile money providers, Lonestar MTN Mobile Money and Orange Money Liberia.

Governor Saamoi disclosed that Liberia’s digital payments ecosystem has already begun delivering measurable results.

In 2025, mobile money transactions in Liberia reached approximately L$585.88 billion and US$6.92 billion in value, while the country’s systemically important payment systems processed approximately 230,367 transactions valued at US$8.5 billion.

He further disclosed that since its launch in December 2025, Liberia’s Inclusive Instant Payment System has processed more than 5.3 million interoperable transactions, including approximately 4.2 million Liberian-dollar transactions valued at over 4.1 billion Liberian dollars and 1.1 million United States dollar transactions valued at US$22.2 million.

According to Governor Saamoi, these achievements demonstrate growing public confidence in digital financial services and underscore the importance of interoperable payment infrastructure in advancing financial inclusion, economic efficiency, and private-sector growth.

The CBL Executive Governor also used the occasion to share key lessons from Liberia’s experience, emphasizing that successful payment system transformation requires strong leadership, collaboration among stakeholders, and recognition of interoperable payment systems as critical national infrastructure.

Looking beyond Liberia, Governor Saamoi called for greater collaboration among African central banks to strengthen regional payment connectivity and support the goals of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), stressing that Africa’s economic integration will depend not only on the movement of goods and services across borders, but also on the ability to move money quickly, securely, and affordably across the continent.

He concluded by reaffirming Liberia’s commitment to building a modern, inclusive, and interconnected financial system while contributing to Africa’s broader digital transformation agenda.

“Africa does not need to wait for the future of payments. Africa can build it. The future of African financial inclusion will not be determined by the number of institutions we create. It will be determined by how effectively those institutions connect,” Governor Saamoi said.

MojaCom 32 brought together central banks, regulators, financial institutions, development partners, and technology providers from around the world to discuss emerging trends and innovations in digital payments, interoperability, and financial inclusion.

World.title: Liberia: NHA Outlines Framework to Unlock Diaspora Investment in Liberia’s Housing Sector — Targets 5,000 Housing Units Nationwide
World.content:
The National Housing Authority (NHA) has outlined a framework aimed at converting growing interest among Liberians in the diaspora into concrete investment in Liberia’s housing sector.

Under the framework, the NHA plans to support the development of 5,000 housing units across all 15 counties from 2026 to 2029, through public-private partnerships and other investment mechanisms.

The initiative is supported by plans for a National Housing Trust Fund and focuses on two major challenges identified by the NHA: limited confidence in land transactions and inadequate knowledge of the estate development process.



Presenting at the just-concluded Liberia Diaspora Investment Conference in the United States on 25 September 2026, NHA Managing Director, Madam Florence Geegbae, said the framework is designed to provide diaspora investors with a more secure and predictable pathway from land acquisition through construction and occupancy.

According to the presentation, the NHA will work with relevant government institutions, including the Liberia Land Authority (LLA) and the Ministry of Public Works, to strengthen land verification, simplify development procedures, and provide professional support to investors.

The initiative forms part of the NHA’s broader 2026–2029 vision for transforming Liberia’s housing sector.

Under the vision, the NHA plans to support the direct government construction of 600 housing units between 2026 and 2027, while pursuing partnerships for the development of the 5,000 affordable units.

The NHA also plans to construct 16 water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH) facilities in four informal settlements in Monrovia and establish Liberia’s first National Housing Information System.

Strengthening Confidence in Land Transactions

The NHA identified land ownership and verification as a major concern for diaspora investors, noting that fewer than 20 percent of Liberia’s land is formally registered.

The entity says it will work with the Liberia Land Authority to strengthen verification systems and ensure that land designated for NHA-affiliated projects is properly verified before development begins.

A key component is the National Deed Verification System, which uses standardized deeds with security features linked to the national land registry.

Verification can be conducted through county land offices, licensed surveyors, and the courts.

The NHA also referenced recent judicial and land governance developments, including a court ruling that struck down a 931.4-acre land grab, as part of efforts to strengthen protection for legitimate land interests.

Simplifying Estate Development

The NHA also identified the complexity of Liberia’s estate development and permitting processes as a barrier for investors unfamiliar with local requirements.

To address this, the National Housing Authority is developing a plain-language, step-by-step estate development roadmap covering the process from land acquisition to occupancy permits, in coordination with the Liberia Land Authority.

The NHA is also working with the Ministry of Public Works to map the building permit process and provide clearer timelines for investors.

Environmental compliance, including an Environmental and Social Impact Assessment (ESIA) and an Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) permit, will also form part of the guidance.

Improving Investment Predictability

The NHA presentation cited an average of 74 days and 22 procedures for obtaining a construction permit, highlighting the need for greater cost and time predictability.

To support investors, the Authority is proposing a Housing Investment Portal that would provide online access to services and information, including land verification, permit checklists, cost calculators, and directories of licensed professionals.

Through these measures, the NHA seeks to create a more transparent, predictable, and secure environment for Liberians in the diaspora and other investors interested in Liberia’s housing sector.

World.title: UL Adjunct Faculty Elects First President, Tengbeh Vows Stronger Advocacy for Faculty and Students
World.content:
Monrovia – The Adjunct Faculty Association of the University of Liberia has elected George Sahr Tengbeh as its first president, establishing an organized leadership structure for adjunct instructors and opening a new chapter in advocacy for faculty welfare and institutional development.

By Gerald C. Koinyeneh

Tengbeh was elected during the association’s inaugural election on Wednesday, September 30, in Room TH 50 on the University of Liberia’s Capitol Hill Campus.



The election also produced a full leadership team, with Joseph Kla Wisner Jr. elected Vice President; Cephas MMD Flanzamaton, Secretary General; and Isaac Saah Lakpasiyoe, Assistant Secretary General.

Humphrey Tarpeh was elected Financial Secretary, Nathan Ballepa Treasurer, Amos B. Karbedeh Chaplain, and James D. Sinnatwah Jr. Advisor.

The newly elected leadership represents adjunct faculty members serving across the University’s campuses, colleges, schools and academic departments, including the Fendell Campus, Sinje in Grand Cape Mount County, Amos Sawyer College, T.J. Faulkner College and the School of Public Health.

Tengbeh Pledges Dialogue

In remarks following his election, Tengbeh thanked adjunct faculty members for entrusting him and his colleagues with the responsibility of representing their interests.

He pledged to pursue the association’s advocacy agenda through dialogue and constructive engagement with the University administration and other stakeholders.

At the center of the association’s agenda are concerns over adjunct faculty compensation, job security, employment pathways for long-serving instructors, access to University identification cards and equitable opportunities for professional and human-capacity development.

For adjunct instructors who have served the University for years, the absence of a clear pathway toward more sustainable employment remains a longstanding concern.

Tengbeh’s administration says it intends to engage University authorities on these issues while seeking practical and sustainable solutions rather than confrontation.

The association also plans to advocate for greater access to professional development, training, research and other capacity-building opportunities for adjunct instructors.

Students Remain a Priority

While placing faculty welfare high on its agenda, the new leadership says students remain central to the University’s academic mission.

The association maintains that better working conditions, professional development and support for faculty should ultimately translate into improved teaching, stronger faculty-student engagement and better educational outcomes.

The new leadership is therefore expected to support initiatives aimed at strengthening teaching quality and promoting academic excellence across the University.

Tengbeh and his team have also expressed a willingness to work with University administrators, student leaders, other faculty associations, alumni, government, development partners and other stakeholders on initiatives aimed at advancing the institution.

Beyond Faculty Welfare

The association says its mandate extends beyond the immediate interests of adjunct instructors to the broader development of the University of Liberia.

Its leadership says it will promote dialogue, collaboration, professional responsibility and solutions-oriented engagement in addressing challenges affecting faculty and students.

With adjunct instructors playing a significant role in teaching across multiple academic programs, the association believes a stronger and more professionally supported adjunct faculty can contribute to the University’s academic mission.

The association also intends to improve communication among adjunct faculty members and create a coordinated platform for presenting their concerns, recommendations and professional interests to University authorities.

New Leadership

The association’s inaugural elected leadership comprises:

President: George Sahr Tengbeh

Vice President: Joseph Kla Wisner Jr.

Secretary General: Cephas MMD Flanzamaton

Assistant Secretary General: Isaac Saah Lakpasiyoe

Financial Secretary: Humphrey Tarpeh

Treasurer: Nathan Ballepa

Chaplain: Amos B. Karbedeh

Advisor: James D. Sinnatwah Jr.

Following the election, the association thanked former Acting President Wilhelmina Garr-Steven and her team for their service during the transitional period.

It also commended the Election Committee, chaired by Abayomi K. Nmah, for overseeing the inaugural electoral process, while special appreciation was extended to Acting President James Massaboi for facilitating what the association described as a smooth election.

The election marks the establishment of the association’s first permanent elected leadership and provides adjunct faculty members with a formal platform for collective representation.

The association has adopted the slogan: “United in Representation. Committed to Service. Focused on the Future.”
