More than 30 million people visited a museum in the Netherlands in 2025, a 2.5% increase over the year prior, according to trade association Museumvereniging.

Dutch museums welcomed 31.6 million visitors in 2025, almost back to pre-pandemic levels. In 2019, museums saw 32.6 million guests.

Nearly 90% of Dutch people go to a museum at least once a year, the Museumcijfers 2025 report found.

In 2025 the Netherlands had 492 registered museums. Most institutions are history museums, making up 62%, followed by art museums, which account for 24%.

The use of the yearly Museum Card hit a record high of 9.7 million visits in 2025. Visits using the subscription service is up 5% over the 2019 peak.

A recent survey by Ipsos I&O found that trust in museums is high and most adults consider them to be an important part of society.

World.title: Golf to a Japanese garden: 13 great things to do in October
World.content:
It’s October and the cultural season is off to a good start. There are lots of restful established names in this month’s cultural offerings, with some modern challenges mixed in.

Experience Butoh

It’s the 10th edition of the Butoh Festival at the Teatro Munganga in Amsterdam this month. Fourteen dancers from Austria, Belgium, Finland, France, Italy, Mexico, Taiwan and the UK will be performing their interpretation of the avant-garde “dance of darkness”, which originated in Japan after the devastation of the atomic bombs. October 2 and 3. Website

Get your skates on for some colf

It is touted as the earliest depiction of golf: Hendrick Avercamp’s Colf Players on the Ice dating from around 1625. Then as now, the players in the foreground look like well-to-do-gentlemen while in the back two others seem to be playing a game of ice hockey.

The Rijksmuseum and the Mauritshuis have just bought the painting for an eyewatering €11.4 million from a private owner in the United States. It will go on show in Avercamp’s home town of Kampen as part of the exhibition Averkamp back in Kampen: the 17th century through the eyes of Hendrick and Barent. (Barent, Hendrick’s nephew, also specialised in winter landscapes) From October 3. Website

Believe it (or not)

In a time when scientific fact is regarded as just another opinion, the Teylers Museum in Haarlem is mounting Zeker Weten? (Are we sure?), an exhibition around the five tenets of scientific research: prove, repeat, modify, check and build.

That is exactly what the scientists of yore did, for instance when sightings of black swans overturned the assumption that only white ones existed, and the discovery in 1938 of a coelacanth, which proved it was not extinct. Historical books, models and instruments illustrate the search for “exact” science. From October 2. Website

Meet Matisse at the H’ART

The H’ART Museum in Amsterdam has unselfishly offered to relieve the soon-to-be refurbished Centre Pompidou of its Matisse collection, along with other paintings by the likes of Mark Rothko, Pablo Picasso, and Barnett Newman that also needed a new temporary home.

Chez Matisse – Masterpieces from the Centre Pompidou, comprises some 80 works, including La Blouse roumaine, which is hardly ever allowed off the Pompidou premises. The collection follows Matisse as he experimented with colour and shapes, culminating in his work at the Chapelle du Rosaire in Vence. From October 3. Website

Catch a De Kooning

The Rijksmuseum blockbuster this autumn is a retrospective of Dutch abstract expressionist painter Willem de Kooning (1904-1997) which puts his drawings centre stage. De Kooning left his native Rotterdam at age 24 and entered the United States as a stowaway. Willem de Kooning at work shows over 120 drawings, and some of his sculptures and paintings, mapping out De Kooning’s journey from house painter to important innovator of modern art. From October 6. Website

Get a taste of Japan in The Hague

The Japanese Garden at the Clingendael Estate in The Hague, which opens for a few weeks every year, is more popular than ever. Make sure you get your ticket for a slot to see its autumnal splendour. From October 10. Website

Cock a snoot at speculators

Plus ça change…Cherry Town is a jolly musical romp about housing shortage, corruption and the healing power of love, based on the operetta by Russian composer Dmitri Shostakovich written in 1959. Performed by the Dutch National Opera and supported by the Netherlands Philharmonic, the comical shenanigans of speculators and indignant tenants are a treat for young (from 10) and old. Sung in English. October 8-20. Website

Remember Marisol

The Boijmans van Beuningen museum in Rotterdam has dusted off the largely forgotten work of Marisol (1930-2016), a Venezuelan artist whose playful wooden sculptures about serious subjects, such as women’s rights and the environment, became popular in the 1960s. The museum organised her first solo show and The Car became one of its most celebrated exhibits. From October 9. Website

Say hello to Whistler’s mum

Van Gogh liked and wrote about many of his contemporaries, including James Whistler, which spurred the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam to organise the major retrospective Whistler, Dandy and Disruptor. The dandy bit refers to his dashing looks while his l’art pour l’art attitude upset the critics of the time.

His most famous painting Arrangement in Gray and Black, No. 1, better known, to his annoyance, as Whistler’s Mother, moved Van Gogh, who said it reminded him of his own mother. From October 16. Website

..and see his take on Amsterdam

At the same time as the main exhibition in Amsterdam, the Mesdag Collection in The Hague presents Whistler. Loving the Netherlands. The painter visited the Netherlands 10 times, resulting in etchings and atmospheric watercolours.

With dandyish good taste, he chastised his Dutch fellow artists: “You Dutch painters don’t know what you’re missing by neglecting your beautiful city of Amsterdam, which I find more beautiful than Venice.” From October 16. Website

Explore some great design ideas

Dutch Design Week is ‘returning to RAW or Rebel Authentic Worth, unpolished and real”, so prepare to get basic. The Sausage Stool (Wuerstelhocker), a sausage-shaped perch on which to enjoy a wuerstel (and future sausage stool), is a case in point.

Eindhoven becomes the focal point of international creative ideas on serious subjects such as sustainability, new materials, technology, education, play and much, much more. October 17-25. Website

Get to know Eve at the Vrijthof

The Fotomuseum aan het Vrijthof in Maastricht presents All About Eve, a retrospective of celebrated Magnum photographer Eve Arnold. The selection of 150 photographs focuses on her work from the 50s, 60s and 70s and includes images of famous filmstars and several series, including Malcolm X and Fashion Shows in Harlem. From October 19. Website

Get a buzz at the ADE

The 30th edition of the electronic music festival Amsterdam Dance Event is about to be unleashed on the capital, featuring, among many others, the Concertgebouw Orchestra playing Beethoven’s Fifth Symphony against the background of Einder, an artificial and ever-changing sky of floaty fabric covering the vast Centrale Markthal.

The ADE is also putting in a special appearance at the Van Gogh Museum (see above) on October 23, when electronic music band Devon Rexi and musician Coby Sey will respond electronically to Whistler’s work Nocturnes. October 21-25. Website

World.title: Young Amsterdammers drink less as ketamine gains ground
World.content:
Young people in Amsterdam are drinking less alcohol, but drugs like ketamine have become far more popular at the same time, according to an annual monitor of drug and alcohol use commissioned by addiction care organisation Jellinek.

The researchers say Gen Z drinks less often and more consciously, partly because of rising prices.

The Antenne Amsterdam 2025 report was published on Wednesday by the Amsterdam University of Applied Sciences (HvA). It draws on a survey of 1,183 vocational college (mbo) students, interviews with 22 nightlife insiders and five youth workers, and close to 5,000 drug samples handed in to testing services.

Of the students surveyed, 59% had drunk alcohol in the past year and 46% in the past four weeks. Both figures are lower than among their peers at hbo colleges and universities.

Ketamine on the rise

Ketamine use is widespread in Amsterdam’s nightlife and has risen sharply again since 2024, the report says. Ketamine, MDMA and other powder drugs are relatively cheap, going for €25-30 per gram, and are easily obtained via home delivery services.

Demand for 3-MMC, a synthetic stimulant, appears barely affected by a ban on several groups of related substances that took effect on July 1 last year. Drugs sold as 3-MMC often turn out to contain other substances, such as 2-MMC.

Among vocational students, however, 3-MMC is relatively rare: 7% have ever tried it and 5% used it in the past year. Laughing gas has almost disappeared since the sales ban. Just 9% of students said they had ever used it, down from 24% in 2021.

Vaping and gambling

Fewer students smoke than in previous years, but nicotine products remain popular. Some 24% smoke, 18% vaped in the past four weeks, and 7% used nicotine pouches, known as snus.

The share of students who gambled online in the past year has tripled, from 6% in 2021 to 18%. The researchers caution that the question was worded differently in 2025.

Less drinking is a positive development but it brings new concerns, Jellinek prevention specialist Raoul Koning said in a statement. He named vaping, snus, 3-MMC, ketamine, and gambling as particular problems.

If you are concerned about your own or someone else’s use of alcohol, drugs, or gambling, the Jellinek addiction helpline can be reached on 088 505 1220 or at jellinek.nl. The line is staffed in Dutch and English on weekdays, 1pm to 5pm.

World.title: EU halts aid funds to Sierra Leone over Bolle Jos extradition
World.content:
The European Commission has stopped payments to Sierra Leone with immediate effect because the country will not extradite fugitive drugs baron Jos Leijdekkers, known as Bolle Jos, justice minister David van Weel has confirmed.

Van Weel told De Telegraaf: “I am very happy with this step. It is galling that EU money goes to a country that does not want to cooperate with the extradition of someone like Bolle Jos.”

Jos reportedly has a child with the daughter of Sierra Leone’s president, Julius Maada Bio, and maintains close ties with the government there. Drugs shipments passing through the West African coast are an increasing concern, for which Van Weel wants to establish a permanent secretariat.

Sierra Leone was expected to receive €18 million euros in budget support from Europe this year, most of it intended to bolster education, food programs and infrastructure projects. The Netherlands is also hoping to stop a planned payment of €22.5 million to the country next year.

Van Weel travelled to West Africa recently to garner support from surrounding nations like Ghana and Liberia.

Van Weel is in Luxembourg on Thursday for a meeting with EU justice ministers, where tougher sanctions on criminals hiding outside Europe, such as entry bans and asset freezes, will be discussed.

Pressure to tackle the cocaine trade has grown since an armed attack on a farm in Overasselt, Gelderland, last month, in which a security guard was killed. The attack is thought to be linked to the drugs trade.

World.title: Clitoris reconstruction surgery successful at Radboudumc
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Doctors at Radboudumc have successfully completed clitoral reconstruction surgeries in women who lost part of the sex organ to vulvar cancer, including restoring their ability to orgasm.

In a statement, the hospital in Nijmegen said that of 23 women who underwent the procedure, 90% were able to experience a clitoral orgasm again.

In the Netherlands, approximately 450 women are diagnosed with vulvar cancer every year. In around 25% of those cases, the clitoris or the surrounding area is affected.

In patients whose tumour is located on or near the clitoris, part of the organ may need to be removed.

“Until now, the wound was closed afterwards and the clitoris disappeared under a layer of skin, without regard for quality of life or the question of whether an orgasm is still possible,” gynecological oncologist Mieke ten Eikelder said.

This advancement has happened almost 40 years after similar surgery for the penis. The first reconstructive surgery for the penis after cancer dates back to 1987.

Clitoral reconstruction is now being rolled out nationwide as part of scientific research.

World.title: Curaçao refused Machado flight after request “from higher up”
World.content:
Curaçao’s aviation authority refused landing permission for a plane carrying Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado on her way back to Venezuela last week after a “request from higher up”, the authority’s director told broadcaster NOS.

Peter Steinmetz, head of the Curaçao Civil Aviation Authority (CCAA), did not say who made the request. Ministers in Willemstad and The Hague have also not commented on who made it.

The private plane was due to fly from Panama, where Machado is living, to Curaçao on September 22. An attempt to fly her to Aruba the same day also fell through. Journalists travelling with Machado said at the time that the flights had been cancelled because of problems with paperwork.

Machado won the Nobel peace prize last year for her efforts in opposing Venezuela’s former president Nicolás Maduro, who was captured by US forces in January. US policy is officially neutral on whether she should return, Axios reported in July, adding that her repeated attempts had angered senior officials in the Trump administration.

Who made the request?

The island’s prime minister Gilmar Pisas declined to comment, and the national transport minister Charles Cooper said the request did not come from him.

Curaçao controls its own civil aviation, but foreign policy is a joint matter for the whole Kingdom of the Netherlands.

Eric van der Burg, the Dutch junior minister for kingdom relations, told Caribbean media that foreign minister Tom Berendsen would speak on the issue, calling it “a very delicate situation.”

According to NOS, the decision was taken by the kingdom council of ministers, which brings together the Dutch cabinet and ministers from Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten.

Berendsen attended a meeting of the council on September 25, three days after the flights were refused. Prime minister Rob Jetten declined to rule out Dutch involvement at his weekly press conference last week.

Unanswered questions

It remains unclear whether the request came from Curaçao, the Netherlands or another government.

Earlier this week, Leiden university professor Wouter Veenendaal, who specialises in relations between the nations in the Kingdom of the Netherlands, told Dutch News: “I can’t prove it, but it sounds to me like The Hague has been put under pressure by the Americans.”

“Although the Americans formally take a positive view of Machado, her arrival is seen as potentially threatening the relative stability that they’ve been able to create with the interim president.”

Machado’s team says she has made at least seven attempts to return to Venezuela.

Dutch News has asked the foreign affairs ministry who made the request and whether the Netherlands was involved. The ministry had not responded at the time of publication.

World.title: Writer and cabaret performer Paulien Cornelisse dies at age 50
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Celebrated writer and cabaret performer Paulien Cornelisse, known for her popular books about the Dutch language, died on Wednesday of cancer.

The 50-year-old was a jury chair on the popular TV quiz show De Slimste Mens as well as authoring a number of books, including Taal is zeg maar echt mijn ding or Language is really my thing.

She announced in 2024 that she had been diagnosed with cancer. During an appearance on De Slimste Mens last month she wore a blue beanie to cover her head after losing her hair to chemotherapy.

Broadcaster KRO-NCRV announced on Wednesday that the evening’s episode of De Slimste Mens would be cancelled.

“I am incredibly sad. Paulien was sweet, funny, and also – between treatments – greatly energetic,” her co-host Herman van der Zandt said in a statement.

Cornelisse began her career as a cabaret performer. In 2008, Taal is zeg maar echt mijn ding was published and became a bestseller, with over 700,000 copies sold.

She later wrote absurdist novels about a guinea pig working in an office, starting with De verwarde cavia (The Confused Guinea Pig), which was also a bestseller. The follow-up, De verwarde cavia – Terug op kantoor (The Confused Guinea Pig – Back at the Office), won the NS Public Prize last year.

She wrote a weekly column about language for the NRC for 10 years, and had been a front-page columnist for the Volkskrant since 2018.

Volkskrant editor-in-chief Pieter Klok said her death was “a loss for the whole of the Netherlands.”

Cornelisse was born and raised in Amsterdam. The city’s mayor Femke Halsema wrote in a post on social media that she was someone “who loved the small, the everyday, the absurd, and the theatre.”

“Sadly, that stage was no longer granted to her,” Halsema said.

World.title: Leading Polish business owners invest in small nuclear reactor venture
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A group of prominent Polish businesspeople have announced that they are investing in a project to develop small modular nuclear reactors being led by the country’s richest man, Michał Sołowow. Among them are Rafał Brzoska, founder of delivery giant InPost, and Mati Staniszewski, CEO of ElevenLabs, a leading artificial intelligence firm. The group is investing 500 million zloty (€114 million) in Sołowow’s Synthos Green Energy (SGE), which, together with 1.35 billion zloty from foreign investors, will secure the company’s financing for the next two years as it seeks to roll out BWRX-300 reactors in Poland, Central and Eastern Europe and the UK. As a European SMR development platform headquartered in Warsaw, Poland’s energy security is of special importance to us. We are proud to announce that today our founder, Michał Sołowow, unveiled a PLN 500 million investment by a group of leading Polish entrepreneurs in SGE’s… pic.twitter.com/J2SerVjIlG — SGE (@SGE_Nuclear) September 30, 2026 The investment, which was formally announced at a business conference in Warsaw on Wednesday, comes as Sołowow seeks to expand his nuclear project beyond SGE’s troubled partnership with Polish state energy giant Orlen, where disagreements have delayed plans to build SMRs in Poland. Alongside Brzoska and Staniszewski, the other new investors are Dariusz Gałęzewski, co-founder of drinks maker Oshee; Krzysztof Pawiński, CEO of food company Maspex; Michał Brański of media group Wirtualna Polska; and Michał Wypychewicz of ZPUE, the largest manufacturer of transformer stations in Europe. “They invested their own private funds because they understood the problem and then believed in the concept and the solution,” Sołowow told Business Insider Polska. SMRs, which are prefabricated in factories before being installed on site, are seen by their proponents as a fast and cost-effective way of installing nuclear capacity. In July, SGE announced plans to build 14 BWRX-300 reactors with a combined capacity of 4.2 gigawatts (GW) across three sites in the UK, which it said would generate enough electricity to meet 11% of the country’s demand. The company also hopes to deploy up to 26 reactors across six locations in Poland. The BWRX-300 is a 300-megawatt water-cooled small modular reactor. Construction of the first ever unit began in Canada in 2025, with completion planned for 2029 and commercial operation expected in 2030. Synthos Green Energy, a firm owned by Polish billionaire Michał Sołowow, has announced plans to build 14 small modular nuclear reactors in the UK. It says that the £35 billion project could deliver enough power to meet 11% of the UK’s demand https://t.co/YTMIzYERuJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) July 2, 2026 Brzoska said that developing SMR technology “is an investment in Poland’s future”, because without “reliable, predictable and competitively priced energy…it is difficult to talk seriously about further growth in industry, data centres, artificial intelligence, automation or modern logistics”. Staniszewski, whose company recently received an $11 million investment from Poland’s state-owned National Development Bank (BGK) to establish an AI development centre in Poland, said lower electricity prices were important for the sector. SGE notes that demand for electricity is set to rise 40% in Poland over the next 14 years, according to grid operator PSE. Electricity prices have risen rapidly in recent years and are now the second most expensive in the European Union in relation to the cost of living. Poland has recorded the EU's third-fastest rise in household electricity prices this year. The country now also has the bloc’s second-most-expensive electricity, when taking cost of living into account https://t.co/WNLdCfOP16 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 30, 2025 Poland remains the EU’s most coal-dependent country, with more than half of its electricity generated from coal. Over the past decade, however, the country has diversified its energy mix, with the share of renewable energy sources tripling to nearly 30% in 2025. Poland plans to reduce its reliance on coal further, including through the construction of its first nuclear power plant (of the traditional type, not an SMR). The 3.75-gigawatt project is scheduled to be commissioned in 2036. Sołowow has also been pursuing the deployment of SMRs in Poland through Orlen Synthos Green Energy (OSGE), a joint venture between SGE and state energy giant Orlen, Poland’s largest company, to develop BWRX-300 reactors in Poland. OSGE is seeking a so-called contract for difference (CfD) framework, an agreement with a state that guarantees a fixed price for electricity and helps shield developers from market swings, covering 14 reactors at three sites. Polish state energy firm Orlen has announced an agreement to build the country’s first small modular nuclear reactor (SMR). It says Poland will be the first country in Europe to deploy an SMR developed by US-based firm GE Hitachi Nuclear Energy https://t.co/MPWXS3qZ1d — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 28, 2025 The project, however, has been delayed by disagreements between the two shareholders. Sołowow told Business Insider Polska that they reached an agreement last month that would allow construction of two reactors to move forward, but said he regretted entering into the partnership with Orlen. “I find it deeply regrettable, because it is precisely due to Orlen’s unnecessary involvement that we are discussing this project in political terms, even though it is not a political project,” he said. Sołowow has argued that a private-sector model can shorten construction times and improve cost control compared with traditional state-led nuclear projects. At the same time, he has highlighted the importance of the state’s role in implementing the project, saying its success depends on coordination between private investors and state policy. This includes contracts for difference, administrative procedures and the preparedness of the nuclear regulator. World.title: Activists launch world’s first abortion pill delivery locker in Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Activists in Poland have launched what they say is the world’s first delivery locker that provides women with abortion pills, access to which is normally tightly restricted. They have placed the device opposite parliament in Warsaw, a location intended to send a message to the politicians who have made Poland’s abortion laws among the strictest in the world. The locker (called an “abortomat” in Polish, combining the words aborcja, meaning abortion, and automat, meaning an automatic machine) has been launched by Women Help Women (WHW), a global organisation that provides “self-managed abortion”, and Abortion Dream Team (ADT), a Polish activist group. They emphasise that the installation “is completely real [and] not an artistic performance”. It consists of 22 numbered lockers and a numeric keypad. Women who have contacted WHM seeking an abortion are given a six-digit PIN code that opens one of the doors, inside which is a package containing the pills. Recipients can either take the pills at home or do so in a specially prepared space opened last year by ADT and where the locker is located. The activists emphasise that such delivery mechanisms for abortion pills are particularly important in Poland because of the country’s highly restrictive laws. Abortions are only allowed in two circumstances: if pregnancy is the result of a crime (such as rape or incest) or if it threatens the mother’s life or health. As a result, only 851 legal terminations took place in Poland last year. However, activist groups such as WHW, ADT and Women on Web (WOW) say that they help tens of thousands of women in Poland obtain abortions each year through other means, in particular by providing pills. But they face legal risks for doing so: assisting someone in obtaining an unlawful abortion is a crime punishable by up to three years in prison. In 2023, ABW activist Justyna Wydrzyńska was convicted of that offence. Two years later, the sentence was annulled on a technicality and a new trial was ordered. Polish activist Justyna Wydrzyńska, who was convicted for providing abortion pills to a pregnant woman, has succeeded in having the conviction overturned on appeal. However, the case will now return to the lower court, where it will be heard again https://t.co/U3J5FmXdMw — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 14, 2025 “The abortomat transforms a closely guarded, criminalised procedure into something as simple as picking up a package,” wrote ADT. “A door that opens when all others have slammed shut.” They say that the machine is intended for women who have an urgent medical need that means they cannot wait for the several days it takes to deliver pills by post, or who are in abusive, controlling relationships that make postal delivery unsafe. Wydrzyńska’s conviction came after the husband of a woman she helped obtain abortion pills found them and reported the case to the police. However, although assisting a woman in obtaining an unlawful abortion is an offence, the woman who had the abortion is not criminally liable. “The abortomat is not a human being, and the person collecting the pills, in accordance with the regulations, is not breaking the law,” said Wydrzyńska, quoted by news website Wirtualna Polska. WHW and ADT do not collect any personal information from women using the service. The European Court of Human Rights has ruled that Poland violated the rights of a pregnant woman who had to travel abroad to obtain an abortion after her foetus was diagnosed with a birth defect https://t.co/TgckusMxmJ — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) November 13, 2025 Under the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government, which ruled from 2015 to 2023, the abortion law was tightened and was strictly enforced. In December 2023, a new, more liberal coalition led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk came to power, promising to liberalise the abortion law. However, it has so far failed to pass any such legislation. In 2024, a move to decriminalise abortion assistance up to the 12th week of pregnancy was rejected by parliament, after the most conservative element of Tusk’s coalition joined the right-wing opposition in voting against it. Tusk subsequently admitted that it would be impossible during the current parliament to soften abortion laws. Instead, his government issued guidelines on when and how abortions can be carried out, with the aim of ensuring that doctors and prosecutors “take the women’s side” when making decisions on the issue. World.title: Fugitive opposition politician granted safe passage to return to Poland against prosecutors’ wishes
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A Warsaw court has approved a request from Marcin Romanowski, a fugitive former government minister who has been on the run for almost two years, to receive safe passage back to Poland. Romanowski is believed to currently be in the pro-Russian Moldovan breakaway region of Transnistria. Although Polish prosecutors have long been seeking Romanowski’s return, they opposed his request for safe conduct, arguing that he cannot be trusted to comply with its terms given that he has repeatedly sought to evade the law. Waldemar Żurek, the justice minister and prosecutor general, has already announced that prosecutors will appeal the court’s decision, which he claims was issued by an illegitimately appointed judge and in violation of regulations. Nie ma i nie będzie bezkarności dla ludzi Zbigniewa Ziobry. Prokuratura złoży ZAŻALENIE na decyzję o wydaniu listu żelaznego dla Marcina Romanowskiego. Spójrzmy prawdzie w oczy: kto jednoosobowo próbuje zapewnić nietykalność człowiekowi podejrzanemu o gigantyczne nadużycia w… — Waldemar Żurek (@w_zurek) September 30, 2026 Romanowski served as deputy justice minister in the former Law and Justice (PiS) government between 2019 and 2023. After PiS lost power, prosecutors sought to bring charges against him for 11 alleged crimes committed while he served in government, including participating in an organised criminal group. However, Romanowski fled Poland in December 2024 and was granted asylum by Hungary, which was then ruled by Viktor Orbán, a conservative ally of PiS. When Orbán lost power earlier this year, Romanowski went on the run, and for months his location was unknown. In August, it emerged that Romanowski had sent a letter to Poland requesting safe passage to return. The document indicated that he was in Tiraspol, the capital of Transnistria, a region that sought to break away from Moldova in the 1990s and is now effectively under Russian control. Prime Minister @donaldtusk says that, based on intelligence sources, Poland is now “99% certain” that fugitive opposition politician Marcin Romanowski is in Transnistria, a breakaway region of Moldova that has close links to Russia https://t.co/mdvmJpkFf7 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) August 18, 2026 At the time, the spokesman for Poland’s National Prosecutor’s Office, Przemysław Nowak, said that there were “no grounds whatsoever” to approve Romanowski’s request for safe passage to Poland. He noted that “the suspect has evaded legal proceedings, questioned the legality of the authorities’ actions, left Poland and then Hungary to avoid arrest, and publicly declared his lack of intention to return to the country due to the ongoing criminal proceedings against him”. However, on Wednesday, Warsaw’s district court approved Romanowski’s request. A spokeswoman for the court said that the decision had been made as “previous methods used [to secure Romanowski’s return] were ineffective” and safe passage would “allow the case to be clarified”. The politician’s lawyer, Bartosz Lewandowski, said that safe passage meant his client could not be detained in Poland and that a European Arrest Warrant against him, which applies in other EU countries, would no longer be valid. ❗️Sąd Okręgowy Warszawie wydał @RomanowskiPL list żelazny, uchylając środek zapobiegawczy w postaci tymczasowego aresztowania od momentu uprawomocnienia się orzeczenia❗️ Mój Klient na terytorium Polski nie będzie mógł być zatrzymany i tymczasowo aresztowany, a ENA „upada”, jeśli… — Bartosz Lewandowski (@BartoszLewand20) September 30, 2026 In a subsequent justification for the ruling, quoted by the Rzeczpospolita daily, judge Konrad Mielcarek wrote that Romanowski had pledged to “voluntarily return to the country”. Conditions for his safe passage include Romanowski reporting to the court and prosecutors at designated times and places, not leaving his declared place of residence, and not seeking to obstruct the criminal proceedings against him. The judge said that prosecutors had failed to provide adequate arguments as to why Romanowski’s request should be denied. He also found that Romanowski had not obstructed proceedings against him, but had merely exercised available legal remedies. The fact that Romanowski had fled Poland does not count against him, argued the judge. In fact, “the very nature of safe passage is to provide a person residing abroad with a legal guarantee…in exchange for voluntarily submitting to the jurisdiction of Polish authorities”. The judge also clarified that safe passage is neither a “reward” nor a “privilege” and that, given that evidence in the case is already secured and Romanowski no longer has influence over justice ministry officials, the risk of tampering is low. The National Prosecutor’s Office immediately issued a statement declaring its opposition to the ruling and its intention to appeal. It noted that there had been no confirmation that Romanowski really is in Tiraspol and that the suspect had repeatedly sought to evade the law. “These circumstances do not provide assurance that the suspect will comply with the conditions of the letter of safe conduct,” wrote the prosecutors, who also pointed to the fact that Romanowski had admitted to using travel documents issued under a false identity. Żurek, meanwhile, noted that Mielcarek is one of the so-called “neo-judges”, appointed by a judicial body rendered illegitimate by PiS’s reforms. There are legal doubts about the status of such judges and the rulings issued by them, some of which have been overturned on that basis. In his statement, the justice minister also argued that, under the law, safe passage cannot be issued without a prosecutor’s consent. Lewandowski, however, cited examples of case law that he said disproved this. He also noted that prosecutors had not filed any motion to recuse Mielcarek from the case. Prokurator ocenia dzisiejsze postanowienie Sądu o wydaniu podejrzanemu Marcinowi Romanowskiemu listu żelaznego jako niezasadne. Na postanowienie to prokurator złoży zażalenie. Sąd może wydać list żelazny, jeżeli podejrzany przebywający za granicą złoży oświadczenie, że stawi… — Prokuratura (@PK_GOV_PL) September 30, 2026 Romanowski served in the justice ministry when it was led by Zbigniew Ziobro, a deputy leader of PiS, who is also wanted by the Polish authorities on suspicion of 26 crimes relating to his time in office. Like his deputy, Ziobro also obtained asylum in Hungary. When Orbán lost power, Ziobro fled to the United States, reportedly with help from a senior Trump administration official. Poland has requested that Ziobro be extradited, though that process could take years. Both Ziobro and Romanowski deny committing the crimes they are accused of and claim that they are being pursued as an act of “political revenge” by the government of Prime Minister Donald Tusk. To mark the occasion, the speaker of the lower-house Sejm, Włodzimierz Czarzasty, personally informed Cobra of the decision. “An application for transfer to retirement?” said Czarzasty, sitting opposite the extremely well-behaved Cobra in a video published by the Sejm. “Impeccable reputation. No disciplinary punishments. You’ve never barked in the Sejm,” he read from her files. “OK, signed. As of tomorrow, you are free.” Cobra idzie na emeryturę! 🐕‍🦺 Decyzję o przejściu w stan spoczynku przypieczętował podpisem Marszałek Sejmu @wlodekczarzasty. 😉 Psy Straży Marszałkowskiej to ważny element systemu ochrony Sejmu. Czuwają nad bezpieczeństwem wszystkich osób w gmachach pozostających w zarządzie… pic.twitter.com/dKRvHOlKxe — Sejm RP🇵🇱 (@KancelariaSejmu) September 30, 2026 On a more serious note, the Sejm pointed to the vital role played by dogs in the so-called Speaker’s Guard (Straż Marszałkowska), which is responsible for security in parliament. “They watch over the safety of all people in the buildings managed by the chancellery of the Sejm,” they wrote, thanking Cobra for eight years of “exemplary” service and wishing her well on her “well-deserved retirement”. Two weeks ago, the Sejm announced the arrival of a new dog, Otik, who would serve as part of the Speaker’s Guard. He has worked alongside Cobra and another canine colleague, Hela, until now. State broadcaster TVP reports that Cobra was one of the first dogs to enter service in the Speaker’s Guard. It notes that dogs serving in the force are eligible for retirement after reaching the age of nine. Their handler has the option of taking in the dog after it retires, or they can nominate another person to care for the animal. The chancellery of the Sejm then continues to cover the costs of any veterinary care that the dog requires. It has not been revealed where and with whom Cobra will spend her retirement. In 2021, Poland’s government moved to introduce retirement benefits for dogs and horses who had served in the police force, border guard and fire service, providing them with support after they finished working. The following year, that was extended to the prison service. World.title: Inflation hits 4% in Poland as fuel prices surge
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Poland’s inflation accelerated to an annual rate of 4.0% in September, up from 3.4% a month earlier, driven primarily by higher fuel prices amid the ongoing conflict in the Middle East and the end of Polish government subsidies that kept down prices at the pump. The development means that inflation has now risen above the upper bound of 3.5% set by the National Bank of Poland (NBP), which aims to keep the figure at 2.5%, plus or minus one percentage point. Analysts say that an interest rate hike by the NBP is now more likely. The new preliminary inflation figures from Statistics Poland (GUS), a state agency, show that prices in September were 4% higher than a year earlier, the fastest rise since June 2025. On a monthly basis, prices in September were up 0.7% from August. The rise was caused in particular by the price of fuel for private transport, which was up 36.1% on a year earlier and 9.2% from the previous month. Energy prices also rose, with electricity, gas and other fuels up 4.9% year-on-year and 0.9% month-on-month. To shield consumers from the energy crisis triggered by US and Israeli attacks on Iran, Poland has twice introduced temporary measures to curb petrol station prices, including daily price caps and cuts in VAT and excise duty. The system was in place from March to June and again during the the last two weeks of August. The government has been under pressure from the opposition and opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki to reintroduce the subsidies. However, it argues that Nawrocki’s decision to block a proposed windfall tax on fuel companies makes the measures harder to fund Food and non-alcoholic beverage prices provided some offset, falling 0.5% from a year earlier, although they edged up 0.1% from August. Analysts, however, expect food prices to rise later in the year to reflect lower agricultural yields. According to GUS’s own estimates, also published on Wednesday, the grain harvest came in 5% lower compared to the last season. This will, in turn, “push the CPI index higher in the coming months”, wrote Erste Bank. The breach of the upper end of the central bank’s inflation target and the 4% threshold could influence the stance of the NBP’s Monetary Policy Council (RPP), prompting it to hike rates, added Erste Bank analysts. Inflacja CPI we wrześniu w górę do 4,0%r/r (ING: 4,2%; konsensus: 4,1%). Wyraźny wzrost cen paliw (36,1%r/r) odpowiada już za ok. połowę wzrostu cen w ujęciu rocznym. Zahamowanie spadków cen żywności m/m. Inflacja bazowa prawdopodobnie w dół do 3,0-3,1%r/r, co oznacza że wciąż… pic.twitter.com/AqdIXBthFl — ING Economics Poland (@ING_EconomicsPL) September 30, 2026 Economists at ING Bank Śląski, meanwhile, expect the first rate hike – after a series of nine cautious cuts between September 2023 and March 2026 – to come in early 2027. “The RPP may opt to wait, leaving interest rates unchanged in October, with discussions on potential monetary policy tightening beginning in November following the release of the NBP’s new projections,” they wrote on X. Poland’s benchmark interest rate currently stands at 3.75%, down from a peak of 6.75% reached during the country’s last tightening cycle in 2021-2022, when policymakers were grappling with persistent inflation fuelled by the post-pandemic recovery and the war in Ukraine. Inflation peaked at 18.4% during that period.

World.title: US ambassador inaugurates planned Polish-American Centre at Kraków’s Kościuszko Mound
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The US ambassador to Poland, Thomas Rose, has launched a planned new Polish-American Centre to be established in Kraków, Poland’s second-largest city. Rose symbolically laid a cornerstone for the new facility and announced a $150,000 (577,000 zloty) grant to restore and preserve the site. The centre, whose website describes it as a “home for all Polish-American initiatives in Poland”, will be established alongside the famous mound in Kraków created in honour of Tadeusz Kościuszko, a hero of both the Polish and American struggles for independence in the 18th century. Proud to announce a $150,000 AFCP grant to help restore and preserve the future site of the Kościuszko Mound’s Polish American Center — a living symbol of the friendship between our two nations. Under @POTUS, we remain committed to preserving the shared history that binds the… pic.twitter.com/5atStUIid2 — Ambassador Tom Rose (@USAmbPoland) September 29, 2026 “This is a tremendous opportunity for me, on behalf of President Donald Trump and the American people, to celebrate what I consider the most important relationship the United States has with Europe today,” said Rose at the ceremony on Monday. “America is fortunate to have many, many good friends around the world. But we have no better friend in Europe,” he added, quoted by broadcaster RMF. Together with Małgorzata Kidawa-Błońska, the speaker of Poland’s Senate, he laid a cornerstone for the new centre and announced the $150,000 grant, which comes from the Ambassadors’ Fund for Cultural Preservation, a programme run by the US State Department. “Tadeusz Kościuszko is a symbol of the historical bond between Poland and the USA,” declared Kidawa-Błońska. “There is no better place for the Polish-American Centre than Kraków and the mound commemorating a hero of both nations.” Tadeusz Kościuszko to symbol historycznej więzi między Polską i USA. Nie ma lepszego miejsca dla Centrum Polsko-Amerykańskiego niż Kraków i kopiec upamiętniający bohatera obu narodów. Niech powołane dziś Centrum dobrze służy naszym relacjom, które budujemy od 250 lat 🇵🇱🇺🇸 pic.twitter.com/8nOkCYDLfD — Małgorzata Kidawa-Błońska (@M_K_Blonska) September 29, 2026 Kościuszko’s Mound was established in Kraków in 1823, following the pattern of two prehistoric mounds that already existed in the city. It honours Kościuszko, a military officer who had fought against Russian rule over Poland and in the Continental Army during the American Revolutionary War. Construction of the new Polish-American Centre is being supported by the Kościuszko Mound Committee in Kraków in partnership with USA250PL, the platform for celebrations in Poland of this year’s 250th anniversary of the American Declaration of Independence. The Kościuszko Mound Committee has long been engaged in efforts to preserve the mound against partial collapses caused by heavy rain. Polish hydraulics manufacturer PONAR Wadowice is also listed as a partner of the new centre. The facility says it “will serve as a living symbol of friendship, understanding, and transatlantic cooperation”, providing “a welcoming space for dialogue, creativity, and exchange”. The centre will house event spaces, conference rooms, and offices. In June, the centre acted as a patron of a United States–Central and Eastern Europe Connection Weekend at Kraków’s Jagiellonian University. Next year it plans a commemoration of the Battle of Saratoga, where Kościuszko designed fortifications that contributed to the American victory. Poland has long looked to the United States for support and as an example during its struggle for independence over the last two centuries, including during the period of partitions in the 19th century, the reestablishment of the Polish state after the First World War, and during the later decades of communist rule. Since the fall of communism, the US has become Warsaw’s most important security partner – including establishing its first permanent military garrison, named Fort Kościuszko, in Poland in 2023. The US has opened its first military garrison in Poland, and its first anywhere on NATO's eastern flank. "This is a historic moment," says Poland's defence minister. "We have been striving for years for this word 'permanent' and it has now become fact" https://t.co/knJEcqv4MB — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 21, 2023 Last week, President Donald Trump, in a virtual address to the Polish-American Congress (an entity unrelated to the new centre in Kraków), praised his Polish counterpart Karol Nawrocki, a close Trump ally, and described himself as a “great friend of the people of Poland”. Shortly before that, Nawrocki had expressed confidence that a planned new US military base in Poland would soon be confirmed, and suggested that it would be named Fort Trump. World.title: EU court rejects Poland’s request to suspend implementation of Mercosur trade deal
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The Court of Justice of the European Union has rejected a request from Poland to suspend the implementation of the EU’s recently launched free trade agreement with the Mercosur bloc of South American countries. The CJEU found that the Polish government had failed to prove its claims that the trade deal would cause serious harm to European farmers, consumers or the environment. #ECJ: Order in Case C-460/26 R Poland v Council: should the implementation of the Council’s decision authorising the provisional application of the EU-Mercosur interim trade agreement be suspended pending the Court’s ruling?#CJEU #Mercosur pic.twitter.com/ocb4I4PsE8 — EU Court of Justice (@EUCourtPress) September 29, 2026 Poland has long been critical of the agreement, in particular over the potential negative impact that imports of agricultural products from Mercosur, which includes Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay and Uruguay, could have on Polish farmers, who have repeatedly protested against the deal. In January, Poland failed in a bid to block the agreement at the European Council, where 21 of the EU’s 27 member states voted in favour of the deal. Although the agreement has not yet received final ratification – still requiring approval from the European Parliament and national parliaments – it nevertheless went into provisional force on 1 May. Shortly afterwards, Poland submitted a complaint to the CJEU, calling for implementation of the agreement to be suspended. It argued, first of all, that the process through which the deal had been provisionally implemented violated the EU’s treaties. Second, it claimed that liberalising trade in agricultural products without imposing the same production standards in both the EU and Mercosur created a risk of harm to human and animal health, the environment, the income of farmers, and the functioning of the market in the EU. Poland has filed a complaint to the European Court of Justice against the EU's free-trade deal with the South American Mercosur bloc that recently went into provisional force. It wants the agreement to be suspended until the court issues a ruling https://t.co/wE7DIbDazU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 11, 2026 However, on Tuesday, the CJEU announced that it had dismissed the application to suspend the agreement, finding that “Poland has not provided any concrete evidence to establish the likelihood and imminence of serious and irreparable damage”. The court pointed out that agricultural products from Mercosur could already be imported to the EU before the free-trade deal, and that they were and continue to be subject to food safety and health regulations similar to those for products manufactured in the EU. It also noted that the new trade deal includes tools allowing the EU to bar products that do not meet standards, including emergency measures in the case of a serious threat to human, animal or plant life. Finally, the CJEU said that Poland’s “general and abstract claims” regarding potential harm to farmers and markets did not include “any evidence capable of establishing, with a sufficient degree of probability, that the implementation [of the agreement]…will cause disruption”. In response to the court’s decision, the Polish government’s spokesman, Adam Szłapka, immediately blamed the former national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) administration, which was in power in Poland from 2015 to 2023. Szłapka said that the details of the Mercosur deal had been agreed during that period and that PiS had “failed to secure Polish interests in any way”. He argued that it was the current government which secured the addition of last-minute safeguards intended to protect farmers. The spokesman also noted that Polish agricultural exports to the Mercosur bloc have actually increased under the new agreement while imports from there have fallen, showing that “Polish farmers are profiting from this”. Rząd i Premier Tusk najpierw mówili, że umowa UE-Mercosur będzie „bezpieczna dla polskich rolników”. Potem nie potrafili zbudować koalicji blokującej w Radzie Europejskiej – choć polityka europejska jest domeną rządu. Politycy KO, PSL i Lewicy nie potrafili nikogo przekonać.… https://t.co/EqOJr4sneP — Marcin Przydacz (@marcin_przydacz) September 29, 2026 However, Marcin Przydacz, the head of the foreign policy office of President Karol Nawrocki, who is aligned with the right-wing opposition, argued that the CJEU’s decision showed the impotence of the current pro-EU government. “The government and Prime Minister Tusk first said that the EU-Mercosur agreement would be ‘safe for Polish farmers’. Then they failed to build a blocking coalition in the European Council,” wrote Przydacz. “In the end, under pressure from public opinion in Poland, they filed a complaint with the ECJ. [It was] so weak that they lost the request for interim relief,” he added. “Ineffective policy and ineffective government.” Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. A Polish painting looted by Nazi Germany during World War Two, and which once hung in an SS officers’ club, has been returned by its owner, who donated it to the National Museum in Warsaw. “History is coming home,” said culture minister Marta Cienkowska, celebrating the return of Alfred Wierusz-Kowalski’s Winter – Napoleon’s Retreat from Moscow, which she described as “one of the most significant wartime losses in Polish painting”. Her ministry is responsible for seeking the return of tens of thousands of artworks and other cultural items that were looted during the war and remain missing. Kolejny sukces restytucyjny! Odzyskaliśmy jedną z cenniejszych i najbardziej znanych strat wojennych malarstwa polskiego. Obraz „Zima – Odwrót Napoleona spod Moskwy” Alfreda Wierusza-Kowalskiego trafił dziś do zbiorów Muzeum Narodowego w Warszawie. To efekt naszej współpracy z… pic.twitter.com/Y0wDIBgIGG — Ministerstwo Kultury i Dziedzictwa Narodowego (@kultura_gov_pl) September 28, 2026 Wierusz-Kowalski, who was active in the late 19th and early 20th centuries, was a renowned realist painter whose work often featured animals alongside people. His Winter – Napoleon’s Retreat from Moscow had, by the 1930s, become part of the collection of Andrzej Rotwand, a wealthy banker and industrialist. In June 1939, it was featured in an exhibition organised by the Society for the Encouragement of Fine Arts in Warsaw, which occupied the building that is now the famous Zachęta National Gallery of Art. However, the exhibition was brought to an abrupt end when Nazi Germany invaded Poland on 1 September 1939. The works on display, along with other items from the gallery, were seized by the occupiers, with many used to decorate the offices and apartments of German officials. Winter – Napoleon’s Retreat from Moscow was displayed in a club for high-ranking SS and police officers located in Warsaw’s Blanka Palace. The same building also housed Warsaw’s German-installed commissioner, Helmut Otto, and mayor, Ludwig Leist. No information has been released as to the fate of the painting in the immediate aftermath of the war. However, it eventually came into the possession of Ewa Tsonis, who has now handed it back. Speaking at a ceremony in the National Museum in Warsaw, Tsonis said that her late father, Michał Stefan Koryzna, had purchased the painting in the 1960s from Desa, a major gallery and auction house, in the city of Kraków. “I grew up with this painting. It was greatly appreciated and loved in our family,” she said. However, after recently conducting research into the painting’s history, she became aware of its provenance and notified the culture ministry. Experts from the National Museum in Warsaw confirmed the identity of the painting, which remains in good condition and in its original frame. Tsonis then donated the work to the museum. “Restitution is not possible without the cooperation of many people and institutions – both on the side of the state and on the part of the owners of the works,” said Cienkowska, who thanked Tsonis for her “incredibly responsible and civic-minded attitude”. “Such attitudes are still rare but, because we constantly talk about restitution – we search for lost works and strive to recover them – we are increasingly approached by people who own lost objects and feel a sense of responsibility for cultural heritage.” Cienkowska noted that the culture ministry has so far secured the return of over 920 works, with around 200 more restitution cases currently underway in 18 countries. Germany has agreed to return to Poland a collection of 73 medieval documents that were looted during WWII. The culture minister has hailed it as "the most important and valuable return of stolen cultural heritage in modern Polish history" https://t.co/GxHQ8A0jyr — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) December 1, 2025 However, that is still just a small fraction of the over 60,000 missing items listed in the ministry’s database of missing works, which includes seven further paintings by Wierusz-Kowalski. Two other works from Rotwand’s collection – Italian Woman by Anna Bilińska and Mother with Children by Kazimierz Alchimowicz – were also hung in the SS officers’ club during the war and today remain missing. Poland has in recent years stepped up efforts to secure the return of historical and cultural items looted during the German and Soviet occupations. In 2022, it appealed to UNESCO for help in securing the return of cultural items that remain missing after being looted by Nazi Germany. It also launched a campaign seeking the return of thousands of items that ended up in Russia after the war. World.title: Prague Passengers Can Now Request Czech or English Speaking Bolt Drivers
World.content:
Bolt has introduced two new ride categories in Prague that allow passengers to request drivers who speak either Czech or English.

The new options are available at the same price as a standard Bolt ride.



They are open to drivers of any nationality who can communicate in the relevant language at a level suitable for everyday conversation.

Czech-speaking passengers who are less comfortable communicating in English can request a Czech-speaking driver, while foreign residents, tourists and business travellers can choose a driver who speaks English.

Bolt already provides automatic translation for communication between passengers and drivers within its app. Booking information, addresses and messages can therefore be translated automatically. The new categories are designed to cover situations in which communication takes place outside the app, particularly during the journey itself.

The company said the new options are already available in Prague, where it has enough partner drivers who meet the language requirements.

Drivers can choose whether to participate in the new categories. They may offer rides in Czech, English, both languages or continue driving exclusively in the standard category.

Participation is voluntary.

Passengers will see the two new options directly in the Bolt app. The Czech-speaking category is identified by an icon featuring the Czech flag, while the English-speaking option uses an English flag icon.

World.title: Pegasus Airlines Completes Acquisition of Czech Airlines and Smartwings
World.content:
Pegasus Airlines has completed its acquisition of Czech Airlines and the Smartwings Group, marking a major change in the ownership of one of the Czech Republic’s most established aviation businesses.

The Turkish low-cost carrier announced the completion of the transaction on Thursday, October 1, following the approval of the relevant regulatory authorities and the fulfilment of the required closing conditions.



The deal brings together Pegasus Airlines and the Czech-based Smartwings Group, creating an aviation group with a combined fleet of more than 175 aircraft.

The two airlines also have firm orders for a further 140 aircraft.

For passengers in Prague and across the Czech Republic, Smartwings will continue to operate under its existing brand. Its day-to-day operations, customer relationships and service are expected to remain in place, while the company will gain access to new opportunities for expansion and development through its new ownership.

Pegasus expands further into Central Europe

Founded in 1990, Pegasus Airlines has operated as a low-cost carrier since 2005. The airline currently serves 161 destinations in 57 countries from its main hub at Istanbul Sabiha Gökçen Airport and other bases in Türkiye.

Its network covers Europe, the Middle East, North Africa and Asia, making the acquisition an opportunity to strengthen Pegasus’ presence in Central and Eastern Europe.

Smartwings, meanwhile, operates a network of around 80 destinations across 20 countries. The group has a particularly strong position in the Czech leisure travel market, with scheduled and charter services as well as private flights and special flights for international companies and organisations.

The Czech airline has been operating under the Smartwings name since 1998, while the Czech Airlines (ČSA) brand is one of the oldest names in European aviation.

The combined business is expected to benefit from the complementary networks of the two airlines. Pegasus brings a large international network and experience with the low-cost model, while Smartwings has an established customer base and strong relationships with tour operators in the Czech Republic and wider Central European market.

Pegasus said that Smartwings will continue operating under its established brand following the completion of the acquisition.

Pegasus carried a record 43.3 million passengers in 2025 and operates one of Europe’s younger aircraft fleets.

World.title: Ibiza Is Coming to Prague: A Night of DJs, Lasers and Tropical Vibes
World.content:
On April 17, 2027, OX Club in Prague will transform for one night into an Ibiza-inspired party featuring DJs, immersive visuals and tropical-themed spaces.

The Sound of Ibiza event will bring British DJ and producer Daxson, Dutch DJ and producer Laura Van Dam, Czech DJ Lucca and DJ TiGi to one stage.



The night will combine electronic music with a full immersive laser show, acrobatic performances above the dancefloor and Ibiza-inspired décor throughout the club.

There will also be a dedicated Sunset Experience for photos and social media, as well as a Chillout Zone with its own DJ programme and mentoring by Pavel Bidlo.

Daxson has performed at major festivals and clubs including Creamfields, EDC, UNTOLD and Ministry of Sound, while also creating several anthems for Transmission Festival. Laura Van Dam has appeared at Tomorrowland, Ultra, EDC, Sziget and Ushuaïa Ibiza and has built a following with her melodic techno and trance sound.

DJ Lucca, one of the country’s best-known electronic music artists, has performed alongside international names including Carl Cox and Paul van Dyk.

The event will also feature competitions for an iPhone and other prizes. An Ibiza Beach Outfit is suggested, although the dress code is optional.

With a capacity of 1,000 people, Sound of Ibiza aims to recreate the atmosphere of the famous Mediterranean party island in the centre of Prague for one night.

Tickets went on sale on October 1. Party packs are also available.

The event has no age restriction. Tickets are available through GoOut.

World.title: The Prague Post’s First Issue Goes Online 35 Years Later
World.content:
The Prague Post has launched a digital archive marking 35 years since the publication of its first issue.

October 1, 2026, marks the 35th anniversary of the newspaper’s debut.

Founded in 1991, The Prague Post was Czechoslovakia’s longest-running English-language weekly newspaper.



The newly launched archive begins with that very first issue, which is available to read in full, browse online and search by text.

A new issue will be added each week, corresponding to the same week 35 years earlier.

The project will allow readers to follow the political, social and cultural changes of the early 1990s through the newspaper’s coverage, much as readers did at the time.

The Prague Post Archive is also active on Facebook and Instagram, where updates about newly digitized issues and the project will be shared.

The archive is administered by Modrá sova z.s., a nonprofit English-language library and learning center in Loužnice, where The Prague Post’s physical archives are housed.

Issues published between 1991 and 1994 have already been scanned and processed.

Around two decades of additional issues remain to be digitized, making the project a long-term and costly undertaking. Modrá sova has independently funded the digitization work since the project began and is now inviting organizations and individuals interested in supporting the project to contribute through the archive’s website.

The archive will also continue to handle requests from people looking for specific articles and welcomes visitors by appointment.

For more information, contact Mimi Fronczak-Rogers at [email protected] or +420 721 518 385.

World.title: Halloween Trick-or-Treat for Charity to Return to Prague on October 22
World.content:
A Halloween charity event will bring children and families to several Prague neighbourhoods on October 22, combining trick-or-treating with fundraising for SOS Children’s Villages.

The Halloween Trick-or-Treat for Charity will take place from 4 p.m. to 8 p.m. across Vinohrady, Vršovice, Žižkov, Prague 15, Holešovice and Barrandov.



The concept is simple. Children dressed in Halloween costumes and accompanied by their parents will visit participating host locations, which can include cafés, restaurants, shops, confectioneries, schools, children’s centres and other businesses or organisations.

The participating locations will remain a secret until children register for the event and receive a special map showing where they can go trick-or-treating.

At each location, children will make a contribution of at least CZK 10 to a sealed collection box supporting SOS Children’s Villages. In return, they will receive a sweet treat before continuing to the next location.

Last year’s event attracted more than 1,100 registered participants and raised CZK 296,157 despite rainy weather.

The entire amount was donated to SOS Children’s Villages, which has supported children, families, young people and foster carers in the Czech Republic for more than 50 years.

How it started

Dinah Spritzer-Richter and several of her friends organized the first American Halloween in Prague for her two children in 2017. The event has supported charity from the very first year, with the proceeds going to help children in SOS Children’s Villages.

Dinah sees the charity side as just as important as creating a joyful and memorable experience for the kids.

How to take part

Families who want to participate can register in advance and then use the secret map to find the participating locations on October 22.

Children are encouraged to come in costume and bring enough coins to make contributions at the individual stops.

Businesses and organisations can also join the event as hosts. Each host is asked to prepare sweets, add some Halloween decorations and wear at least part of a costume or Halloween accessory.

Hosts must be available for at least two hours between 4 p.m. and 8 p.m.

The organisers will provide the collection boxes, while hosts provide the sweets for visiting children.

World.title: Prague Study Reveals How Much Waste Tourists Leave in the City Center
World.content:
Specialists from Prague City Hall and the Institute of Circular Economy (INCIEN) have analyzed the contents of public waste bins in central Prague, finding that about one ton of rubbish is discarded on Wenceslas Square every day.

The latest analysis was carried out to examine how the composition of waste changes with the seasons and fluctuations in tourist traffic.

A similar measurement was conducted during the winter, providing a basis for comparison.



Beverage packaging made up roughly one-third of the waste collected from bins on Wenceslas Square. Cans and plastic bottles were among the most common items.

Another third consisted of disposable food-service items, particularly cups. The remaining third was made up of general household waste.

Researchers also found waste originating from businesses in the surrounding area, including cafes and shops. Some household rubbish appeared to have been left by tourists staying in apartments rented through short-term accommodation platforms.

Food waste was another recurring part of the findings. Partially eaten food was frequently found in the bins, with trdelník pastries among the more common examples.

The summer analysis gives Prague authorities a clearer picture of the waste generated in one of the city’s busiest public spaces during the peak tourist season and allows them to compare the results with the winter survey.

World.title: Prague Hospitals Warn of Critical Blood Shortages
World.content:
Several hospitals in Prague are reporting critically low blood supplies, prompting the Czech Ministry of Health to urge people to donate blood in the coming days.

The shortage is affecting more than individual blood groups. Hospitals and transfusion centers in several parts of the Czech Republic are reporting a broader decline in available supplies, with some facilities nearing the minimum levels needed to maintain safe operations.



The situation differs from one region to another. Some transfusion centers still have adequate reserves, while others are short of particular blood groups or are approaching critical levels.

The shortage also extends to individual blood components. In Prague, the Institute for Clinical and Experimental Medicine (IKEM) is currently seeking more platelet donors regardless of blood type.

People planning to donate are advised to check the latest information on the website or social media channels of their chosen transfusion center before visiting.

Why hospitals need more donors

Hospitals depend on regular blood donations not only during emergencies but also for planned medical treatment.

Blood is routinely needed for surgery, childbirth and the treatment of patients who require repeated transfusions. This includes some cancer patients whose treatment can interfere with the body’s production of blood cells.

Blood donations are also essential in cases of severe complications during childbirth. Heavy blood loss can become life-threatening within a short period, and an adequate supply of donated blood can be critical to saving the lives of mothers and newborns.

The demand for blood can increase during the summer and holiday period, when hospitals continue to perform scheduled procedures while also dealing with more injuries and traffic accidents. At the same time, the number of people coming to donate tends to fall as residents leave the country or travel elsewhere.

Number of donors continues to decline

Official figures indicate that the Czech donor base has been shrinking. Around 348,000 people donated blood last year, down from 362,000 the previous year.

Transfusion centers are also losing older regular donors as they reach the age limit, while the number of younger people replacing them has not been sufficient.

In the Czech Republic, adults can generally donate blood until the age of 65, provided they weigh more than 50 kilograms. Additional eligibility restrictions may apply, including for people who have recently travelled to countries where certain infectious diseases are present.

Donating blood in the Czech Republic is voluntary and free of charge. Donors are entitled to time off work on the day of their donation, while some health insurance companies provide additional benefits or rewards for regular donors.

World.title: Bangkok Gears Up for the 2026 IMF-World Bank Annual Meetings
World.content:
All eyes are on Thailand as the country prepares to host the 2026 International Monetary Fund (IMF) and World Bank Group (WBG) Annual Meetings, also known as the 2026 Annual Meetings or AM2026 Thailand.

Running from 12-18 October 2026, at the Queen Sirikit National Convention Center (QSNCC) in Bangkok, the event will mark Thailand’s second time hosting the meetings, following its first in 1991. This will make Thailand one of only three nations to have hosted the IMF–WBG Annual Meetings twice.



The IMF–WBG Annual Meetings, held for two consecutive years in Washington D.C. and every third year in one of the 191 member countries, serve as a gathering of top economic figures from around the world. By covering a broad range of issues, the meetings aim to strengthen global financial stability, combat poverty, and ensure inclusive economic growth and job creation.

Thailand’s selection to host again in 2026 highlights how the country has advanced over the past three decades in terms of its institutional progress, economic resilience, and sustained engagement with international partners. As host, Thailand brings decades’ worth of experience in economic transformation and regional leadership to the table.

The “Olympics of Finance”

Often dubbed the “Olympics of Finance,” the meetings are set to attract more than 15,000 participants, including finance ministers, central bankers, economists, business leaders, civil society representatives, and journalists from the IMF and World Bank’s 191 member countries, including the Czech Republic.

The Annual Meetings will be held under the theme of “Thailand’s New Horizons: Empowering People, Building Resilience”. Therefore, the meetings will focus on enhancing people’s potential and creating opportunities, with the goal of fostering a financial and economic system that is safe, sustainable, and inclusive.

Under the theme, the government plans to showcase four policy priorities it believes are increasingly relevant in an era marked by geopolitical fragmentation, economic volatility, and demographic change. These are indeed the issues that warrant serious conversation and sincere collaboration among the global community and all stakeholders to address them in the most efficient way:

Digital Transformation : The first centers on digital transformation and artificial intelligence, using the examples from Thailand’s Digital Public Infrastructure, including PromptPay and cross-border QR payment systems.

The first centers on digital transformation and artificial intelligence, using the examples from Thailand’s Digital Public Infrastructure, including PromptPay and cross-border QR payment systems. Connected Economy : A second pillar focuses on what is called “Building Resilience in a Fragmented World”. In order to achieve this, the concept of a “Connected Economy” capable of bridging divides between competing blocs while strengthening supply chains and investment links will be explored.

A second pillar focuses on what is called “Building Resilience in a Fragmented World”. In order to achieve this, the concept of a “Connected Economy” capable of bridging divides between competing blocs while strengthening supply chains and investment links will be explored. Climate Finance : The third pillar addresses climate finance, with emphasis on reforms to help countries adapt to climate change.

The third pillar addresses climate finance, with emphasis on reforms to help countries adapt to climate change. Longevity Economy: The final priority seeks to turn the challenges of ageing populations into new sources of economic growth.

Alongside these focus areas, the Bank of Thailand plans to unveil the “Bangkok Blueprint,” an international framework developed jointly with the IMF and the World Bank aimed at combating digital financial fraud and strengthening trust in the digital economy.

Readiness in All Aspects

According to the Fiscal Policy Office, Thailand’s overall readiness has been assessed at “Grade A” following months of coordination between the Ministry of Finance, the Bank of Thailand, and the IMF–World Bank Annual Meetings Secretariat.

Preparations extend beyond the conference venue. Authorities have developed contingency plans for traffic management, emergency responses, and arrangements for high-level foreign officials. A working group has also been established to address cybersecurity matters.

Beyond Tourism: A Regional Economic Capital

Beyond its long-established reputation as a world-renowned tourist destination, the 2026 Annual Meetings offer Thailand an excellent opportunity to present another dimension of the Kingdom to the international community.

AM2026 reinforces Thailand’s standing as a trusted international partner while highlighting its growing role as a regional economic capital and a hub for finance, investment, policy innovation, and multilateral dialogue in Southeast Asia. Having said that, countries and companies vying for economic and business opportunities cannot overlook Thailand and its potential to become an important impetus for their long-term prosperity and growth.

(Source material and reporting courtesy of Thailand NOW)

World.title: Hungary’s central bank probe summons former and current governors
World.content:
A parliamentary committee investigating the use of public funds by Hungary’s central bank has summoned former governor György Matolcsy and current governor Mihály Varga for questioning.

Former and current NBH governors to appear before committee

A parliamentary committee investigating alleged abuses surrounding the operation of the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) has decided to summon former governor György Matolcsy and current governor Mihály Varga.

The ad hoc committee voted unanimously to summon Matolcsy, who headed the central bank between 2013 and 2025. The decision to summon Varga, who succeeded Matolcsy as governor in 2025, was approved with five votes in favour, no votes against and one abstention.

The committee’s chairman, Attila Csőszi of the governing Tisza Party, said the decisions would formally require both men to appear and give oral testimony. The next committee meeting is expected to take place in three to four weeks. Csőszi told state news agency MTI that the committee plans to question Matolcsy and Varga on several occasions.

György Matolcsy. Photo: National Bank of Hungary

Committee requests data from NBH foundation

The committee also voted to request data from the Pallas Athene Domus Meriti Foundation, one of the foundations established by the central bank. The request was approved with five votes in favour, one abstention and no votes against.

The parliamentary committee was established to examine the use of public funds and alleged abuses linked to the operation of the NBH. Its work is expected to focus on the central bank and entities connected to it.

If you missed it: Central bank chief on the scenario for introducing the Hungarian euro

Several former officials already questioned

The committee has already begun questioning figures connected to the NBH case. On Thursday, it spent more than three hours questioning Erik Bánki and Lajos Kósa. The committee has previously said that it intends to identify and summon the key figures involved in the case. Further hearings are expected to include Matolcsy’s son, Ádám Matolcsy, among others.

Matolcsy served as NBH governor from 2013 until 2025. Varga was Hungary’s economy minister from 2013 to 2018 and finance minister from 2018 to 2024 before taking over as central bank governor in 2025.
